I'm a sneaker-and-uniform designer from Eugene, which means I review jerseys and route trees with exactly the same ferocity. A slant with sloppy footwork? That's a wrinkled hem, darling. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and before I analyze anybody, I rate their uniform. It's the law. My catchphrase is "Uniform of the week? Ten out of ten." When we win, the review reads "10 out of 10, uniform AND execution." When we lose, I review it like a runway show where somebody tripped in the wrong shoes: honest, kind and very detailed. Each week you get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a little sparkle. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Oregon has played football since 1894 [S10]. Autzen Stadium opened in 1967 and is listed at 54,000 seats, though anyone who's been inside knows it sounds much bigger [S10][S2]. In 2014 quarterback Marcus Mariota became Oregon's first Heisman Trophy winner, after throwing for 4,454 yards and 42 touchdowns [S10][S11]. He finished with the second-most points of any Heisman winner, behind only O.J. Simpson [S11]. The Ducks moved to the Big Ten in 2024 and won the league right away: 13-1 overall and 9-0 in conference play [S12]. Last year they went 13-2 and 8-1 in the league [S13]. Two straight seasons of runway-ready football.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Dan Lanning was hired on Dec. 11, 2021 [S2]. His 2024 team went 9-0 in the Big Ten and won the title [S12], and Ducks Wire notes he has never lost a Big Ten road game [S4]. In 2026 the offense throws the ball well: 283.3 passing yards a game and 16 passing touchdowns, with an even split between runs and passes (about 48% runs) [S2]. Oregon averages 37.0 points and 420.3 yards a game [S2]. The defense allows 20.7 points and only 3.25 yards a carry, and it has intercepted nine passes [S2][S7]. One thing to tailor: Oregon has lost 11 turnovers and forced 11 [S2]. That's a perfectly even hem, but I want it tucked.

4. Players to Know

• QB Dante Moore: 69 of 99 for 926 yards, 9 TD and no interceptions in four games, with a 178.27 rating [S7]. He suffered a concussion at USC on Sept. 26. His MRI and CT scans were clean, but he was listed OUT on every Big Ten availability report for UCLA and Nebraska [S5]. Oregon has not announced a return date [S5].
• QB Dylan Raiola: 515 yards, 6 TD, 2 INT this season [S7]. Against Nebraska, his former team, he came in with Oregon down 14-6 and threw the winning 4-yard touchdown to TE Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds left [S6]. QB Brock Thomas started that game and went 9 of 20 for 54 yards [S6]. Lanning said the two will keep competing in practice [S4].
• RB Jordon Davison: 301 yards and 6 TD on 62 carries [S8].
• WR Evan Stewart: 27 catches, 352 yards, 4 TD [S8]. He was listed out on the Oct. 17 report [S6].
• Defense: LB Matayo Uiagalelei has 5 sacks [S8], DB Jett Washington has 2 interceptions [S8], and DB Koi Perich has 34 tackles and 2 interceptions [S9].

5. The Conference Picture

Oregon is 4-2 overall and 2-1 in the Big Ten, 3-1 at home and 1-1 on the road [S2]. The Ducks are No. 25 in this week's Coaches Poll [S2]. The losses came at Oklahoma State, 39-31, and at home to UCLA, 17-15 [S2]. With a road trip this week and Northwestern next [S6], this is a stretch where the outfit has to come together.

6. This Week: Oregon (4-2) at Illinois (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3 p.m. ET (noon PT) · Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign · Big Ten Network [S3][S4]. It's only Oregon's third visit to Illinois, and the first since 1993 [S4].
Last week: Oregon beat Nebraska 17-14 with two fourth-quarter scoring drives [S4][S6]. Illinois had a bye after winning 38-37 in overtime at Michigan State on Oct. 10 [S4][S2].
Our offense vs. their defense: Illinois allows 27.8 points and 375.2 yards a game, and 248.3 passing yards [S2]. Whoever plays quarterback for us should have chances through the air.
Their offense vs. our defense: Illinois averages 31.8 points and runs for 5.06 yards a carry [S2]. WR Collin Dixon has 47 catches, 608 yards and 9 touchdowns, which ranks third in FBS in receiving touchdowns [S8][S9]. Starting QB Katin Houser broke his left hand at Michigan State, and freshman Michael Clayton II will likely make his first career start [S4].
Series: Oregon leads 3-1 and won the last meeting 38-9 at Autzen in 2024 [S8][S3].
Availability: On Oregon's last official report (Oct. 17), Aaron Flowers, Dante Moore, Evan Stewart and Jeremiah McClellan were out and Dave Iuli was a game-time decision [S6]. The first report for this game comes out during game week [S5]. Illinois: Houser is out with the broken hand [S4]. I found no other official Illinois report as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Who plays quarterback for us: Moore, Raiola or Thomas. (2) Can our secondary stay with Dixon? (3) How a freshman QB handles his first start against a defense allowing 3.25 yards a carry [S2][S4].
And to Margery Vandermolen, Illinois's insider: your orange is gorgeous this time of year. I'm giving the Illini uniforms a sincere nine. The tenth point is reserved for us.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in Eugene? The Big Dirty on Olive Street does a game-day burger worthy of a runway.

report.title: "Exit 9 Never Lies": Vinny Scolari Takes the Scarlet Knights to Evanston
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Yo, Rutgers! How you doin'? Welcome to The Cover Window! Vinny Scolari here, your Rutgers insider, born and raised off Exit 9 of the New Jersey Turnpike. I give directions by Turnpike exit for everything, and I mean everything. Where's the stadium? Exit 9. How am I feeling after a loss? Somewhere around Exit 7A. I grade every Big Ten trench battle like a boardwalk arm-wrestle: who leaned in, who flinched, who walked away with the stuffed animal. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I order a sub big enough for the whole studio. Six feet. Everybody eats. When we lose, I say "Fuhgeddaboudit"... and then I can't. I really can't. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Jersey-style. "Exit 9 never lies." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Here's something every college football fan should know. The very first college football game was played right in New Brunswick on Nov. 6, 1869, and Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4 [S8]. That's right: the birthplace of the whole sport is off Exit 9. Home now is SHI Stadium in Piscataway, listed at 52,454 [S2]. The man running the show is Greg Schiano, who came back to coach Rutgers again in December 2019 [S9]. The Scarlet Knights play in the Big Ten [S2], and every week is a heavyweight fight.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Schiano's second stint began with his return on Nov. 30, 2019 [S2][S9]. The 2026 numbers say this offense can sling it: 265.8 passing yards a game (35th in FBS) and 16 passing touchdowns [S3][S2]. Rutgers averages 31.2 points and 403.3 yards a game [S3]. And here's a stat I'll yell from the top of the Driscoll Bridge: Rutgers is the least penalized team in FBS, at 28.7 penalty yards a game [S3]. Discipline, baby. The defense, though, needs some fixing. It allows 31.8 points a game (119th) and 185.2 rushing yards (118th) [S3]. Turnovers are a problem too, at minus-5 (122nd) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• WR K.J. Duff: 42 catches, 741 yards and 9 TD [S3]. At Maryland he had 9 catches for 113 yards and two touchdowns [S3], including a catch AP called incredible [S4]. The man's a Turnpike express lane.
• QB Dylan Lonergan: 1,066 yards, 10 TD, 6 INT [S3]. He went 23 of 35 for 291 yards and three touchdowns at Maryland [S3].
• RB Antwan Raymond: 498 yards and 5 TD on 105 carries [S3].
• RB Clay Thevenin: 109 rushing yards and a touchdown at Maryland, plus a receiving TD [S3].
I couldn't verify current defensive leaders from a free source, so I'm not guessing. Jersey guys are loud, not sloppy.

5. The Conference Picture

Rutgers is 2-4 overall and 1-2 in the Big Ten, 1-3 at home and 1-1 on the road [S2]. We're not ranked [S2]. The losses were to UMass, at Boston College, to USC (42-35) and to Indiana [S2]. We hung with USC until the end, losing by seven, and the Maryland comeback showed what this team's made of [S2][S4]. On the ground we're at 3.78 yards a carry, and the protection has given up 14 sacks [S2]. If the big guys win their arm-wrestles, this offense can go the whole length of the Turnpike. Michigan comes to Piscataway next week [S3], so this is a big two-week stretch.

6. This Week: Rutgers (2-4) at No. 24 Northwestern (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Ryan Field, Evanston · Peacock [S3][S1]. The new Ryan Field opened this season [S6].
Last week: Rutgers trailed Maryland 23-13 at halftime and came back to win 37-30 [S4]. Northwestern beat Michigan State 24-21 on a 34-yard field goal with two seconds left [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Northwestern allows just 17.0 points a game (26th), but its pass defense ranks 100th at 230.5 yards a game [S3]. Lonergan to Duff is our best punch.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the arm-wrestle I'm worried about. Northwestern runs on about 62% of its plays for 191.5 yards a game [S2][S3]. Our run defense allows 185.2 a game [S3]. QB Aidan Chiles hasn't thrown an interception all year [S3], and Northwestern scores on 96.4% of red-zone trips (fourth) [S3].
Series: a full series record was not in a free source I could verify.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 9 sacks and has allowed 14, with 6 takeaways against 11 giveaways, and it has 9 rushing and 16 passing touchdowns [S2].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our front stop Northwestern's run game? (2) Turnovers. They're plus-7 and we're minus-5 [S3]. (3) Can Duff win his matchups against a pass defense ranked 100th?
And to Ezra Lindqvist, Northwestern's insider: I hear you footnote your own jokes. Here's one for you. Footnote: we came to win, pal. Exit 9 never lies.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in New Brunswick? Stuff Yer Face on Easton Avenue. Order the stromboli. Thank me later.

report.title: "In a World...": Sterling Ashworth-Vance Premieres the Trojans in Madison
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

In a world... where one team plays every Saturday like it's opening night... Good evening, I'm Sterling Ashworth-Vance, film buff, football historian and your guide to the Trojans. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, polished and presented in glorious widescreen. I treat every game like a premiere, because at USC, every game is one. The Coliseum is the grandest movie set in sports, and every fall our Trojans play the lead. Traveler gallops, the band strikes up, and Los Angeles remembers why it loves this team. When we win, the music swells and I say, "Roll credits." When we lose, I call it a second-act setback, because the best films always have one. Fight On! (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Trojans were formed in 1888 [S6]. The program has more than 860 wins and claims 11 national championships, seven of them from the AP and/or Coaches polls [S6]. USC has had 13 undefeated seasons, eight of them perfect [S6]. We now play in the Big Ten, at the 77,500-seat Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park, right next to campus [S6]. CFBD dates the Coliseum to 1923 [S2]. The last five seasons: 4-8, 11-3, 8-5, 7-6 in our first Big Ten year, and 9-4 [S2]. A classic comeback arc.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Lincoln Riley is the director's chair; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2021 [S2]. His offense is a blockbuster: 310.1 passing yards a game (7th in FBS), 462.4 total yards (17th) and 36.4 points (27th) [S5]. We convert 51.2% of third downs, 14th [S5], and hold the ball 32:50 a game (21st) [S5]. The defense stops the run, 111 yards allowed (32nd) [S5], with 15 sacks [S2]. The plot hole: the pass defense allows 239 yards a game, 109th [S5], and opponents score on 84.6% of red zone trips (76th) [S5]. Every great film needs some tension.

4. Players to Know

• QB Jayden Maiava: 152 of 224 for 2,045 yards, 18 TD, 3 INT [S4][S5]. CollegeFootballDigest says he's No. 2 in FBS in passing yards [S9]. At Penn State he went 21 of 33 for 301 yards and three scores [S5]. Leading-man material.
• RB King Miller: 595 yards on 114 carries, 4 TD; 102 yards and a touchdown at Penn State [S4][S5].
• WR Kayden Dixon-Wyatt: 27 catches, 400 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. Trent Mosley: nine catches for 111 yards and a touchdown at Penn State [S5].
• S Christian Pierce: team-leading tackler [S4][S9]. S Kennedy Urlacher: 3 sacks [S4]. CB Prophet Brown: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

USC is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big Ten, ranked No. 16 by the AP and No. 15 in the coaches poll [S2][S5]. The wins: San José State 42-26, Fresno State 39-0, Louisiana 49-30, at Rutgers 42-35, Washington 25-21 and at Penn State 31-23 [S2]. The one loss: Oregon, 41-27 [S2]. We had last week off [S2]. After Madison comes a true blockbuster: No. 3 Ohio State at the Coliseum on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math tonight. I'll only say the sequel is lining up beautifully.
The road so far: two road games, two wins [S2]. Our heroes travel well.
The one dark scene: Oregon came to the Coliseum and won 41-27 [S2]. Every great franchise has an episode like that. What matters is what came next: a 25-21 win over Washington and that statement night at Penn State [S2]. That's a hero who gets knocked down in act two and gets back up for the finale.

6. This Week: No. 16 USC (6-1) at Wisconsin (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Camp Randall Stadium, Madison · NBC [S1][S5][S8]. Forecast at kickoff: 65 degrees, mostly cloudy, south wind 10 mph [S9].
The backstory: USC leads the series 7-1 [S9]. The meetings include the Rose Bowl after the 1962 season, a 42-37 USC win, and a Holiday Bowl after 2015 that Wisconsin won 23-21 [S9]. The last meeting, in 2024, went to USC 38-21 [S9]. A rich film library.
Last time out: we beat Penn State 31-23 on Oct. 10 [S5]. Wisconsin lost 17-7 at UCLA on Oct. 17 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the main event. Wisconsin's defense is excellent: 286.7 yards allowed (17th), 171.2 passing yards allowed (20th) and 16.7 points (24th) [S5]. Maiava against that secondary is the scene everyone will remember.
Their offense vs. our defense: Wisconsin averages 351.8 yards (103rd) [S5], but quarterback Colton Joseph is also its leading rusher, 333 yards and 4 TD [S5]. And Wisconsin scores on 94.1% of red zone trips, 14th [S5].
Availability: no availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Maiava against a top-20 pass defense. (2) Containing Joseph's legs. (3) Our red zone defense.
To Lars "Brat" Ellefson, Wisconsin's insider: a cheese wedge at every game? Magnificent costume design. I'd cast you in a heartbeat.

Why I Love This Team

I love an offense that plays like a summer blockbuster [S5]. I love a quarterback with 18 touchdowns and three interceptions [S4]. I love that the Trojans have won on the road twice already [S2]. And I love the history: 11 national championships and a Rose Bowl win over this very opponent [S6][S9]. Roll credits.

report.title: "Pass the Curds": Brat Ellefson Welcomes the Trojans to Camp Randall
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Pass the curds. (Polka accordion: oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, folks, I'm Lars Ellefson, but everybody calls me Brat. I was a fullback for the Badgers back in my day, and I still carry a cheese wedge to every game. Every single one. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, wholesome as a glass of cold milk. You'll notice I play a little polka before I share a stat. My doctor says it's good for my heart. When we win, I jump around, literally, and pass out cheese curds. When we lose, I eat a brat in thoughtful silence. Then I eat another one. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

(Oom-pah.) The Badgers have played in the Big Ten since it formed in 1896 [S7]. Wisconsin is one of 26 programs to win 700 or more games [S7]. Home is Camp Randall Stadium, the fourth-oldest stadium in college football [S7], opened in 1917 and listed at 80,321 seats [S3]. The last five seasons were 9-4, 7-6, 7-6, 5-7 and 4-8 [S3]. So this 4-2 start? That's a fresh batch of squeaky curds, folks. Squeaky fresh.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Luke Fickell is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 27, 2022 [S3]. (Oom-pah.) This team is built on defense, the way a good barn is built on a stone foundation. We allow 286.7 yards a game (17th in FBS), 171.2 passing yards (20th), 115.5 rushing yards (37th) and 16.7 points (24th) [S5]. Now, the offense. I love it like family, and family is honest: 351.8 yards a game (103rd) and 199.7 passing yards (100th) [S5]. But in the red zone, we score on 94.1% of trips, 14th in the country [S5]. Get us close, and we'll punch it in. Spoken like a fullback.

4. Players to Know

• QB Colton Joseph: 87 of 159 for 1,198 yards, 10 TD, 5 INT, and he's also our leading rusher, 333 yards and 4 TD on 69 carries [S4][S5]. At UCLA he ran 18 times for 71 yards and a touchdown [S5]. That's my kind of quarterback. Fullback heart.
• WR Tyrell Henry: 27 catches, 343 yards, 1 TD [S4][S5].
• RB Abu Sama III: six carries for 34 yards at UCLA [S5]. WR Jaylon Domingeaux: two catches for 26 yards [S5].
• LB Cooper Catalano: team-high 50 tackles [S4][S9]. LB Sebastian Cheeks: 2.5 sacks [S4]. S Marvin Burks Jr.: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

(Oom-pah.) Wisconsin is 4-2 and 2-1 in the Big Ten, 3-0 at home [S3]. We opened with a 41-13 loss to Notre Dame at a neutral site, then beat Western Illinois 36-9, Eastern Michigan 54-10, Penn State 24-20 on the road and Michigan State 31-3 [S3]. Last week, UCLA beat us 17-7 [S3]. After USC, we head to No. 15 Iowa on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math. I'm just saying a win over a ranked team at Camp Randall would make the whole state jump.
The Penn State win is the one I'll keep telling my grandkids about: on the road, 24-20 [S3]. That's a cheese wedge held high.
Season so far, by the polka: the Notre Dame game was a slow waltz we didn't want to dance [S3]. Then came three home wins and that road win at Penn State, a real toe-tapper [S3]. Michigan State managed just 3 points against our defense [S3]. UCLA held us to 7, and Joseph completed 6 of 16 passes [S5]. That's a sour note, folks. But we had a week off before UCLA, and the band's been practicing ever since [S3]. (Oom-pah.) I've seen this defense all year. It's the real deal, and it'll keep us in this one.
A fullback's note on Joseph: 69 carries through six games [S4]. That young man runs like he's carrying the cheese wedge himself.

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 Central) · Camp Randall Stadium, Madison · NBC [S1][S5][S8]. Forecast at kickoff: 65 degrees, mostly cloudy, south wind 10 mph [S9]. Perfect brat weather.

Their offense vs. our defense: here's the big one. USC throws for 310.1 yards a game (7th) [S5], and Jayden Maiava has 18 touchdown passes [S5]. Our pass defense is 20th [S5]. That's a heavyweight bout at the county fair.
Our offense vs. their defense: USC's pass defense ranks 109th [S5], so Joseph should have chances. And USC allows opponents to score on 84.6% of red zone trips [S5]. Get us inside the 20, folks.

What decides it: (1) Our pass defense against Maiava. (2) Joseph's legs and our red zone finishing. (3) Third downs; USC converts 51.2% (14th) [S5].
To Sterling Ashworth-Vance, USC's insider: I'd be honored to be in your movie, as long as I get to play the fullback.

report.title: "Bear Down, Friends": Inez Paloverde Welcomes the Cyclones Home for Homecoming
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hi, hi, hi, Wildcat family, welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Inez Paloverde, your Arizona insider, and I am a desert-sunrise optimist. I talk fast, I love hard, and I will defend this team to the last saguaro. I love the desert and I want you to love it too, so be warned: there will be cactus metaphors. A good defense is a lot like a cactus. It's beautiful from a distance, and you do not want to touch it. And when people complain about the Tucson heat, I just smile and say, "It's a dry hype." Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus all the sunshine I can carry. And I always end the same way: "Bear Down, friends." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Let's start with those two words. "Bear Down" goes back to October 1926 and John "Button" Salmon, the student-body president and the Wildcats' quarterback. He was badly hurt in a car accident, and before he died he asked coach J.F. "Pop" McKale to tell the team to "bear down" [S15]. It's been our rallying cry ever since [S15]. Home is Arizona Stadium in Tucson, listed at 50,782 seats [S2]. The program had a big 2025, going 9-4 and reaching the Holiday Bowl, where it lost to SMU 24-19 [S16]. This season is Arizona's best start since 2014 [S3]. Pretty as a sunrise over the Catalinas.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Brent Brennan was hired on Jan. 16, 2024 [S2][S16]. He went 4-8 his first season, then turned it around with nine wins in 2025 [S16]. The 2026 numbers say this offense starts with Noah Fifita's arm. Arizona throws for 303.8 yards a game with 16 passing touchdowns, and splits runs and passes evenly [S2]. It averages 35.7 points and 456.5 yards a game [S2]. The defense is the cactus: it allows 19.0 points a game and just 3.34 yards a carry, and it has 15 sacks [S2]. Two prickly spots: 16 sacks allowed, and eight turnovers lost against five forced [S2]. Also, West Virginia put up 522 yards against us, which dropped Arizona to ninth in the Big 12 in total defense [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Noah Fifita: 140 of 191 for 1,756 yards, 16 TD and 4 INT [S5]. At West Virginia he went 16 of 23 for 341 yards and 3 TD [S7].
• WR Isaiah Mizell: 19 catches, 359 yards, 4 TD [S5], including 6 catches for 183 yards and 2 TD at West Virginia [S7]. WR Tre Spivey: 4 touchdown catches [S6].
• RB Kedrick Reescano: 262 yards and 4 TD on 72 carries [S5].
• LB Chase Kennedy: 4 sacks [S5]. LB Taye Brown: the leading tackler. Sources differ on the total, 39 in one preview [S7] and 27 in another snapshot [S6] (conflicting).

5. The Conference Picture

Arizona is 5-1 overall and 2-1 in the Big 12, 3-0 at home and 2-1 on the road [S2]. The Wildcats are No. 25 in this week's AP poll [S2]. The only loss came at BYU, 28-17, and since then they've won four straight: Northern Illinois, Washington State, Cincinnati and West Virginia [S2][S3]. Our 456.5 yards a game ranks seventh in the Big 12 in total offense [S3], and our run defense started last week third in the league before sliding to seventh [S3]. Translation: room to grow, plenty of sunshine to grow it in. Win on homecoming and Arizona stays right in the middle of the Big 12 race.

6. This Week: Iowa State (3-3) at No. 25 Arizona (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4:30 p.m. MST (7:30 p.m. ET) · Arizona Stadium (Casino Del Sol Stadium) · ESPN2 · Homecoming [S3][S4][S1]. It's the third straight year our homecoming has kicked off before 5 p.m. [S3]
Last time out: both teams are coming off bye weeks [S3]. Arizona won 52-31 at West Virginia [S2]. Iowa State lost 24-10 at No. 8 BYU and managed just 200 total yards [S8][S9].
Our offense vs. their defense: Iowa State allows 21.7 points a game and 198.5 passing yards a game [S2]. Fifita against that secondary is where I'd look first.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Cyclones love to run, at 181.5 yards a game [S3]. RB Aiden Flora has 680 yards and 6 TDs [S5]. Our run defense allows 3.34 a carry [S2]. Pretty from a distance, remember?
Series: Arizona leads 4-2-1 [S5], but Iowa State won last season's meeting 39-14 in Ames [S3]. It's Iowa State's first trip to Tucson since 1966 [S3].
Availability: Iowa State WR Dominic Overby is reported out for the season with a knee injury [S10]. I found no official availability report for Arizona as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our front slow Flora? (2) Can Fifita keep finding Mizell and Spivey? (3) Turnovers. We've lost eight; Iowa State has forced eight [S2].
And to Twyla Hemmingsen, Iowa State's insider: honey, your forecast can say whatever it wants. Down here it's sunny and 100% Bear Down.

report.title: "Hydrate and Dominate": Skylar Vanterpool Welcomes the Wildcats to Tempe
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hi, Sun Devil Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Skylar Vanterpool. Yes, I'm the girl by the pool in the giant maroon sunhat, and yes, I also have a master's degree in sports science, so I will talk your ear off about recovery windows and sweat rates. I travel with this team and live with this team. Fair warning: about every 90 seconds I'm going to remind you to drink some water. It's not a bit. Okay, it's a little bit a bit. My motto is simple: "Hydrate and dominate." When we win, I cannonball into a kiddie pool on set. When we lose, it's "Hydrate, reflect, recover," and then a well-earned nap. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, with plenty of sunshine and zero sunburn. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Sun Devil football has a Rose Bowl ring to it. On Jan. 1, 1987, quarterback Jeff Van Raaphorst led a comeback as Arizona State beat Michigan 22-15 in Pasadena [S15]. More recently, the Sun Devils won the 2024 Big 12 championship, beating Iowa State 45-19 in the title game [S14]. Home is Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, listed at a capacity of 65,870 [S2][S18]. This team also gets around: in Week 3 it beat Kansas 24-17 at Wembley Stadium in London, England, in the Union Jack Classic [S18]. Sip of water. Okay, moving on.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Kenny Dillingham became Arizona State's 26th head coach on Nov. 27, 2022, and took the Sun Devils to the Big 12 title in his second season [S14]. The 2026 numbers say this offense lives through the air. ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game and has 15 passing touchdowns, against 7 on the ground [S2]. It averages 31.3 points and 420.3 yards a game, and runs on about 48% of its plays at 4.42 yards a carry [S2]. The defense is where we need some shade and electrolytes: ASU allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry [S2]. Two more things to fix are 15 sacks allowed and 10 turnovers lost against 6 forced [S2]. After last week, Dillingham said, "We almost gotta double down on that, because we're doing a lot well." [S9]

4. Players to Know

• QB Cutter Boley (junior, Kentucky transfer): the season starter. One preview lists him at 1,229 yards, 12 TD and 3 INT, though that snapshot may not include the most recent game [S16]. At Texas Tech he went 5 of 10 for 124 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions before he was benched at halftime [S8][S10].
• QB Mikey Keene (sixth-year): 25 of 34 for 256 yards and two touchdowns in the second half at Texas Tech [S8]. He's on the Pat Tillman Leadership Council and has played at UCF, Fresno State and Michigan [S9].
• WR Reed Harris (senior): 34 catches, 590 yards and 7 TD in the same preview snapshot [S16].
• WR Raiden Vines-Bright: caught a 74-yard touchdown at Texas Tech [S8][S10]. WR Derek Eusebio: led the team with seven catches for 89 yards last week after an injury-slowed start [S10].
• RB Cardae Mack (freshman): seven carries for 27 yards and a touchdown catch at Texas Tech [S10].
I could not find current, dated season defensive leaders, so I'm leaving them out rather than guessing.

5. The Conference Picture

Arizona State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 2-1 at home and 0-2 on the road, plus the Wembley win at a neutral site [S2][S18]. The Sun Devils are not ranked this week [S2]. The league losses were 55-19 at home to Baylor and 53-25 at Texas Tech [S18]. The top two Big 12 teams meet in the championship game [S4], and both teams in this one are 1-2, so this is a big afternoon in the desert.

6. This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 12:45 p.m. MST (3:45 p.m. ET) · Mountain America Stadium · ESPN2 [S3][S1]. It's K-State's first visit to Tempe since 1989 [S17].
Last week: ASU trailed Texas Tech 43-10 at halftime and lost 53-25 [S10]. Kansas State came from behind to beat Kansas 35-24, with 568 yards of offense and 359 on the ground [S6].
Our offense vs. their defense: K-State allows only 136.3 passing yards a game and has 13 sacks [S2]. Our pass protection gave up a season-high six sacks last week, even with center Tana Alo-Tupuola and guard Wade Helton back from missed time [S9][S10].
Their offense vs. our defense: the Wildcats run the ball well, at 6.23 yards a carry [S2]. Quarterback Avery Johnson has 462 rushing yards to go with 1,301 passing [S5], and running back Joe Jackson ran for 159 yards against Kansas [S6]. Our run defense allows 4.80 a carry [S2], so tackling is the whole story. Arizona Sports pointed to tackling as a problem at Texas Tech [S10].
Series: Arizona State leads 6-1 and won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024 [S4][S5].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham said he would "assess all personnel" after watching the tape and has not named a starting quarterback [S8]. Johnson was shaken up against Kansas but said he only had the wind knocked out of him [S7].
What decides it: (1) Boley or Keene, and how quickly that quarterback gets settled. (2) Whether our front can win at the point of attack against K-State's run game. (3) Protection. Six sacks can't happen again.
And to Hattie Brandvold, K-State's insider: welcome to Tempe, sweetie! I left a cold water bottle at your seat. It's a dry heat, but your crops will still wilt.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in Tempe? Grab a seafood lunch at Casey Moore's Oyster House on South Ash Avenue before kickoff.

report.title: "That's a Five-Way Take": Skyline Abernathy Welcomes the Unbeaten Red Raiders for Homecoming No. 100
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hello, Bearcats, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Lionel Abernathy, but everybody calls me Skyline, for reasons that will become obvious very quickly. I'm an engineering co-op kid, I chart everything, and I rank it all in Cincinnati chili ways. A three-way is solid. A four-way is impressive. A five-way, with onions AND beans, is reserved for greatness. That goes for quarterbacks, defensive fronts and, yes, coaches' haircuts. When we win, I upgrade the team on air, three-way to five-way, no hesitation. When we lose, I downgrade to "plain spaghetti" and stare quietly into the distance. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a food tangent that somehow loops back into a very sharp stat. I travel with this team and I live with this team. That's a five-way take. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Cincinnati has played football on the Nippert Stadium site since 1901, which makes it the second-oldest playing site in college football [S10]. That's history with extra cheese. In 2021 the Bearcats became the first team from outside the Power Five to make the College Football Playoff, where they played Alabama in the Cotton Bowl [S11]. Now we're in the Big 12, and Saturday is our 100th Homecoming game [S5]. Nippert is listed at 40,000 seats [S2], and every one of them should be full.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Scott Satterfield became the 43rd head coach in program history on Dec. 5, 2022 [S12]. The 2026 numbers say this offense is a five-way: 35.2 points and 460.0 yards a game, on about 59% runs at 5.93 yards a carry, with 20 rushing touchdowns [S2]. Here's the best stat in the whole league, and I don't say that lightly: Cincinnati has lost just two turnovers all season and hasn't thrown a single interception. Both are the best in the country [S4]. The defense is more of a three-way right now. It allows 26.8 points and 434.3 yards a game, and 294.0 passing yards [S2][S4]. The pass rush has 13 sacks [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB JC French IV: 1,338 yards, 9 TD and zero interceptions [S4]. At West Virginia he went 22 of 30 for a career-high 389 yards and accounted for four touchdowns [S5].
• RB Cole Tabb: 448 yards and 8 rushing TD [S4]. He had 118 rushing yards, 54 receiving yards and 3 TDs at West Virginia, his third three-touchdown game of the season [S5].
• WR JV Gibson: 342 yards and 4 TD [S4]. WR Malachi Henry: caught a 69-yard pass at West Virginia, the team's longest play of the season, plus a 59-yarder [S5].
• LB Jonathan Thompson (fifth-year): a team-high 42 tackles [S4], including a career-high 15 last week [S5]. Josh Hough: 3 sacks [S4].
• P Max Fletcher: rolled a 66-yard punt dead at the West Virginia 1 late in the game [S5].

5. The Conference Picture

Cincinnati is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 4-0 at home and 0-2 on the road [S2]. The Bearcats are not ranked [S2]. They beat Kansas State 31-26 at home, then lost 34-7 at Arizona and 45-42 at West Virginia [S2]. Next up is two straight ranked teams at home, Texas Tech and then Utah [S5]. Coming home to Nippert is like coming home to a warm bowl of chili.

6. This Week: No. 8 Texas Tech (6-0) at Cincinnati (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Nippert Stadium · FS1 · Homecoming No. 100 [S3][S5][S1]. It's Texas Tech's first visit ever to Nippert [S3].
Last week: we put up 622 yards at West Virginia, the most against an FBS opponent since last season [S5]. We led 42-35 late but lost 45-42 on a field goal at the final horn [S5]. Satterfield said, "We kept scoring, and we needed to get a stop." [S5] Texas Tech beat Arizona State 53-25 [S6].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the heavyweight four-way. Texas Tech allows only 2.87 yards a carry and 82.0 rushing yards a game [S2][S4], and its 11 interceptions are second-most in the country [S4]. Our run game (5.93 a carry) and French's perfect interception record go right into that [S2][S4].
Their offense vs. our defense: Tech runs on 56% of plays at 5.12 a carry [S2]. RB J'Koby Williams ran for 165 yards last week [S7]. QB Will Hammond has thrown 5 interceptions [S4], so there are chances to take the ball away.
Series: Tech won 44-41 in Lubbock in 2024, and the teams tied 10-10 in 1968 [S3].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S13].
What decides it: (1) Can we keep the ball safe against a defense that loves to take it away? (2) Can our run game get any room against a defense allowing 2.87 a carry? (3) Can our defense finally make the late stop?
And to Bodie Ratliff, Texas Tech's insider: you're a man of few words, so here are a few: welcome to Cincinnati. Have some chili. Three-way at minimum.

report.title: "Cyclone Warning in Effect": Twyla Hemmingsen Forecasts the Trip to Tucson
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Good evening, Cyclone Nation, and here's your Saturday forecast from The Cover Window! I'm Twyla Hemmingsen, your Iowa State insider, coming to you live from the Ames weather center. Okay, it's my kitchen, but it has a very nice map on the wall. I'm high-energy, a little nerdy and joyful about it, and I talk about football the way the TV meteorologist talks about a cold front: pressure systems, wind shifts, and a big red blob moving across the screen. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a full radar sweep of the opponent. Expect conditions to change quickly. When things are going our way, you'll hear "Seventy percent chance of loud." When it's really rolling: "Cyclone warning in effect." Umbrellas optional, joy mandatory. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Our home is Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, which holds 61,500 [S2]. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete. The stadium got his name in 1997 [S14], and it is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man [S13]. Every Cyclone fan should know his story. On the field, Iowa State went 8-4 last season [S12]. Then came the biggest offseason storm in the country. Coach Matt Campbell left for Penn State and took three-year starting QB Rocco Becht with him. More than 50 Cyclones entered the transfer portal, including 16 starters [S12]. That's a full barometric reset.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jimmy Rogers was named Iowa State's 34th head coach on Dec. 5, 2025, coming from Washington State on a six-year contract [S11]. Before that he went 27-3 and won an FCS national title at South Dakota State, and he brought in more than 45 transfers to rebuild this roster [S12]. The 2026 numbers say this team runs. Iowa State runs on about 59% of its plays, at 5.0 yards a carry, for 181.5 rushing yards a game [S2][S3]. It averages 29.7 points and 359.7 yards a game, which is 12th in the Big 12 in total offense [S2][S3]. The defense allows 21.7 points a game [S2]. The best part of the forecast: Iowa State has forced eight turnovers and lost only five [S2].

4. Players to Know

• RB Aiden Flora: 680 yards and 6 TD on 90 carries [S5]. That's the jet stream right there. He ran for 86 yards at BYU [S7].
• QB Jaylen Raynor: 85 of 148 for 1,001 yards, 7 TD and 4 INT [S5]. At BYU he went 16 of 29 for 98 yards and a touchdown [S7].
• WR Dominic Overby: 10 catches for 212 yards [S5]. He left the BYU game in the first quarter with a knee injury, and it has been reported as season-ending [S10].
• LB Sullivan Schlimgen: the team's leading tackler. Sources differ on his total: 56 in one CFBD-based preview [S7] and 35 in another snapshot [S6] (conflicting).
• DE Isaac Terrell: 3 sacks [S5].

5. The Conference Picture

Iowa State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 3-1 at home and 0-2 on the road [S2]. The Cyclones are not ranked [S2]. They lost 16-13 at Iowa, 31-17 at home to Utah and 24-10 at BYU, and beat West Virginia 45-42 at home [S2]. A road win at a ranked team would brighten the whole radar.

6. This Week: Iowa State (3-3) at No. 25 Arizona (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. MST) · Arizona Stadium (Casino Del Sol Stadium), Tucson · ESPN2 · Arizona homecoming [S3][S4][S1]. It's Iowa State's first game in Tucson since 1966 [S3].
Last time out: Both teams are coming off bye weeks [S3]. Iowa State lost 24-10 at No. 8 BYU on Oct. 9 and was held to 200 total yards [S8][S9]. Arizona won 52-31 at West Virginia, its fourth straight win [S2][S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Arizona allows just 3.34 yards a carry and 19.0 points a game, and it has 15 sacks [S2]. Our ground game will be heading into a strong high-pressure system.
Their offense vs. our defense: Arizona throws for 303.8 yards a game [S2]. QB Noah Fifita has 1,756 yards and 16 touchdowns [S5], and at West Virginia he threw for 341 yards and 3 TDs, 183 of them to Isaiah Mizell [S7].
Series: Arizona leads 4-2-1 [S5]. Iowa State won the last meeting, 39-14 in Ames on Sept. 27, 2025 [S5][S3].
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 9 sacks and has allowed 8, with 8 takeaways against 5 giveaways, and it has 11 rushing and 9 passing touchdowns [S2].
Availability: Overby is reported out for the season [S10]. I found no other official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Flora and our run game stay ahead of the chains against a defense allowing 3.34 a carry? (2) Can our secondary keep Fifita's deep shots under control? (3) Turnovers. We're plus-3 and Arizona is minus-3 [S2].
And to Inez Paloverde, Arizona's insider: your forecast says sunshine, dear. Mine says a 30% chance of a Cyclone in the desert. Bring a light jacket.

report.title: "You Can't Rush a Harvest": Hattie Brandvold Takes the Wildcats to the Desert
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy, Wildcat family, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Hattie Brandvold. I have an agronomy degree, a purple denim jacket, a wheat-sheaf brooch and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I explain defensive fronts the only way I know how: crop rotation. Every drive gets named after a crop. A three-and-out is a dry sorghum patch. A long, patient march is winter wheat. And a touchdown? That's a bumper harvest, and you will hear me holler it. When we win, I do the Wabash Cannonball in my chair, tidy and joyful. When we lose, I whisper my most treasured words, "You can't rush a harvest," and I plant a tiny basil seed right there on set. Sweet as prairie pie, until I hand you the one fact that ends the argument. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Kansas State football is the story of the biggest turnaround in the sport. When Bill Snyder took over in 1989, the program was in the middle of a 27-game winless streak. He turned it into a national contender that went to 11 straight bowl games and had six 11-win seasons in a seven-year stretch [S19]. Snyder won two Big 12 championships, one in 2003 with Darren Sproles and one in 2012 [S12]. He went into the College Football Hall of Fame while still coaching, in December 2015 [S12]. The Wildcats play at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan [S2], and the rivalry with Kansas is the Sunflower Showdown, played for the Governor's Cup [S6]. As of last Saturday, K-State has won that game 18 straight times, the longest active winning streak by any team in a rivalry game [S6]. Now that's a crop that keeps coming back every spring.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Collin Klein was named the 36th head coach in school history on Dec. 4, 2025 [S11]. You may remember him as the quarterback: he was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award that year, when K-State won the Big 12 [S11][S13]. He is the first K-State alum to be head coach since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77 [S11]. Before this job he coached nine years in Manhattan, including two as offensive coordinator (2022-23) that went 19-8 with a Big 12 title, then ran the offense at Texas A&M [S11]. The 2026 numbers say this offense grows on the ground. K-State runs on about 54% of its plays and gains 6.23 yards a carry, with 15 rushing touchdowns [S2]. It averages 35.5 points and 464.7 yards a game [S2]. On defense, the Wildcats allow 20.0 points and 296.3 yards a game, and only 136.3 passing yards [S2]. They have 13 sacks and have allowed just 3 [S2]. One weed to pull: six turnovers lost against four forced [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Avery Johnson (senior, Wichita): 1,301 passing yards and 462 rushing yards, leading the team in both [S5]. Against Kansas he passed for 209 yards and a touchdown and ran for 132, and he became the school's all-time leader in total offensive yards [S6]. He went down after a 59-yard run and pointed to his right shoulder, but he returned and said, "I just got the wind knocked out of me." [S7]
• RB Joe Jackson (senior): a season-high 159 yards and a touchdown against Kansas [S6][S7].
• WR Jaron Tibbs: the team's leading receiver with 268 yards [S5].
• K Luis Rodriguez: four field goals against Kansas, from 22, 51, 28 and 34 yards, the second-most in a game in school history [S6].
• DB Logan Bartley: made an end-zone interception against Kansas [S6].
I could not find official season defensive leaders from a source newer than the start of October, so I'm not listing them.

5. The Conference Picture

K-State is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 4-1 at home and 0-1 on the road [S2]. The Wildcats are not ranked in the AP or Coaches poll this week [S2]. The two league losses came at Cincinnati, 31-26, and at home against Houston, 35-16 [S2][S6]. The top two teams in the Big 12 meet in the championship game [S4], so a 1-2 start means every Saturday from here matters.

6. This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. MST) · Mountain America Stadium, Tempe · ESPN2 [S3][S1]. It's K-State's first game in Tempe since the 1989 season opener, and the Wildcats' last game in this stadium was a 31-14 bowl win over Michigan in 2013 [S17].
Last week: K-State trailed Kansas 17-7 in the first quarter, then won 35-24 and racked up 568 yards, 359 of them on the ground [S6]. Arizona State lost 53-25 at Texas Tech. Coach Kenny Dillingham replaced quarterback Cutter Boley with Mikey Keene at halftime, and Keene threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns [S8][S10].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is where my winter wheat should grow. Arizona State allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry [S2]. Texas Tech gained 7.8 yards a play against the Sun Devils last week [S10].
Their offense vs. our defense: ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game [S2], and senior receiver Reed Harris is a big-play threat [S16][S9]. But the Sun Devils have allowed 15 sacks, including a season-high six at Texas Tech [S2][S9]. K-State has 13 sacks of its own [S2].
Series: Arizona State leads 6-1, and the Sun Devils won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024 [S4][S5]. K-State's lone win was 34-27 on Dec. 27, 2002 [S5].
Availability: Johnson's shoulder scare turned out to be the wind knocked out of him [S7]. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham has not named a starting quarterback for this game [S8][S9].
What decides it: (1) Can K-State's run game keep producing like it did against Kansas? (2) Who plays quarterback for Arizona State, Boley or Keene? (3) Can our pass rush get home against a front that gave up six sacks last week?
And to Skylar Vanterpool, Arizona State's insider: I'll bring the shade hat and the water jug, darlin'. Hydrate all you like. You still can't rush a harvest.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching from Manhattan? Varsity Donuts on North Manhattan Avenue is how I start every game-day morning.

report.title: "Yeehaw, That's a Turnover": Ryder Galloway Welcomes the Mountaineers to Cowtown
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy, Frog fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Ryder Galloway, your TCU insider. I'm a Stockyards cowboy who became a finance guy, so I wear boots with a quarter-zip and I explain defenses as cattle drives. You've got your point riders, your flank riders and your drag riders, and when everyone holds their spot, nobody gets loose. I travel with this team and I live with this team. Fair warning: if something goes wrong, anything at all, I will probably blame Dallas. Flat tire? Dallas. Missed field goal? Dallas. When we win, it's "Yeehaw!" and my hat goes flying. When we lose, I mutter about Dallas some more. And the best sound in football is me hollering "Yeehaw, that's a turnover!" Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Fort Worth style. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

TCU has a national title on the wall. The 1938 Horned Frogs went 11-0, beat Carnegie Tech 15-7 in the Sugar Bowl and won the national championship [S8]. Quarterback Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy that year [S8]. The 2010 team went 13-0 and won the Rose Bowl [S9], and in 2022 Sonny Dykes led TCU all the way to the College Football Playoff national championship game [S9]. Home is Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, listed at 46,000 [S2]. Not one bit of that history happened in Dallas. And the rivalry with Baylor has a name now, the Revivalry, and we just won it in Waco [S7]. Ten more minutes on that and I'd be throwing my hat again.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Sonny Dykes was hired on Nov. 29, 2021 [S2], and in his first season he took the Frogs to the national title game [S9]. The 2026 numbers say defense is driving this herd. TCU allows only 12.2 points and 264.2 yards a game [S2]. Opponents average 2.88 yards a carry and 172.2 passing yards, and the Frogs have 14 sacks [S2]. Every rider is holding his spot. The offense throws for 282.3 yards a game and averages 24.0 points [S2]. The run game needs work, at 3.27 yards a carry, and the blockers have given up 17 sacks [S2]. Turnovers are close: 9 lost, 8 forced [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Jaden Craig: 1,694 yards and 10 TD [S4]. At Baylor he went 21 of 36 for 294 yards and two touchdowns [S7].
• WR Jordan Dwyer: 6 catches for 150 yards at Baylor [S7]. WR Ed Small: 7 catches, 91 yards and a touchdown in that game [S7].
• RB Jeremy Payne: team-high 429 rushing yards and 2 TD [S4].
• DE Koron Hayward: three of TCU's four sacks at Baylor [S7]. S Jamel Johnson: intercepted a pass at Baylor [S7]. LB Hudson Hooper: team-high 33 tackles [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

TCU is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 2-1 at home and 1-1 on the road [S2]. The Frogs are not ranked [S2]. All three losses were close: 15-10 to North Carolina at a neutral site, 21-13 at UCF and 17-10 at home to BYU [S2]. The offense needs to catch up to this defense, and a home win would get us back to .500 in the league.

6. This Week: West Virginia (4-3) at TCU (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 11 a.m. CT (noon ET) · Amon G. Carter Stadium · ESPN2 [S3][S4][S1]. Forecast: 74 degrees and mostly sunny [S4].
Last week: TCU won the Revivalry at Baylor 17-6. The defense held the Bears without a touchdown and kept them scoreless in the second half [S7]. West Virginia beat Cincinnati 45-42 on a 35-yard field goal as time ran out [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: West Virginia allows 34.0 points and 483.9 yards a game, and 310.1 passing yards [S2]. Craig to Dwyer and Small should have room to run.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the big cattle drive. West Virginia runs on 72% of its plays [S2] and came into last week averaging 295.5 rushing yards a game [S5]. QB Michael Hawkins Jr. leads FBS in rushing touchdowns [S4], and RB Cam Cook is fifth in rushing yards [S4]. Our run defense allows 2.88 a carry [S2]. Cincinnati held them to 134 rushing yards last week [S5], but Hawkins threw for 464 [S5].
Series: West Virginia leads 8-6 [S4].
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 14 sacks and has allowed 17, with 8 takeaways against 9 giveaways, and it has 7 rushing and 10 passing touchdowns [S2].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our front keep Hawkins and Cook boxed in? (2) Can our offense finally get the run game going? It's averaging 3.27 a carry [S2]. (3) Turnovers. Yeehaw time.
And to Jolene Buckhannon, West Virginia's insider: ma'am, I hear you don't miss. Neither does our defense. Welcome to Fort Worth, where the West begins.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in Fort Worth? The original Fuzzy's Taco Shop on Bryant Irvin Road. Tacos, not Dallas.

report.title: "Guns Up, Wind's Up": Bodie Ratliff Rides Into Nippert
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Howdy. Bodie Ratliff. Texas Tech insider for The Cover Window. I ride bareback at the rodeo, and in tumbleweed season I chart Air Raid concepts on the back of feed-store receipts. I travel with the team. I live with the team. People say I don't talk much. They're right. One word usually does it, and the wind fills in the rest. Somebody asks how the defense looked? "Mean." How was the trip? "Windy." When we win, I say "Guns up," real quiet, and then I grin longer than anybody's comfortable with. When we lose, I stare into the wind with my hat in my hand. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup from inside the program, West Texas plain. My motto: "Guns up, wind's up." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Last season was the best in school history. Texas Tech went 12-2, crushed BYU 34-7 to win the Big 12 championship and made its first College Football Playoff [S8]. That was the program's first outright conference title since 1955 [S9]. The run ended with a 23-0 loss to Oregon in the Orange Bowl [S8]. Home is Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, listed at 60,454 [S2]. And the run hasn't stopped: Tech is 18-2 since the start of 2025, and 17 of those wins came by double digits [S6]. Long story short. "Good."

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Joey McGuire was hired on Nov. 8, 2021 [S2]. He's 41-18 in five seasons and 26-5 at home [S6]. The Air Raid jokes still follow us around, but this team is built on the ground and on defense. Tech runs on about 56% of its plays, at 5.12 yards a carry with 16 rushing touchdowns [S2]. It averages 37.8 points a game [S2]. On defense, opponents gain only 2.87 yards a carry and 82.0 rushing yards a game [S2][S4]. Tech has 17 sacks and 12 takeaways [S2], and its 11 interceptions are the second-most in the country [S4]. One word: "Stingy."

4. Players to Know

• QB Will Hammond: 1,334 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT [S4].
• RB J'Koby Williams: 538 yards and 5 TD [S4]. He had a career day against Arizona State with 165 yards and two scores [S7].
• WR Kenny Johnson: a team-high 418 receiving yards [S4], including 7 catches for 120 last week [S7][S4]. WR Coy Eakin: a team-high 3 receiving TDs [S4].
• K Stone Harrington: 4 of 5 on field goals against Arizona State [S4].
• Defense: A.J. Holmes Jr. leads with 4 sacks, and Austin Romaine leads with 41 tackles [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Texas Tech is 6-0 overall and 3-0 in the Big 12, 4-0 at home and 2-0 on the road [S2]. The Red Raiders are No. 8 in the AP poll and No. 5 in the Coaches Poll this week [S2]. It's their second straight 6-0 start, and a win would make only the fifth 7-0 start in school history [S3]. We've won four straight road games going back to last season, including 35-24 at Oregon State and 29-7 at Colorado this year [S3]. It's one of six unbeaten teams in the country [S3]. Next come back-to-back home dates with Arizona and West Virginia [S3]. One word: "Busy."

6. This Week: No. 8 Texas Tech (6-0) at Cincinnati (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati · FS1 [S3][S1]. It's Texas Tech's first trip ever to Nippert [S3], and Cincinnati's 100th Homecoming game [S5].
Last week: Tech beat Arizona State 53-25 and averaged 7.8 yards a play [S7]. Cincinnati lost 45-42 at West Virginia on a 35-yard field goal as time ran out [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Cincinnati allows 26.8 points and 434.3 yards a game, and 294.0 passing yards [S2][S4]. LB Jonathan Thompson had a career-high 15 tackles last week [S5], and the Bearcats held West Virginia's Big 12-leading run game to 134 yards [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the big one. Cincinnati hasn't thrown an interception all year and has just two turnovers, the fewest in the country [S4]. QB JC French IV threw for a career-high 389 yards last week [S5], and RB Cole Tabb has 8 rushing touchdowns [S4]. They run for 5.93 a carry [S2]. Our run defense allows 2.87 [S2]. Something gives. "Wind."
Series: this is just the third meeting. The teams tied 10-10 in 1968, and Tech won 44-41 in 2024 behind 172 rushing yards from Tahj Brooks [S3].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S13].
What decides it: (1) Can our ball-hawking defense take one away from a team that never gives it up? (2) Can we stop Tabb and French on the ground? (3) Hammond protecting the football on the road.
And to Skyline Abernathy, Cincinnati's insider: chili's good. Wind's better. See you Saturday.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in Lubbock? Robles Taquería on Main Street. Tacos. Enough said.

report.title: "Load Up, I Don't Miss": Jolene Buckhannon Takes the Mountaineers to Fort Worth
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Mornin', Mountaineers. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Jolene Buckhannon. I used to captain the rifle team, so I count possessions the way I used to count rounds: every one matters and you don't waste any. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm calm, flat, deadpan as a holler on a Sunday morning... until I'm not. I also keep a running pepperoni-roll tally of every fumble the other team coughs up. One roll per fumble, and I eat the tally afterward. When we win, I sing one verse of "Country Roads," drop the mic, then lift it right back up, because mics cost money. When we lose, I count to ten out loud, real slow, like I'm reloading. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, straight shooting. "Load up, I don't miss." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Home is Milan Puskar Stadium in Morgantown, listed at 60,000 [S2], and when that place sings "Country Roads," you feel it in your boots. The man in charge is a familiar one. Rich Rodriguez was named the 36th head coach in school history in December 2024, returning to the program he once led [S10]. His teams have always run the football, and this one sure does. The Mountaineers lead the series with TCU 8-6 over 14 meetings [S4]. Last week's finish showed this team's grit: after Cincinnati tied it with 3:44 left, we started a drive at our own 2 and went 82 yards in eight plays to set up the winning kick [S5]. History is fine. I'm more interested in Saturday.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Rodriguez was hired on Dec. 11, 2024 [S2][S10]. The 2026 numbers say run, run, then run some more. West Virginia runs on about 72% of its plays and has 24 rushing touchdowns [S2]. It came into last week averaging 295.5 rushing yards a game, tops in the Big 12 [S5]. The offense puts up 37.6 points and 497.1 yards a game [S2]. Then there's the other side, and I'm going to be honest, because that's what I do. The defense allows 34.0 points and 483.9 yards a game, and 310.1 passing yards [S2]. Turnovers are even at 7 lost and 7 forced [S2]. I'm counting to ten on that defense. Slowly.

4. Players to Know

• QB Michael Hawkins Jr.: 1,519 passing yards and 10 TD, and he leads all of FBS in rushing touchdowns [S4]. Against Cincinnati he threw for a career-best 464 yards and three touchdowns [S5], and he ran 26 times for 77 yards and two more scores [S4].
• RB Cam Cook: 833 yards and 7 TD, fifth in FBS in rushing yards [S4]. Cincinnati held him to 40 on the ground, but he caught a 40-yard touchdown to tie the game late [S5].
• WR Prince Strachan: caught passes of 41 and 39 yards on the final drive against Cincinnati, starting from our own 2 [S5].
• K Jack Cassidy: made the 35-yard field goal as time expired to beat Cincinnati [S5][S6].
• LB Isaiah Patterson: a team-high 44 tackles, plus a sack and an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

West Virginia is 4-3 overall and 1-3 in the Big 12, 3-2 at home and 0-1 on the road, plus a neutral-site win over Virginia [S2]. We're not ranked [S2]. The losses: Oklahoma State 41-24 and Arizona 52-31 at home, and 45-42 at Iowa State [S2]. Winning a road game in Fort Worth would be a big step back toward the middle of the standings.

6. This Week: West Virginia (4-3) at TCU (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth · ESPN2 [S3][S4][S1]. Forecast at kickoff: 74 degrees and mostly sunny [S4].
Last week: we beat Cincinnati 45-42 on Cassidy's kick at the horn after a wild finish [S5][S6]. TCU beat Baylor 17-6 and didn't allow a touchdown [S7].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a real fight. TCU allows only 12.2 points and 264.2 yards a game, and 2.88 yards a carry [S2]. DE Koron Hayward had three sacks against Baylor [S7]. Our run game against that front decides a lot.
Their offense vs. our defense: TCU averages 24.0 points a game and doesn't run much, at 3.27 yards a carry [S2]. But QB Jaden Craig has 1,694 yards and 10 touchdowns [S4], and he threw for 294 against Baylor, with Jordan Dwyer catching six balls for 150 yards [S7]. Our pass defense gives up 310.1 yards a game [S2]. Somebody hand me a pepperoni roll.
Series: West Virginia leads 8-6 [S4].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Hawkins and our run game move against a defense allowing 2.88 a carry? (2) Can our secondary stop Craig and Dwyer from hitting big plays? (3) Possessions. Every one counts. I'll be counting.
And to Ryder Galloway, TCU's insider: I hear you blame everything on Dallas. That's fine. Saturday you can blame it on Morgantown.

report.title: "Objection: Sustained": Siobhan Dunleavy Takes the Eagles to the Flats
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

All rise, Eagles fans. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Siobhan Dunleavy, your Boston College insider, grad student and former debate champion. I argue every play like it's a moot-court case, and I always appoint myself the judge, which my co-hosts find wicked unfair. I travel with this team and I live with this team, with a large iced coffee in hand at all times, including January. When we win, I bang my toy gavel and announce, "Objection overruled, we WON." report.title: "Power to the Play-Call!": Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch Marches the Bears to Dallas
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Greetings, comrades of the Blue and Gold, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, your Cal insider. I'm writing a philosophy dissertation on the ethics of the fourth-down decision, and I have opinions. When I see a bad play-call, I don't just complain. I make a picket sign. I have a closet full of them: "THIRD-AND-LONG IS A SOCIAL CONSTRUCT." "RUN IT ON SECOND DOWN, PLEASE (RESPECTFULLY)." I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I believe, deeply and earnestly, in the people's right to a well-designed screen pass. When we win, I raise a fist and shout "Power to the play-call!" When we lose, I organize a peaceful, fully permitted protest against the punter. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, argued with conviction. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Every Cal fan knows the greatest play in college football history, and we just call it The Play. In the 1982 Big Game against Stanford, the Bears returned the final kickoff through five laterals, and Kevin Moen scored as the Stanford band wandered onto the field. Cal won 25-20 [S6]. Our home is California Memorial Stadium in Berkeley, listed at 62,467 [S2], with the hills right behind it. Cal now plays in the ACC [S2], which means trips like this one to Dallas. A cross-country revolution, if you will.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Tosh Lupoi was named the 35th head coach in program history on Dec. 4, 2025, replacing Justin Wilcox [S5]. The 2026 numbers say Cal throws to win. It passes on about 61% of its plays, and its 288.1 passing yards a game rank 15th in FBS [S2][S3]. The run game needs a movement: 90.3 rushing yards a game ranks 137th, at 3.29 yards a carry [S3][S2]. The offense averages 23.9 points a game [S3], with 12 passing touchdowns and 7 rushing [S2]. The data are clear, comrades: the revolution will be thrown, not run. The defense allows 27.7 points and 387.6 yards a game, and 181.4 rushing yards (111th) [S3]. On the bright side, Cal has forced nine turnovers and lost eight [S2]. And then there are penalties, 81.4 yards a game, 131st in FBS [S3]. I have a sign for that.

4. Players to Know

• QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele: 1,290 yards, 9 TD, 5 INT and 67.0% completions [S3]. He was 15 of 18 for 110 yards and a touchdown at Wake Forest [S3].
• WR Chase Hendricks: 47 catches, 415 yards, 2 TD [S3], including eight catches against Wake [S3].
• RB Adam Mohammed: 336 yards and 3 TD on 73 carries [S3]. RB Ashten Emory: 56 yards on 12 carries last week [S3].
I couldn't verify current defensive leaders from a free source, so I'm leaving them out. Intellectual honesty is a core value.

5. The Conference Picture

Cal is 3-4 overall and 2-2 in the ACC, 2-3 at home and 1-1 on the road [S2]. The Bears are not ranked [S2]. The ACC wins came at Syracuse (21-18) and at home against Virginia Tech (25-20). The losses were to UCLA, Clemson, UNLV and Wake Forest [S2]. A road upset of a ranked team would be a true people's victory. The pass rush gives me hope: 13 sacks so far [S2]. But opponents are averaging 5.07 yards a carry against us [S2], and I've already started painting the sign about that.

6. This Week: California (3-4) at No. 23 SMU (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Gerald J. Ford Stadium, University Park, Texas [S3][S1]. TV is listed as The CW on two game pages, but I couldn't confirm it officially [S4].

Their offense vs. our defense: SMU throws for 329.3 yards a game, fifth in FBS [S3]. QB Kevin Jennings has 1,859 yards and 16 touchdowns [S3]. RB Kendrick Raphael ran for 124 yards last week [S3]. SMU converts 48.1% of third downs, and Cal's defense allows 42.4% (107th) [S3].

What decides it: (1) Can our pass rush and coverage slow Jennings? (2) Can we run the ball at all? (3) Penalties. Both teams are heavily penalized, and SMU is 114th [S3]. Fewer flags, more football.
And to Tatum Delacroix-Price, SMU's insider: I've drafted a picket sign in your honor. It reads "WELCOME, GRACIOUS HOST (WE STILL INTEND TO WIN)."

THE FANATIC EDITION

Greetings, Jackets fans, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Wendell Quist, your Georgia Tech insider. When we win, I calculate the exact trajectory of the winning kick and cheer in decimals. When we lose, I re-run the simulation 10,000 times looking for the bug. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plotted to scale. "Graph paper doesn't lie." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Georgia Tech claims national championships in 1917, 1928 and 1990 [S7]. Home is Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field, listed at 55,000 [S7][S2], in the middle of Midtown Atlanta. Nine passing touchdowns and nine rushing [S2]. The defense is the variable to fix. It allows 392.2 yards a game (110th) and 179.0 rushing yards (110th) [S3]. Turnovers, too: we've lost 7 and forced only 3, a minus-4 margin (113th) [S2][S3]. Penalties average 70.5 yards a game (117th) [S3]. And the clock: we hold the ball only 27:47 a game, 120th in FBS [S3]. Three variables. Solve for all three, and the output improves.

4. Players to Know

I've re-run that simulation more than 10,000 times), Tennessee, at Stanford 34-27 and at Virginia Tech 34-24 [S2]. The wins: Mercer 44-11 and Duke 28-25 [S2]. At Virginia Tech we fell behind 24-3, then cut it to seven early in the second half before falling short [S5]. The comeback curve was there. The finishing slope wasn't. Georgia Tech On SI listed the recurring bugs: turnovers, missed field goals and explosive plays allowed on defense [S5]. Three bugs. Every one is fixable in the code.

6. This Week: Boston College (3-3) at Georgia Tech (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bobby Dodd Stadium · Homecoming [S3][S5][S1]. TV wasn't listed in the AP preview I used.

What decides it: (1) Run defense against McKenzie. (2) Turnovers. We're minus-4 [S3], and BC is plus-1 [S3]. (3) Penalties. Seventy yards a game is a lot of drag. (4) Possession. THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

¡Qué tal, Canes! Welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Javi Castillo, but you can call me The Breeze. I played defensive back at The U back in the day, and now I scout in linen and sunglasses, rain or shine. I travel with this team and I live with this team. My thing is bilingual hype one-liners that always rhyme. "Mensah lets it fly, adiós, goodbye!" I'm working on them. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, smooth as an ocean breeze. When we win, I throw up the "U" with my arms and shout "Swag!" When we lose, I put my sunglasses on indoors and say nothing. Very loudly. My motto never changes: "It's all about the U, baby." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Miami owns five national championships: 1983, 1987, 1989, 1991 and 2001 [S8]. Last season the Canes made it all the way to the national championship game, losing 27-21 to Indiana at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026 [S9]. Hard Rock is listed at 64,767 [S2]. This year the Canes are No. 1 in both the AP and Coaches polls [S2]. Miami is the only FBS team that has scored at least 30 points in every game this season [S4]. Sí, señor.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Mario Cristobal was hired on Dec. 6, 2021 [S2][S8]. The 2026 numbers are ridiculous, in the best way. Miami scores 48.5 points a game, the most in FBS, and averages 559.5 yards a game, second in FBS [S3]. It throws for 333.0 yards a game (third) and runs for 226.5 (13th), at 6.09 yards a carry [S3][S2]. On defense, the Canes allow just 14.0 points a game (seventh) and 58.5 rushing yards a game (second) [S3]. They have 18 sacks and have allowed only 6 [S2]. They hold the ball for an average of 33:58 a game, sixth in FBS [S3]. Miami converts 51.6% of its third downs (12th in FBS), and its red-zone defense ranks sixth, with opponents scoring on 66.7% of trips [S3]. The Canes are plus-4 in turnover margin [S3]. Smooth like the breeze. The one spot to watch: the pass defense allows 223.3 yards a game, 91st [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Darian Mensah: 1,764 yards, 18 TD and just 1 INT, completing 80.8% of his passes [S3]. That's fourth in FBS in touchdown passes [S4]. Against Florida State he went 23 of 34 for 326 yards and three touchdowns [S3].
• WR Malachi Toney: 50 catches for 758 yards and 8 TD, fourth in FBS in receiving yards [S3][S4]. He had 11 catches for 154 yards and two touchdowns against the Seminoles [S3].
• RB Javian Mallory: 397 yards and 5 TD on 52 carries [S3]. Against FSU: 13 carries, 108 yards, two scores [S3].
• LB Mohamed Toure: a team-high 30 tackles, including 12 against Florida State [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Miami is 6-0 overall and 4-0 in the ACC, 3-0 at home and 3-0 on the road [S2]. The Canes are No. 1 in the AP and Coaches polls [S2]. They're one of six unbeaten teams in FBS [S4]. Road wins at Stanford, Wake Forest and Clemson (41-13) show this team travels well [S2]. Next up is a trip to North Carolina [S3].

6. This Week: Pittsburgh (5-2) at No. 1 Miami (6-0)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Hard Rock Stadium · ESPN [S3][S1]. Forecast: 80 degrees, a 44% chance of storms and an 18 mph northeast wind [S4]. Typical South Florida, mi gente.
Last week: Miami beat Florida State 43-35 [S3]. Pitt lost 27-21 at Boston College [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Pitt has the best run defense in FBS, allowing 57.3 yards a game [S3]. But its pass defense ranks 115th at 249.0 yards a game [S3]. Mensah to Toney, baby. "The ball's in the air, Toney's there!"
Their offense vs. our defense: Pitt lost starting QB Mason Heintschel for the season to a torn ACL [S6]. Corey Dailey started at BC and went 11 of 25 with two interceptions [S3], and Narduzzi hasn't named a starter for this game [S6]. WR Cataurus Hicks is a big-play threat, with 135 yards last week [S3].
Series: Miami leads 30-12-1 [S4].
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 18 sacks and has allowed 6, with 8 takeaways against 4 giveaways, and it has 17 rushing and 21 passing touchdowns [S2].
Availability: one unofficial site reports LB Max Buchanan out after knee surgery. I could not confirm that from an official source, so treat it as unconfirmed [S10]. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Pitt's run defense slow down our ground game? It's the best in the country against the run. (2) Can our defense take advantage of a new Pitt quarterback? (3) Weather. Storms could slow both offenses.
And to Yinz Bertolucci, Pitt's insider: much respect, hermano. Enjoy the sunshine. And grab some cafecito, it's on me.

report.title: "Carolina Blue, Through and Through": Ainsley Pemberton Welcomes the Orange to Kenan
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Carolina blue, through and through. Hello, darlings, I'm Ainsley Pemberton. I grew up in Chapel Hill, I came out at a debutante ball, and then I went and earned a PhD in kinesiology, because a lady should understand exactly how a linebacker generates force. I travel with the Tar Heels and I live with the Tar Heels, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with Southern charm and, I'll confess, a gentle little roast of a certain school eight miles down the road. I don't even need Duke to be on the schedule. When we win, I graciously thank our guests, then whisper "Carolina blue, through and through." When we lose, I say "Carolina blue skies will return," and I absolutely refuse to cry on camera. Mostly. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Tar Heels, often just "Carolina," represent the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in the ACC [S7]. North Carolina has played in 37 bowl games and won three Southern Conference titles and five ACC titles [S7]. Home is Kenan Stadium, opened in 1927 and listed at 50,500 seats [S3], and darling, there is no prettier place in college football on an autumn evening. The last five seasons: 6-7, a lovely 9-5 in 2022, 8-5, 6-7 and 4-8 last year [S3].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Bill Belichick is our head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2024 [S3]. This team wins with defense and discipline. We allow 19.2 points a game, 34th in FBS [S5], our red zone defense ranks 22nd [S5], and we average just 33.7 penalty yards a game, 5th in the country [S5]. Darling, that's manners. Xavier Lewis has 7 sacks [S4]. The offense is a work in progress: 329.7 yards a game (117th) and 116.2 rushing yards (120th) [S5]. And opponents convert 43.3% of third downs against us (113th) [S5]. Elegant, mostly. Not always. But a team that wins close games on the road, two weeks in a row, has learned how to finish, and finishing is the most elegant skill of all [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Billy Edwards Jr.: 94 of 157 for about 1,260 yards (1,259 per AP), 9 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. A first-year Tar Heel, he said he felt "the weight of this game" against Duke [S9].
• WR Jordan Shipp: 33 catches, 441 yards [S4][S5]. He caught the first touchdown at Duke and said, "That's why you come to Carolina, for a rivalry game like that" [S9].
• RB Jaylen McGill: 12 carries for 75 yards and the game-winning 24-yard touchdown with 1:53 left at Duke [S5][S9]. RB Benjamin Hall: the season leader with 283 yards [S4].
• TE Jelani Thurman: caught the 12-yard fourth-and-4 conversion on the winning drive [S9].
• DL Xavier Lewis: 7 sacks [S4]. LB Derek McDonald: team-high 55 tackles [S4]. DB Greg Smith III: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

North Carolina is 4-2 and 2-1 in the ACC [S3]. We beat TCU 15-10 at a neutral site, East Tennessee State 35-3, Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and Duke 24-20 on the road [S3]. We lost at Clemson 28-20 and to Notre Dame 37-26 [S3]. After Syracuse, No. 1 Miami comes to Kenan on Oct. 31 [S5]. I won't do standings math, darling. I'll only say it's a lovely time to be wearing blue.
And the Victory Bell is home. After the Duke game, our players rushed across the field to reclaim it [S9]. AP says the bell kept ringing so loudly outside the locker room it nearly interrupted Coach Belichick's press conference [S9]. I'd call that the sweetest music in the Triangle. And two years ago in that same stadium, Duke rallied from 20 points down to beat us [S9]. This time, darling, the bell came home with us, where it belongs. Duke had won eight straight against in-state opponents before we arrived [S9]. Bless their hearts.

6. This Week: Syracuse (2-4) at North Carolina (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill · ACC Network [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we beat Duke 24-20. We led 17-0, went more than 41 minutes without scoring, then marched 78 yards for the winner [S9]. On fourth-and-4 from our own 28, Coach said, "I wasn't punting again. I wanted to take our best shot" [S9]. Syracuse lost to Louisville 34-26 [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: Syracuse throws for 291 yards a game (12th) [S5], and Umari Hatcher has 784 receiving yards, including 224 last week [S5]. Darling, we must know where he is at all times. Their quarterback situation is unsettled; no Week 8 ACC report yet [S10][S11].
Our offense vs. their defense: Syracuse's pass defense ranks 43rd and its run defense 64th [S5]. Syracuse is also 138th in penalty yards [S5]. Free yards are always welcome at Kenan.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
Availability: no North Carolina availability report found as of Oct. 18 [S12].
What decides it: (1) Containing Hatcher. (2) Getting off the field on third down. (3) Staying the most disciplined team on the field [S5].
To Nico Calabrese, Syracuse's insider: a snowbank shaped like a block S? How charming. We have dogwoods. Come in April, darling.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Chapel Hill for the game? La Residence on West Rosemary Street is a lovely sit-down supper.
