report.title: "Dat's a Yinz Problem, Not a Yikes Problem": Yinz Bertolucci Takes the Panthers to No. 1 Miami
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hey, Pitt fans! How's it goin', n'at? Welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Dominic Bertolucci, but around here they call me Yinz. I played linebacker back in a little steel-mill town, and these days I grade every tackle this team makes on my personal scale. It goes from "yinz," meaning a beautiful, textbook form tackle, all the way down to "yikes," meaning somebody whiffed. I blow a homemade whistle for every grade. The producers love it. Okay, they tolerate it. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I holler "Yinz SEE that?!" so loud the board op flinches. When we lose, I eat a sandwich with the fries right inside it, in total silence. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, loud and lovable. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Pitt has a national championship in its trophy case: the 1976 Panthers went 12-0, and running back Tony Dorsett won the Heisman Trophy that season [S7]. Then in 2021 under Pat Narduzzi, Pitt won its first ACC championship, beating Wake Forest 45-21 in the title game [S7]. Home is Acrisure Stadium, listed at 68,400 [S2], right there on the North Shore. The series with Miami is a long one, 43 meetings, though the Hurricanes lead 30-12-1 [S4]. Dat's history, n'at.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Pat Narduzzi was hired on Dec. 16, 2014 [S2]. Defense is his thing, and this year's group is a "yinz" all the way. Pitt allows only 57.3 rushing yards a game, the best in FBS, and 16.4 points a game, 23rd [S3]. Opponents average 2.02 yards a carry [S2]. The Panthers have 15 sacks and 11 takeaways [S2]. The offense puts up 32.9 points and 450.1 yards a game, and its 284.6 passing yards rank 17th [S3]. Now for the "yikes" section: 81.7 penalty yards a game, which ranks 132nd [S3]. And the pass defense allows 249.0 yards a game, 115th [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Mason Heintschel: 1,304 yards, 14 TD and only 1 INT [S3]. But he tore the ACL in his right knee at Virginia Tech and is out for the season [S6]. Prayers for a full recovery, kid.
• QB Corey Dailey: made his first start at Boston College and went 11 of 25 for 193 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions [S3][S5]. Narduzzi said he hasn't decided who will start at Miami [S6].
• RB Damon Ferguson Jr.: 438 yards and 3 TD on 83 carries [S3], including 119 yards at BC [S3].
• WR Cataurus Hicks: 26 catches, 500 yards, 4 TD [S3]. He had five catches for 135 yards and a touchdown at BC [S3].
• DB Cruce Brookins: a team-high 46 tackles [S4]. That's a whole lotta "yinz."

5. The Conference Picture

Pitt is 5-2 overall and 2-2 in the ACC, 4-1 at home and 1-1 on the road [S2]. We're not ranked [S2]. We started 5-0, including a 35-33 win at Virginia Tech, but then lost 21-17 at home to North Carolina and 27-21 at Boston College [S2]. Beating No. 1 on the road would flip this whole season around.

6. This Week: Pittsburgh (5-2) at No. 1 Miami (6-0)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens · ESPN [S3][S1]. Forecast: 80 degrees, a 44% chance of storms and an 18 mph wind [S4].
Last week: Pitt lost 27-21 at Boston College [S5]. Miami beat Florida State 43-35 [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a big ask. Miami allows only 58.5 rushing yards a game, second in FBS, and 14.0 points a game [S3]. Opponents average 2.34 yards a carry [S2]. We'll need Hicks to make plays down the field.
Their offense vs. our defense: Miami scores 48.5 points a game, the most in FBS, and it's the only team that has scored 30 or more in every game [S3][S4]. QB Darian Mensah has 18 touchdowns, one interception and an 80.8% completion rate [S3]. WR Malachi Toney has 758 yards [S3]. Our run defense is the best in the country [S3], but Miami's passing game is the real test for a pass defense ranked 115th [S3].
Series: Miami leads 30-12-1 [S4].
Availability: Heintschel is out for the season [S6]. Pitt hasn't named a starting quarterback [S6]. One unofficial site reports Miami LB Max Buchanan out after knee surgery, but I could not confirm it officially [S10]. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Who plays quarterback for Pitt, and can he protect the ball? (2) Can our secondary slow down Mensah and Toney? (3) Penalties. We can't give a team this good free yards.
And to Javi Castillo, Miami's insider: nice sunglasses, buddy. Bring 'em to Pittsburgh sometime and we'll find out if they work in the snow.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in Oakland? Hello Bistro on Forbes Avenue for a quick game-day bite.

report.title: "Pony Up or Sit Down, Sugar": Tatum Delacroix-Price Welcomes Cal to the Hilltop
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, hello, Mustangs, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Tatum Delacroix-Price, your SMU insider. I run a little boutique in Highland Park. I know every handshake in this town, and I know every nickel blitz in our playbook. I travel with this team and I live with this team. Now, fair warning: I grade the other team's sideline outfits on air, and darling, I am never wrong. Polished, sweet as can be, and then savage. That's the Dallas way. When we win, I pop imaginary confetti and declare the Boulevard officially iconic. When we lose, I put on bigger sunglasses. Much bigger. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with just a little sparkle. My motto: "Pony up or sit down, sugar." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

SMU has a Heisman Trophy winner: Doak Walker in 1948 [S7]. Then came the Pony Express era, with Eric Dickerson and Craig James in the backfield [S7]. More recently, the Mustangs played in the 2024 ACC championship game and lost to Clemson 34-31 on a field goal at the end [S7]. Home is Gerald J. Ford Stadium in University Park, listed at 32,000 [S2], an intimate little jewel box of a stadium. And it's spotless. This season that little jewel box has been perfect: four home games, four wins [S2]. Bring your sunglasses, Cal. The regular ones, I mean.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Rhett Lashlee was hired on Nov. 30, 2021 [S2]. The 2026 numbers say SMU lives through the air: 329.3 passing yards a game, fifth in FBS, and 470.8 total yards, 14th [S3]. It averages 32.7 points a game and converts 48.1% of third downs (23rd) [S3]. The defense is a showstopper against the pass, allowing just 164.8 yards a game, 11th in FBS [S3]. SMU has 18 sacks and has allowed only 7 [S2]. Overall the defense allows 303.0 yards a game, 26th in FBS. It's a bit softer against the run (138.2 yards a game, 61st) than the pass [S3]. Two things that need a tailor: 69.0 penalty yards a game (114th), and a red-zone offense that scores on 81.5% of trips (95th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Kevin Jennings: 1,859 yards, 16 TD, 5 INT and 72.9% completions [S3]. He was 23 of 36 for 246 yards and two touchdowns against Virginia, with no interceptions [S3].
• RB Kendrick Raphael: 542 yards and 6 TD on 99 carries [S3], including 124 yards against the Cavaliers [S3].
• WR Yamir Knight: 35 catches, 418 yards, 2 TD [S3]. WR Yannick Smith: 5 catches for 87 yards last week [S3].
I couldn't verify defensive leaders from a free source as of Oct. 18, so I'm not naming names. A lady doesn't guess.

5. The Conference Picture

SMU is 5-1 overall and 3-1 in the ACC, 4-0 at home and 1-1 on the road [S2]. The Mustangs are No. 23 in the AP poll and No. 20 in the Coaches Poll [S2]. The only loss came at Louisville, 41-31, and the wins include a 27-24 road win at Florida State [S2]. Next comes a trip to Syracuse [S3]. Keep winning and SMU stays in the ACC title conversation. At home the Mustangs have outscored visitors 138-63 [S2]. Fair warning, though: the turnover column needs work, with 9 lost and only 6 forced [S2]. Darling, we do not hand out free gifts at this boutique.

6. This Week: California (3-4) at No. 23 SMU (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Gerald J. Ford Stadium [S3][S1]. Two game pages list the TV as The CW, but I couldn't confirm that officially [S4].
Last week: SMU beat Virginia 23-13 [S3]. Cal lost 41-7 to Wake Forest [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Cal allows 27.7 points a game and 181.4 rushing yards (111th) [S3]. Raphael should have room to run. Cal's defense also allows 42.4% on third down (107th) [S3].
Their offense vs. our defense: Cal throws on about 61% of its plays [S2] for 288.1 yards a game (15th) [S3]. QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has 1,290 yards [S3]. Our pass defense ranks 11th [S3]. That's the matchup. And Cal's offense has been held to 10 points or fewer in two of its last four games [S2]. Our pass rush, with 18 sacks, will want to make it three [S2]. Cal's sideline outfits? I'll review those live, sugar.
Series: a full series record wasn't in a free source I could verify.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our pass defense keep Cal's passing game quiet? (2) Can Raphael take advantage of Cal's run defense? (3) Red zone. Touchdowns, not field goals, sugar.
And to Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, Cal's insider: I adore your picket signs, darling. Very handmade. We'll have them laminated for you.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching near campus? Kuby's Sausage House in Snider Plaza is a University Park classic.

report.title: "A Foot of Snow of a Take": Nico Calabrese Heads South to Chapel Hill
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

That's a foot of snow of a take. Hey, how ya doin', I'm Nico Calabrese, born and raised in the Salt City, survivor of more lake-effect winters than I can count. I travel with the Orange and I live with the Orange, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with full upstate bluster. My scale for every play is feet of snow. A two-yard run? A dusting. A long touchdown? Twenty inches overnight, school's canceled. A turnover by us? That's the plow truck sliding into the ditch. When we win, I'll yell "That's a foot of snow of a WIN!" so loud they'll hear me in Utica. When we lose, I shrug: "Just a lake-effect squall." Then I grab a salt potato and get back to work. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Syracuse plays in the ACC, and here's a fact I love: it's the only FBS school in New York in a Power Four conference [S6]. Home is the JMA Wireless Dome on campus, also known as "The Loud House" [S6], opened in 1980 and listed at 49,057 seats [S2]. The last five seasons: 5-7, 7-6, 6-7, a big 10-3 in 2024 and 3-9 last year [S2]. That 10-3 year? That was the Blizzard of '93, the one we still talk about.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Fran Brown is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2023 [S2]. This offense throws it: 291 passing yards a game, 12th in FBS, and 449.7 total yards (29th) [S5]. We hold the ball 33:59 a game, 5th in FBS [S5]. The defense is solid against the pass, 191.8 yards allowed (43rd) [S5], with 15 sacks [S2]. The problem? Penalties. We average 98 penalty yards a game, 138th in the country [S5]. That's driving the Thruway in a whiteout with the brakes on. And in the red zone we score on 78.1% of trips, 111th [S5]. Clean those two up and this is a different team.

4. Players to Know

• WR Umari Hatcher: 50 catches, 784 yards, 7 TD [S4][S5]. Against Louisville he caught 13 passes for 224 yards and a touchdown [S5]. That's three feet overnight, folks. Lake Ontario is jealous.
• QB Malachi Nelson: threw for 315 yards and two touchdowns, with two interceptions, against Louisville [S5]. The local paper's headline says he left that game with another injury [S11].
• QB Steve Angeli: the season passing leader, 57 of 104, 731 yards, 4 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. He was out for the Louisville game [S10].
• RB Tylik Hill: 431 yards on 80 carries [S4][S5]. RB Ahmad Miller: 123 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries against Louisville [S5].
• LB Chris D'Appolonia: team-high 42 tackles [S4]. LB Keyshawn Johnson: 4 sacks [S4]. DB Davien Kerr: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Syracuse is 2-4 and 0-4 in the ACC [S2]. We beat New Hampshire 66-3 and won a 42-41 thriller at UConn [S2]. The four league losses: California 21-18, at Pittsburgh 27-13, at Virginia 28-25 and Louisville 34-26 [S2]. Three of those were one-score games [S2]. After Chapel Hill, No. 23 SMU comes to the Dome on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math today. I'm just saying this team has been close, real close.
The close ones: a field goal against Cal, a field goal at Virginia, one score against Louisville [S2]. That's a whole winter of near-misses on the plow route.
Why I love this team anyway: because it keeps moving the ball no matter who's under center. Hatcher is on pace for a monster year [S4]. Miller ran hard last week [S5]. And the team that went 10-3 two years ago had a coach named Fran Brown too [S2]. Upstate folks don't quit when it snows. We shovel out, and we go to work.

6. This Week: Syracuse (2-4) at North Carolina (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill · ACC Network [S1][S5][S8].
The quarterback question: I can't tell you who starts. The ACC hasn't posted a Week 8 availability report yet [S10]. Angeli was out last week, Nelson played and then, per the local paper's headline, left with another injury [S10][S11]. I'll update you when the report comes out. I won't guess.
Our offense vs. their defense: North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.3% of third downs (113th) [S5], and its pass defense is 69th [S5]. Hatcher should get his chances. But the Tar Heels' red zone defense ranks 22nd [S5], and that's where we've struggled.
Their offense vs. our defense: North Carolina averages 329.7 yards a game (117th) and 116.2 rushing yards (120th) [S5]. Jordan Shipp leads them with 441 receiving yards [S5]. Our defense can win this matchup.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
What decides it: (1) Who's healthy at quarterback. (2) Penalties; they average 33.7 penalty yards a game (5th), we average 98 [S5]. (3) Red zone finishing.
To Ainsley Pemberton, North Carolina's insider: Carolina blue is nice, but have you ever seen a snowbank shaped like a block S? Come visit in February.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back home? Varsity Pizza on South Crouse Avenue has been feeding Orange fans on the hill for a long time. Get a slice.

report.title: "Surf's Up on Tempo, Babe": Kaia Brightwater Welcomes Rice to Boca
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hey, Owls, welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Kaia Brightwater, your Florida Atlantic insider. I used to play beach volleyball here in Boca Raton, and now I analyze offenses like swell reports. Choppy means three-and-outs. Clean means long, smooth drives. And a closeout? That's when the whole wave crashes at once, which is how a defense feels when we go tempo. I travel with this team and I live with this team. The beachy talk is real, but so is the analysis underneath it, I promise. When we win, it's "a perfect swell day" and a slow-motion hair flip. When we lose, I sigh "flat water" and post a sunset anyway, because it's still Boca. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, sun and stats. "Surf's up on tempo, babe." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Florida Atlantic football is young, and it was built by a legend. Howard Schnellenberger founded the program from scratch and served as its first head coach [S8]. Home is FAU Stadium in Boca Raton, listed at 29,419 [S2], close enough to the Atlantic to smell the salt on a breezy Saturday. The Owls play in the American Athletic Conference [S2], and the series with Rice is as even as a glassy morning: 3-3 [S3]. The recent history is a lot of close finishes: FAU won 27-21 in 2025 and 17-14 in 2022, and Rice won 24-21 in 2023 [S3]. Back in 2016, FAU won 42-25 [S3]. I love a program that's still writing its story.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Zach Kittley was named the Hagerty Family Head Football Coach on Dec. 2, 2024 [S9]. The 2026 numbers say this offense is all about the air. FAU throws for 307.3 yards a game with 15 passing touchdowns [S2]. It averages 35.0 points and 422.3 yards a game [S2]. The run game is choppier, at 3.29 yards a carry [S2]. On defense, the waves are bigger than I'd like. FAU allows 31.5 points a game and 5.43 yards a carry [S2]. On the bright side, the Owls have forced eight turnovers and lost six [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Caden Veltkamp: 1,743 yards and 15 TD [S3]. At Army he went 33 of 48 for 318 yards and three touchdowns [S3]. That's a clean swell, and the kind of day I want every Saturday.
• WR Kelby Valsin: 47 catches, 601 yards and 6 TD [S3], including 7 catches, 89 yards and a touchdown at Army [S3].
• LB Joseph Sipp Jr.: a team-high 41 tackles and a sack [S3].
I couldn't verify other season leaders from a free source, so I'm keeping the list short and accurate.

5. The Conference Picture

Florida Atlantic is 4-2 overall and 1-1 in the American, 3-0 at home and 1-2 on the road [S2]. The Owls aren't ranked [S2]. The wins came against Navy (38-30), FIU (16-10), UL Monroe and Texas Southern, and the losses were at Florida and at Army [S2]. Staying perfect at home keeps FAU in the conference mix. At home the Owls are outscoring opponents 120-50 [S2], which is my kind of clean, glassy water. On the road it's been choppier, with 66 points allowed at Florida and 56 at Army [S2]. Good news, babe: this one's at home.

6. This Week: Rice (1-6) at Florida Atlantic (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · FAU Stadium · ESPNU [S3][S1]. Surf report: 81 degrees, a 52% chance of showers and storms, and a 20 mph northeast wind [S3]. Choppy, babe.
Last week: FAU lost 56-24 at Army [S2]. Rice lost 38-17 at home to Tulsa [S2].
Our offense vs. their defense: Rice allows 29.0 points a game and 188.7 passing yards [S2]. Veltkamp and Valsin should find room, as long as the wind cooperates.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the wave to watch. Rice runs on 79% of its plays [S2], and QB Jacurri Brown has 668 rushing yards [S3], including 154 against Tulsa [S3]. Our run defense allows 5.43 a carry [S2], and Army just ran all over us. Everyone has to stay in their lane. One positive: Rice has lost 10 turnovers and forced just 4 [S2], and its passing game averages only 78.7 yards a game [S2]. So if our front gets Rice behind schedule, that's when the closeout wave comes.
Series: tied 3-3. FAU won the last meeting, 27-21 in 2025 [S3].
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 8 sacks and has allowed 11, with 8 takeaways against 6 giveaways, and it has 8 rushing and 15 passing touchdowns [S2].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our defense stop a run-heavy offense one week after Army scored 56? (2) Can Veltkamp handle the wind? (3) Tempo. If we go fast and stay clean, it's a perfect swell day.
And to Odalys Chen-Moreau, Rice's insider: love a fellow Owl! Bring your clipboard and some sunscreen.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching in Boca? Max's Grill on Plaza Real for a post-game dinner, sunset optional but recommended.

report.title: "Steady as She Goes": Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather Welcomes the Mean Green to Annapolis
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Good afternoon, and welcome aboard The Cover Window. I'm Commander Annabel Merriweather, retired, your Navy insider. I spent my career as a surface warfare officer, and I read an option play the way I read a nautical chart: depth, current and where the rocks are hiding. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I speak in nautical terms, and I cannot be stopped. When we win, I say, "Anchors aweigh!" and ring a ship's bell. When we lose, I say, "Steady as she goes," and plot a new course. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with crisp navigation. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Navy plays at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, listed at 34,000 [S2]. Last season was a fine voyage. Navy went 11-2 and 7-1 in the American, won the Liberty Bowl 35-13 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll [S7]. The Midshipmen also won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy for the second straight season, beating Air Force 34-31 and Army 17-16 [S8]. The win over Army came on a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass [S8]. Anchors aweigh. Navy has now beaten Army in back-to-back seasons [S8], and in Annapolis that's the voyage everyone remembers.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Brian Newberry was hired on Dec. 19, 2022 [S2]. The scheme is the option, and it's the fleet's pride. Navy runs on 81% of its plays, for 297.8 yards a game, 4th in FBS, at 5.74 yards a carry [S2][S3]. That's 17 rushing touchdowns [S2]. The passing game is used sparingly, at 115.5 yards a game, but it hits big: Jordan Collins has 189 yards on just five catches [S3]. On defense, Navy allows only 98.8 rushing yards a game (21st) and 2.73 yards a carry [S3][S2]. The pass defense allows 247.7 yards (113th) [S3]. The ship has a leak, too: Navy is minus-6 in turnovers (126th), with 9 lost and 3 forced [S3][S2]. That needs patching. The pass rush has 14 sacks, and the blockers have allowed only 9 [S2], which is fine seamanship for an option team that rarely drops back. We are disciplined, at 45 penalty yards a game (24th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Jackson Gutierrez (No. 8): our captain. He has 640 rushing yards and 9 TD on 123 carries, plus 559 passing yards, 6 TD and 1 INT [S3]. At UTSA he ran 21 times for 139 yards and two TDs and threw two TD passes [S3]. Against Tulsa, he ran for 232 yards and three scores [S4].
• QB Braxton Woodson (No. 5): 73 yards and a touchdown on five carries at UTSA [S3].
• WR Jordan Collins: two catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns at UTSA [S3].
• LB Coleman Cauley (No. 58): 41 tackles and a sack [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Navy is 2-4 overall and 1-3 in the American, 2-0 at home and 0-4 on the road [S2]. The losses were all on the road and close: 38-30 at Florida Atlantic, 24-20 at UAB, 14-9 at Air Force and 38-34 at UTSA [S2]. That's four losses by a combined 21 points. The wins were at home, over Towson 42-15 and Tulsa 34-26 [S2]. Good news, then: we're home this week. Steady as she goes. Notre Dame is next [S3], so this one matters before the schedule gets heavier.

6. This Week: North Texas (4-2) at Navy (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium · CBS Sports Network [S3][S4].
Last week: Navy lost 38-34 at UTSA [S3]. North Texas had a week off after beating Charlotte 50-10 on Oct. 10 [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: North Texas allows 142.7 rushing yards a game (73rd) and 29.2 points (113th) [S3]. That's open water for the option.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the storm. North Texas averages 42.2 points (5th in FBS) and 347 passing yards (2nd) [S3]. QB Tayven Jackson has 1,868 yards and 15 TDs [S3]. Our pass defense ranks 113th [S3]. The best defense may be our offense, keeping the ball and keeping their quarterback on the sideline.
Series: North Texas won last year 31-17, but Navy leads 2-1 [S4]. Navy won the 2007 meeting 74-62 [S4], which I consider a historical anomaly. In 2023, a closer contest: Navy 27, North Texas 24 [S4]. That's the course I'd like to chart again, a tight game decided late, at home, in front of the Brigade.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Ball security. We are minus-6 [S3], and we can't give this offense extra trips. (2) Third downs. North Texas converts 48.8% (21st), and our defense ranks 121st [S3]. (3) Time of possession. North Texas averages 33 minutes a game [S3], so we'll have to take the clock back.

report.title: "That Offense Is in 7/8 Time": Grady Mayhew-Ochoa Takes the Mean Green to Annapolis
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Mean Green, baby! Welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, your North Texas insider, coming at you from Denton, a town with more music going on per square block than just about anywhere in Texas. I'm a sports nerd and an indie-rock nerd, and I hear football the way I hear a record. Every offense has a tempo. Some are steady four-on-the-floor. Ours? Ours is in 7/8 time, and the defense keeps counting wrong. I travel with this team and I live with this team, headphones on. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with liner notes. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

North Texas plays at DATCU Stadium in Denton, listed at 30,850 [S2]. Last year was a record-breaking season, and the Mean Green were ranked No. 20 in the country when the coaching change was announced [S6]. Eric Morris left for Oklahoma State, and Neal Brown took over [S6]. The headline single this season: an offense that ranks among the best in the country. North Texas averages 42.2 points a game, 5th in FBS, and 533.8 yards, 3rd [S3]. Mean Green, baby. And the defense has 14 sacks and 9 takeaways [S2]. We're plus-2 in turnover margin (47th) [S3].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Neal Brown was named the 21st head coach in North Texas history on Dec. 2, 2025 [S5][S2]. He had 10 seasons as an FBS head coach at Troy and West Virginia and went 72-51 [S5]. At Troy he won the 2017 Sun Belt title and was the conference's Coach of the Year, and his 2016-18 teams went 31-8 [S5]. His 2023 West Virginia team went 9-4 [S5]. He's 5-1 in bowl games [S5]. The sound in 2026 is balanced: about 50% runs, 347 passing yards a game (2nd in FBS) and 186.8 rushing yards (41st) [S2][S3]. That's 17 passing touchdowns and 14 rushing [S2]. The blockers have allowed only 5 sacks [S2], and North Texas converts 48.8% of third downs (21st) [S3]. The red-zone offense scores on 93.9% of trips (16th) [S3]. And we hold the ball an average of 33 minutes a game, 17th in FBS [S3]. That's a long song. The defense allows 29.2 points (113th) [S3], so the B-side needs work.

4. Players to Know

• QB Tayven Jackson (No. 2): 1,868 yards, 15 TD, 4 INT, 72.2% completions [S3], third in FBS in passing yards [S4]. Against Charlotte he went 24 of 31 for 349 yards and five touchdowns [S3]. Headliner.
• RB Jahiem White (No. 1): 687 yards and 9 TD on 96 carries [S3], sixth in FBS in rushing touchdowns [S4]. He had 105 yards and a touchdown against Charlotte, plus two catches for 37 yards [S3].
• WR Justin Stevenson: 33 catches, 453 yards, 5 TD [S3]. Against Charlotte he caught nine for 122 yards and two scores [S3].
• LB Zakye Barker (No. 3): 43 tackles and 2 sacks [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

report.title: "N Equals Too Small": Odalys Chen-Moreau Takes the Owls to Boca
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hello, Owl family, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Odalys Chen-Moreau, your Rice insider. I'm finishing a bioengineering PhD, and I model football like a clinical trial: control group, treatment group and a very long methods section. I travel with this team and I live with this team. You should also know I'm basically a stats cop with a badge. If someone makes a sweeping claim off two games, I will walk over, flash the badge and say, "N equals too small." When we win, I shout "Statistically significant!" and do a dance worthy of any halftime show. When we lose, I say "N is too small to panic"... and then I panic quietly in the lab. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, peer-reviewed. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Rice Stadium is one of the most historic venues in American sports. On Sept. 12, 1962, President John F. Kennedy stood there and gave his speech recommitting the country to landing on the moon [S5]. On Jan. 13, 1974, the stadium hosted Super Bowl VIII, when Miami beat Minnesota 24-7 [S6]. It's listed at 47,000 seats [S2]. Rice is a small private school playing big-time football in the American Athletic Conference [S2], and that's a story worth telling every single week. Our hypothesis is that grit travels well. Let's test it.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Scott Abell was named head coach on Nov. 26, 2024, after seven seasons at Davidson [S7]. The data are very clear on what this offense is. Rice runs on about 79% of its plays, gains 4.87 yards a carry and has 13 rushing touchdowns, against just 2 through the air [S2]. That's not a small sample. That's a whole identity. The challenges are just as clear: Rice averages 17.0 points and 318.6 yards a game and allows 29.0 points [S2]. Turnovers have hurt, with 10 lost against 4 forced [S2]. The defense has 10 sacks [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Jacurri Brown: 668 rushing yards and 6 TD on the ground, plus 471 passing yards and 2 TD [S3]. Against Tulsa he ran 11 times for 154 yards and two touchdowns [S3]. Statistically significant? I'd say so.
• RB Tyvonn Byars: 372 yards and 2 TD [S3].
• DE A.J. Brown: a team-high 52 tackles, which is a lot for a defensive end [S3].
Season leaders past these three were not in a free source I could verify, so I'm not listing more names.

5. The Conference Picture

Rice is 1-6 overall and 0-3 in the American, 1-3 at home and 0-3 on the road [S2]. Several of those losses were close: 16-14 to UTSA and 28-21 to Western Michigan, both at home [S2]. The goal now is to grow week by week. Yes, the record is the record. But I'd still call the season an incomplete dataset. The run game is real: 4.87 yards a carry is nearly identical to what our defense allows (4.88) [S2]. Our pass rush has 10 sacks, and we've given up 13 [S2]. The variable to watch is ball security.

6. This Week: Rice (1-6) at Florida Atlantic (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · FAU Stadium, Boca Raton · ESPNU [S3][S1]. The forecast calls for 81 degrees, a 52% chance of rain and a 20 mph wind out of the northeast [S3]. For a team that runs 79% of the time, that's not the worst news.
Last week: Rice lost 38-17 to Tulsa at home [S2], with Brown running for 154 yards [S3]. Florida Atlantic lost 56-24 at Army [S2].
Our offense vs. their defense: here's a promising variable. Florida Atlantic allows 5.43 yards a carry and 31.5 points a game [S2]. Army just ran up 56 points on them [S2].
Their offense vs. our defense: FAU throws for 307.3 yards a game [S2]. QB Caden Veltkamp has 1,743 yards and 15 touchdowns, and WR Kelby Valsin has 47 catches for 601 yards [S3]. Our pass defense allows 188.7 yards a game [S2], but FAU will test it constantly.
Series: tied 3-3. FAU won the last meeting, 27-21 in 2025, and Rice won in 2023, 24-21 [S3]. Most of these games come down to a handful of points: five of the six were decided by six or fewer, including Rice's wins of 27-26 in 2015 and 18-14 in 2013 [S3]. That's a consistent effect across six trials.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our run game control the clock the way Army's did? (2) Can we win the turnover battle for once? We're minus-6 [S2]. (3) Can we keep Veltkamp from hitting big plays to Valsin?

report.title: "Roll Wave!": Twan Ducros-Labat Parades Into Week 8
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Roll Wave! Hey now, I'm Antoine Ducros-Labat, but all Uptown calls me Twan. I've lived within earshot of a brass band my whole life, and I believe every football game is a brass-band parade: you dance your way through it, no matter what. I travel with the Green Wave and I live with the Green Wave, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little music and a lot of food. You'll hear me say a big play "deserved a beignet." I mean that literally. I keep a bag of them in the booth. Uptown on game day, there's a brass band on every corner and a Green Wave flag on every porch. When we win, the parade rolls all night. When we lose, we still dance home. Roll Wave, and save me a beignet. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Green Wave represent Tulane University and compete in the American Conference [S7]. Home is Yulman Stadium on campus in Uptown New Orleans [S7], opened in 2014 and listed at 30,000 seats [S3]. And the music lately has been sweet: after 2-10 in 2021, Tulane went 12-2, 11-3, 9-5 and 11-3 [S3]. That's four straight years of brass band, y'all.

The calling card of this defense is the red zone: opponents score on just 65.4% of their trips inside our 20, 5th in FBS [S5]. We allow 21.7 points a game, 50th [S5], and we have 12 sacks [S3]. That's a defense that bends like a trombone slide but doesn't break. The trouble spots: we allow 212.5 rushing yards a game (133rd) [S5], and opponents convert 45.6% of third downs (124th) [S5]. On offense, we gain 332 yards (116th) and score 20.5 points (117th) [S5]. We've turned it over just 5 times [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB: Kadin Semonza leads the team with 64 of 119 for 804 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT [S4][S5]. Trace Johnson started against Memphis and threw for 165 yards and a touchdown [S5]. Who starts this week? I haven't seen it announced [S9].

5. The Conference Picture

Tulane is 3-3 and 1-1 in the American, 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road [S3]. The home wins: South Alabama 28-24, Southern Miss 24-21 and Memphis 31-17 [S3]. The road losses: at Duke 17-3, at Kansas State 31-20 and a 20-17 heartbreaker at Army [S3]. After UTSA, we go to Charlotte on Oct. 30 [S5]. No standings math in the booth tonight. I'll just say Yulman's been our happy place, and this week we're home.
Home sweet home: three games at Yulman, three wins [S3]. The brass band knows the way.
Season so far: the Army loss was by a field goal [S3]. The Southern Miss win was by a field goal [S3]. This team lives in close games, and close games at Yulman have gone our way. When the Memphis game was over, I swear the whole neighborhood was dancing. That's what this team does for Uptown. A good brass band doesn't play the same song twice, and neither does this team. One week it's the defense, the next week it's Turner breaking a long one. Somebody always steps up to lead the parade.

6. This Week: UTSA (6-1) at Tulane (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 8 p.m. ET (7 p.m. Central) · Yulman Stadium, New Orleans · ESPNU [S1][S5][S8].

Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with aloha. "Island time, but on schedule." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Here's the time-zone math for Saturday: kickoff is 3:30 p.m. Eastern [S3], which is 2:30 p.m. in DeKalb and 9:30 in the morning back home in Honolulu. Set your alarm, make the coffee strong, and grab a malasada. Home for us is the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, listed at 15,194 [S2]. Last season was a big wave. Hawai'i went 9-4, opened the season by beating Stanford, and won the Hawai'i Bowl over Cal after coming back from 21 points down, tying the biggest comeback in program history [S5]. It was our first bowl bid since 2021 [S5]. This season the surf's been flat, but the swell can turn fast.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Timmy Chang was named Hawai'i's 25th head coach on Jan. 22, 2022 [S5][S2]. Before that, he was a Hawai'i legend. As our quarterback from 2000 to 2004, he set the NCAA career records for passing yards (17,072) and total offense, and he won a program-record 29 games as a starter [S5]. He was also a two-time Hawai'i Bowl Most Outstanding Player and a finalist for the Johnny Unitas Award as a senior [S5]. Before all that he was a record-setting quarterback at Honolulu's Saint Louis School [S5]. Local boy. He coached at Nevada, Jackson State, Emory & Henry and SMU before coming home [S5]. In 2025 he was the AFCA Region 5 Coach of the Year [S5]. In 2026 we're a passing team: we run on only about 36% of plays [S2], and we throw for 268 yards a game, 32nd in FBS [S3]. The run game is the problem, at 77.4 yards a game (138th) [S3]. And our blockers have allowed 20 sacks [S2]. The defense holds up against the pass, allowing 202.1 yards a game (60th) [S3], but allows 182.3 rushing yards (112th) [S3].

5. The Conference Picture

We're 1-6 overall and 0-4 in the Mountain West, 1-3 at home and 0-3 on the road [S2]. The win: 29-19 over New Mexico State [S2]. The losses: at Stanford 37-27, UNLV, at Wyoming, San José State 20-16 (close!), at Arizona State and New Mexico 21-10 last week [S2]. Six losses, but several close ones. Next wave. For the season we have 7 passing touchdowns and 4 rushing, with 10 sacks on defense, 6 takeaways and 8 giveaways [S2]. Scoring is the big job: 15.7 points a game, 133rd [S3]. Bring the board wax.

report.title: "Send It": Ridge Corbell Celebrates 130 Years of Wolf Pack Football
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Send it! What's up, Wolf Pack, I'm Ridge Corbell. I ski patrol at Tahoe in the winter, I scout football on a snowboard (figuratively, mostly), and I've discovered that snowboard slang explains advanced football stats better than anything on a whiteboard. Third-down conversion rate? That's just how often you land the jump. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, chill on the outside and surprisingly sharp with the math underneath. When we win, you'll hear "Sick!" and I'll mime a backflip. When we lose, I'll shrug and call it a powder day that went sideways, and then I'll dig into the film. Strap in. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Nevada football was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers [S7]. Check the calendar, friends: Saturday is the program's 130th birthday [S7]. We play at Mackay Stadium on the north end of campus [S7]. The "new" Mackay opened Oct. 1, 1966, seats 27,000, and its field sits 4,610 feet above sea level [S7][S3]. Coach Chris Ault, running back Frank Hawkins and coach Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame, and fullback Marion Motley is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame [S7]. We compete in the Mountain West [S7]. Recent years have been a climb: 8-5 in 2021, then 2-10, 2-10, 3-10 and 3-9 [S3]. Every run starts at the top of the hill.
The trail so far in 2026: we opened with a 49-14 rout of Western Kentucky that was pure fresh powder [S3]. Then Montana State, an FCS power, beat us 20-7 at home, and we lost close ones at Middle Tennessee (27-20) and to Air Force (36-33) [S3]. A 30-13 win at UTEP got us back on the board in league play [S3]. Last week in Fargo we led 11-0 before the special-teams avalanche [S9]. Add it up and this team is closer than its record. Two of the four losses were one-score games, and we led last week's game in the second quarter [S3][S9]. Close is not the same as sending it, but it's the slope right before.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jeff Choate was hired Dec. 4, 2023 [S3]. The 2026 Wolf Pack carve on the ground: 192.8 rushing yards a game, 37th in FBS [S5], 1,140 yards on 218 carries, about 5.2 a carry [S3]. The passing game is lighter, 171.8 yards a game (122nd) [S5]. The defense has a sick pass coverage number, 155.3 yards allowed a game, 7th in FBS, and holds opponents to 32.6% on third down (29th) [S5]. The wipeouts: run defense, 184.3 allowed a game (116th), red zone defense, 94.4% scoring allowed (127th), and turnover margin, minus-8 (134th) [S5]. We've lost 11 turnovers and forced just 3 [S3]. That's the run we need to clean up.

4. Players to Know

• RB Dominic Kelley: 500 yards on 87 carries, 4 TD [S4][S5].
• QB Carter Jones: 53 of 89, 654 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT [S4][S5].
• QB A.J. Bianco: played at North Dakota State, 17 of 34 for 190 yards, a touchdown pass and a rushing touchdown, with two interceptions [S5][S9]. Saturday's starter has not been announced in anything I found as of Oct. 18 [S10].
• WR Gary Givens III: 15 catches, 260 yards, 1 TD [S4][S5]. He caught a 19-yard touchdown at NDSU [S9].
• LB EJ Smith: a team-high 71 tackles [S4]. Myles Williams: 2.5 sacks [S4]. DB Bryson Snelling: an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Nevada is 2-4 overall and 1-2 in the Mountain West [S3]. The wins: Western Kentucky 49-14 and at UTEP 30-13 [S3]. The losses: Montana State 20-7, at Middle Tennessee 27-20, Air Force 36-33 and at North Dakota State 31-17 [S3]. Two of those four losses were one-score games [S3]. After this, it's a trip to UCLA on Oct. 31 [S5]. A home league win would be the cleanest run we've had all year.

6. This Week: San José State (4-3) at Nevada (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Mackay Stadium · MW+ [S1][S5][S8]. Happy 130th, Wolf Pack [S7].
Last week: we led 11-0 early at North Dakota State and lost 31-17 [S9]. A 57-yard field goal try came up short and was returned 100 yards for a touchdown, and a trick play on a two-point try was fumbled and returned for two Bison points [S9]. San José State beat UTEP 24-11 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: SJSU allows 240.9 passing yards (111th) and 148.3 rushing (83rd) [S5]. Its pass rush has 27 sacks [S2], so protection is the whole run.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Spartans convert 34.4% of third downs (111th) [S5]. Our third-down defense, 29th, should land that jump [S5]. Jabari Bates has 556 rushing yards, and our run defense has to hold [S5].
Series: we won five of nine meetings from 2016 through 2025 [S3].
Availability: no injury or availability report found as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Turnovers: we can't keep giving the ball away. (2) Red zone defense. (3) Kelley and the run game against an 83rd-ranked run defense [S5].
And Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, SJSU's insider: welcome to altitude. I'll lend you a beanie.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

I'll keep the Reno tips to the mountains this week: take the family up to Tahoe for the leaves after the game.

report.title: "Red or Green? Both.": Paloma Begaye-Ortiz Welcomes the Bison to Albuquerque
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Red or green? Both. ¡Hola, Albuquerque! I'm Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, and when I'm not at a Lobos game, I'm floating a hot-air balloon over the Rio Grande at sunrise. Every October I fly in the Balloon Fiesta, and every Saturday I read Lobo football like wind currents: where it's drifting, where it's rising, and when it's about to soar. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with some green-chile spice and a balloon metaphor for every drive. That offense floated like a balloon at dawn, up and up. When we win, I yell, "Red or green? BOTH!" and pump my fist. When we lose, I sigh, "Too much heat today." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The New Mexico Lobos compete in the Mountain West [S7]. Our colors are cherry and silver [S7]. Home is University Stadium in Albuquerque [S7], opened in 1960 and listed at 39,224 seats [S3]. The last five years started low: 3-9, 2-10, 4-8, then 5-7 and a big 9-4 in 2025 [S3]. That's a balloon catching a thermal, y'all. Up and up.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jason Eck is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 16, 2024 [S3]. And this defense is the brightest balloon in the sky. In six games, we've taken the ball away 21 times and given it away only 4 [S3]. That's plus-17! We have 19 sacks [S3]. By my math from the season totals, we allow about 10.5 points a game and about 92 rushing yards [S3][S12]. The offense runs the ball, 1,287 yards on 271 carries, and scores about 39.7 points a game [S3][S12]. The passing game is lighter, 978 yards [S3]. When the wind's right, though, we soar: 70 points against Mercyhurst and 61 against UTEP [S3].

4. Players to Know

• RB Scottre Humphrey: 422 yards on 85 carries, 8 TD [S4]. At Hawai'i he ran 15 times for 90 yards and two touchdowns [S9]. That's a balloon at full burn.
• QB Toa Fa'avae: 41 of 73 for about 700 yards (ESPN 698, CollegeFootballDigest 695), 5 TD, 3 INT [S4][S9]. At Hawai'i he ran 10 times for 77 yards and a touchdown [S9].
• WR Bailen George: 12 catches, 240 yards, 3 TD [S4].
• S Tavian Combs: 4 interceptions [S4]. DE Darren Agu: 4 sacks [S4]. LB Mercury Swaim: team-high 32 tackles and 1.5 sacks [S4][S9].

5. The Conference Picture

New Mexico is 5-1 and 2-0 in the Mountain West [S3]. We beat Central Michigan 38-7, Mercyhurst 70-7, New Mexico State 42-18 on the road, UTEP 61-7 and Hawai'i 21-10 on the road [S3]. The one loss: a 14-6 fight at Oklahoma [S3]. We had a week off before Hawai'i [S3]. After the Bison, we head to San José State on Oct. 31 [S9]. No standings math in the basket, y'all. Just know an unbeaten league record is a beautiful view from up here.
About Oklahoma: an SEC team, on the road, and we held them to 14 points [S3]. That's a balloon that didn't drop an inch in a strong wind.
Season so far, from the basket: it's been a sunrise flight, y'all. Five wins, all five by 11 points or more [S3]. When the wind is with you, you just enjoy the view. The defense has allowed 63 points in six games, total [S3]. The Hawai'i trip was a long flight over the Pacific, and we landed it, 21-10 [S3]. Every pilot knows the hardest part is the landing. This team keeps sticking them. And last year's 9-4 team taught this group how to win. Now they're doing it with even more style.

6. This Week: North Dakota State (6-1) at New Mexico (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 10 p.m. ET (8 p.m. Mountain) · University Stadium, Albuquerque · The CW [S1][S8][S9]. Forecast: 58 degrees, slight chance of showers [S9]. Bring a jacket, and green chile to keep you warm.
History: this is the first meeting on record [S9]. A whole new sky.
Their offense vs. our defense: North Dakota State QB Nathan Hayes has 1,272 passing yards and 10 TD [S4]. Receiver Jackson Williams just returned a missed field goal 100 yards for a touchdown against Nevada [S10]. Special teams, y'all. Watch the kicks.
Our offense vs. their defense: the Bison allow about 11.3 points a game by my math and have pitched two shutouts [S2][S12]. They're plus-8 in turnovers [S2]. This is a real defense, and the Bison have 10 FCS national titles since 2011 to prove they know how to win [S6].
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Our turnover magic against a careful Bison offense. (2) Humphrey and the run game. (3) Special teams, especially containing Williams on returns.
To Inga Halvorsen, North Dakota State's insider: hotdish? Hon, I'll trade you a tray of green-chile enchiladas. Christmas style.

Why I Love This Team

I love a defense with 21 takeaways in six games [S3]. I love Humphrey's eight touchdowns [S4]. I love that the Lobos are climbing [S3]. And I love Albuquerque on a fall night, when the balloons are put away and the stadium lights come up. Red or green? Both.

report.title: "Oh for Cute": Inga Halvorsen Brings Hotdish to Albuquerque
report.byline: Ingeborg 'Inga' Halvorsen · North Dakota State Insider
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Oh for cute, they think they can run on us. Well, hi there, I'm Ingeborg Halvorsen, Inga to pretty much all of Fargo. I'm an agricultural economist by trade, and I've tracked every Bison championship since I was a girl with a notebook in the Fargodome stands. These days I keep a little model on my laptop about how a team moves from the FCS to the FBS, and so far, the Bison are making it look easy. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, nice as can be, until it's time not to be. When we win, I say, "Oh, for cute, we won!" When we lose, I say, "Oh, yah, that's a tough one," and I bring hotdish. Truth be told, I bring hotdish either way. Tater tot, of course. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Bison represent North Dakota State and now play in the FBS as members of the Mountain West [S2][S6]. Home is the Fargodome, 18,700 seats [S6], opened in 1992 [S2]. And the trophy case, oh my. The Bison have won 18 national championships, none in their current division, and 39 conference championships [S6]. That includes 10 FCS national titles between 2011 and 2024 [S6]. The last five seasons in the Missouri Valley went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1 [S2]. Yah, we're used to winning around here.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Tim Polasek is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 17, 2023 [S2]. This team plays Bison football: run it, defend it, don't give it away. By my math from the season totals, we score about 29.4 points a game and allow about 11.3 [S2][S12]. We've run it 287 times for 1,223 yards and thrown for 1,311 [S2]. Opponents average about 112 rushing yards a game against us [S2][S12]. We've taken the ball away 14 times and given it away 6 [S2]. That's plus-8, which in my model is "very good." And we have 12 sacks [S2]. Two shutouts, too: Fordham 38-0 and Wyoming 28-0 [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Nathan Hayes: 106 of 163 for 1,272 yards, 10 TD, 5 INT [S4][S9]. Against Nevada he went 19 of 25 for 153 yards and accounted for three touchdowns [S10].
• WR Jackson Williams: 28 catches, 432 yards, 1 TD [S4][S9]. And oh, for cute: against Nevada he caught a missed 57-yard field-goal try in the end zone and ran it back 100 yards for a touchdown [S10]. He also ran for a score and threw a touchdown pass [S10]. That young man deserves extra hotdish.
• RB Myles Mitchell: 354 yards on 81 carries, 3 TD [S4].
• LB Donovan Woolen: team-high 51 tackles, 1.5 sacks and an interception [S4][S9]. DE Kelton McCaslin: 4 sacks [S4]. CB Marion Moore: 4 interceptions [S4].
• Matthew Stenbroten returned a fumbled 2-point try for two points against Nevada [S10].

5. The Conference Picture

North Dakota State is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Mountain West [S2]. We beat Jacksonville State 33-7, Fordham 38-0, Air Force 38-32 on the road, Sacramento State 31-10 on the road, Wyoming 28-0 and Nevada 31-17 [S2]. The one loss: 13-7 at UNLV [S2]. After Albuquerque, we host UTEP on Oct. 31 [S9]. I won't do standings math, but my model is very pleased.
About that UNLV game: a six-point loss on the road [S2]. "Oh, yah, that's a tough one." I brought hotdish. Then the team bounced back against Nevada [S10].
Season so far, by the numbers I love: our defense has allowed 79 points in seven games, total [S2]. Nevada jumped out to an 11-0 lead last week, and nobody panicked [S10]. Williams scored three different ways, and the defense held Nevada to 17 [S10]. That's the Bison way, hon: steady, patient and then, all of a sudden, the game is over. Like a North Dakota winter. You don't notice it coming, and then it's February.

6. This Week: North Dakota State (6-1) at New Mexico (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 10 p.m. ET (8 p.m. Mountain) · University Stadium, Albuquerque · The CW [S1][S8][S9]. Forecast: 58 degrees, slight chance of showers [S9]. Practically a heat wave for Fargo folks.
History: this is the first meeting on record [S9].
Their offense vs. our defense: New Mexico scores about 39.7 points a game by my math, with 1,287 rushing yards in six games [S3][S12]. Scottre Humphrey has 422 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns [S4]. Oh for cute, they think they can run on us. We'll see.
Our offense vs. their defense: here's the gut punch: New Mexico has 21 takeaways and only 4 giveaways in six games [S3]. It allows about 92 rushing yards a game and has 19 sacks [S3][S12]. Hayes has to protect the football.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Ball security against a defense that takes it away. (2) Stopping Humphrey. (3) Special teams; Williams just showed what they can do [S10].
To Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, New Mexico's insider: red or green? Oh, hon, I'm bringing tater tot hotdish. You'll love it.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back in Fargo? No Bull Smokehouse on Northern Pacific Avenue for barbecue, or Mezzaluna on Roberts Street for a nice dinner.

report.title: "Knee-High by the Fourth of July": Nola Brandvik Hosts Hawai'i in DeKalb
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hello, Huskies fans. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Nola Brandvik, your Northern Illinois insider. I studied agricultural science here in DeKalb, and I model the Huskies like a corn crop: planting, growing season, harvest. Nobody understands my measurements, but they trust them, and I appreciate that. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm calm. Very calm. Illinois calm. When we win, I say, "Knee-high by the Fourth of July," which means a great win. When we lose, I stare at a photo of a cornfield for 30 seconds. It helps. Truly, it does. Try it sometime. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, harvested fresh. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Northern Illinois plays at Huskie Stadium in DeKalb, listed at 23,595 [S2]. This is our first season in the Mountain West as a football-only member [S7][S6]. New field, new soil, same Huskies. The recent history is something to be proud of. Under Thomas Hammock, NIU won the 2021 MAC championship, won back-to-back bowl games and beat No. 5 Notre Dame in 2024, one of the biggest wins in school history [S6]. Hammock left in February 2026 to return to the NFL [S6]. And Saturday is our first-ever meeting with Hawai'i [S4]. They're traveling farther than anyone. We'll be polite about it. When he left, Hammock said that representing NIU as a player, alumnus, assistant and head coach was the honor of his life, and that he'll always cheer for the Huskies [S6]. He also called this an exciting time as the program enters the Mountain West [S6]. Hammock's teams earned three of what NIU calls "Boneyard Wins" over Power 4 opponents [S6]. That's the standard we're growing toward.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Rob Harley was our defensive coordinator, and he was promoted to interim head coach when Hammock resigned on Feb. 18, 2026 [S6][S2]. It's been a tough growing season. We're 0-6. The offense scores 14.2 points a game (137th) and runs for 101 yards a game (133rd) [S3]. The blockers have allowed 23 sacks [S2]. The defense allows 35.7 points (132nd) and 228.5 rushing yards a game (135th) [S3]. Opponents convert 61.6% of third downs, 138th in FBS [S3]. The good row in the field: the pass defense allows only 187 yards a game, 33rd in FBS [S3]. That's knee-high, at least. The passing game averages 206.7 yards a game (95th) [S3], with 4 passing and 5 rushing touchdowns [S2]. We've forced 6 turnovers and lost 7 [S2]. And we hold the ball 28:05 a game, 114th in FBS [S3]. Yields are low this year. Seasons change.

4. Players to Know

• RB Telly Johnson Jr.: 439 yards and 4 TD on 81 carries [S3]. At Wyoming he ran 16 times for 139 yards and a touchdown [S3]. Strong stalk. He's the best part of the crop right now.
• QB Taron Dickens: 1,193 yards, 4 TD, 3 INT, 65.8% completions [S3]. He threw for 216 yards and a touchdown at Wyoming [S3].
• WR DeAree Rogers: 49 catches, 422 yards, 2 TD [S3]. Eleven catches for 89 yards last week [S3].

5. The Conference Picture

We're 0-6 overall and 0-2 in the Mountain West, 0-2 at home and 0-4 on the road [S2]. The losses: at Iowa, Illinois State 28-24 (close), at Arizona, at Georgia State, Air Force and at Wyoming [S2]. This is our best chance yet for a first win. The field is ready. The weather is cooperating. I think. The Illinois State game was a four-point loss, 28-24 [S2], so we've been close before. Close is a seedling. Saturday we want a stalk.

6. This Week: Hawai'i (1-6) at Northern Illinois (0-6)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET (2:30 p.m. local) · Huskie Stadium · MW+ [S3][S1].
Last week: we lost 41-23 at Wyoming [S3]. Hawai'i lost 21-10 to New Mexico [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Hawai'i allows 182.3 rushing yards a game (112th) [S3]. Johnson should get a lot of carries. Hawai'i's red-zone defense ranks 93rd [S3].
Their offense vs. our defense: Hawai'i throws the ball a lot: about 64% passes [S2], 268 yards a game (32nd) [S3]. QB Micah Alejado has 1,862 yards [S3]. Our pass defense ranks 33rd [S3], so that's the matchup to watch. Hawai'i runs for only 77.4 yards a game (138th) [S3].
Series: first meeting [S4].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Red zone. We score on only 46.7% of trips (138th) [S3]. Must improve, and soon. (2) Third-down defense. (3) Pressure. Hawai'i has allowed 20 sacks [S2], and we have only 8 [S2].
And to Kainoa Akana-Baird, Hawai'i's insider: welcome to DeKalb. It's flat here. No waves. Lots of corn. You'll love it. Everyone does, eventually. Usually around harvest.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In DeKalb? French Toast Pancake House on South 4th Street, or Thai Pavillion on East Lincoln Highway.

report.title: "Ship It to Prod": Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz Launches Spartan Week in Reno
report.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz · San José State Insider
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Ship it to prod! Hi, Spartan Nation, I'm Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz. By day I'm a product lead at a tech company down the road, and by Saturday I run Spartan game tape like an A/B test: version A, version B, and which one moved the chains. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I treat every game week like a product launch, complete with a roadmap, a standup and a retro. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, explained in plain football language (I promise to keep the jargon in the sprint backlog). When we win, I yell "Ship it to prod!" and do a celebratory keyboard smash. When we lose, I sigh "rollback," open a bug ticket and get to work on the fix. Let's launch. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

San José State first played a regular season in 1898 [S6]. Since then the Spartans have produced more than 90 All-Americans, won 18 conference championships and sent 139 players to the NFL, including Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil [S6]. Home is CEFCU Stadium, built in 1933 as Spartan Stadium [S6], listed at 30,456 seats [S2]. Regional rivals include Fresno State, Stanford, Hawai'i and San Diego State [S6]. We play in the Mountain West [S6]. The last five years went 5-7, 7-5, 7-6, 7-6 and 3-9 [S2]. Release notes: version 2026 already has more wins than all of 2025 [S2].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Ken Niumatalolo is the head coach [S6], hired Jan. 21, 2024 [S2]. The 2026 build: an offense that throws for 246 yards a game (53rd) and runs for 138.7 (98th), averaging 21.4 points (111th) [S5]. The defense is the stable release. It allows 21.7 points a game, 50th in FBS [S5], and its pass rush has 27 sacks in seven games [S2]. That's a feature I'd demo to any investor. The defense does allow 240.9 passing yards a game (111th) [S5]. Two known bugs to patch: third downs, where we convert 34.4% (111th), and time of possession, 26:41 a game (135th) [S5]. We are clean, though, 47.3 penalty yards a game (31st) [S5]. Our turnover margin is exactly even, 0 [S5]. Balanced code.

4. Players to Know

• QB Luke Weaver: 132 of 209, 1,529 yards, 11 TD, 6 INT [S4][S5].
• QB Daniel Rolovich: led the offense at UTEP, 12 of 23 for 193 yards and a touchdown, plus 39 rushing yards [S5]. Who starts Saturday has not been announced in anything I could find as of Oct. 18 [S10].
• RB Jabari Bates: 556 yards on 120 carries, 1 TD [S4][S5]. Viliami Teu ran 20 times for 156 yards and two scores last week [S5].
• WR Carson Clark: 42 catches, 509 yards, 5 TD [S4][S5], with five catches for 104 and a touchdown against UTEP [S5].
• DL Jayland McGlothen: a team-high 6 sacks [S4]. LB Dylan Lee: 65 tackles [S4]. CB Caleb Womack: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

San José State is 4-3 overall and 2-1 in the Mountain West, and 3-1 away from home [S2]. The wins: at Eastern Michigan 27-21, Cal Poly 30-20, at Hawai'i 20-16 and at UTEP 24-11 [S2]. The losses: at USC 42-26, Fresno State 26-10 and Wyoming 16-13 [S2]. Nobody in this game is ranked [S2][S3]. Next up after Reno is New Mexico at home on Oct. 31 [S5], and that's a big sprint in the league race.
The retro so far: the three losses tell a story. USC is a Big Ten program and scored 42 on us in Los Angeles, but we put up 26 [S2]. Fresno State held us to 10 [S2]. And Wyoming beat us 16-13 in a game decided by a field goal [S2]. Meanwhile, three of our four wins came on the road [S2], which is exactly the kind of resilience I want in a product that has to ship on a deadline. The defense has carried the release: we've allowed 16 points or fewer in four of seven games [S2]. If the offense can hold up its end in Reno, this team starts November in the thick of things.

6. This Week: San José State (4-3) at Nevada (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET (2 p.m. Pacific) · Mackay Stadium, Reno · MW+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we beat UTEP 24-11 on the road; Teu ran for 156 yards and two touchdowns [S5]. Nevada lost 31-17 at North Dakota State, where the Bison returned a missed field goal 100 yards for a touchdown and returned a botched two-point try for two more points [S9].
Our offense vs. their defense: Nevada's pass defense is a tough firewall, 155.3 yards allowed a game, 7th in FBS [S5]. But its run defense allows 184.3 a game (116th), and opponents score on 94.4% of red zone trips (127th) [S5]. My A/B test says: run the ball, then finish in the red zone.
Their offense vs. our defense: Nevada runs for 192.8 yards a game (37th) and throws for 171.8 (122nd) [S5]. Dominic Kelley has 500 rushing yards [S5]. The Wolf Pack are minus-8 in turnovers, 134th [S5], so our 27 sacks have a chance to force mistakes [S2].
Series: in the 2016-2025 window, Nevada won five of nine meetings and we won four [S2].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
Elevation: Mackay Stadium's field sits at 4,610 feet [S7]. Hydrate, team.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against a 116th-ranked run defense. (2) Red zone finishing. (3) Whether our pass rush can make Nevada's turnover problem worse.
And Ridge Corbell, Nevada's insider: I hear you snowboard. I ship code. Let's see whose release holds up on game day.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back in San Jose? Original Joe's on South 1st Street is a classic downtown dinner after a road win.

report.title: "Steady, Then a View": Zeb Coldiron Welcomes Undefeated JMU to the Mountain
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy. Come on up the mountain. I'm Zebulon Coldiron, but you can call me Zeb, and I'm your App State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a fourth-generation Watauga County kid, and I learned to whittle and read a defense on the same front porch. My granddaddy could spot a blitz before the snap and carve a perfect duck in the same afternoon. I'm still working on the duck.

I don't hurry, and I don't holler (much). I treat every week like a hike: steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. That means real numbers, plain talk, and a fair word for every visitor. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll go find out. Some programs get a stadium. We got a mountain with a stadium on it. Come up for the game, stay for the leaves, and bring your grandma a jacket. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Appalachian State is in Boone, North Carolina, and has played FBS football in the Sun Belt since 2014 [S5]. Before that, the Mountaineers were an FCS power from 1978 to 2013 [S5]. They won three straight national championships from 2005 to 2007, the first FCS team to do it since the playoffs began in 1978 [S5]. The program has won about 661 games and 22 conference championships, and its all-time winning percentage of .646 ranks 16th nationally [S5]. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do so [S5].

Home is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team went unbeaten and unscored upon in the regular season, outscoring opponents 206-0 [S5]. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,000 [S1]. The last five seasons: 10-4, 6-6, 9-5, 5-6 and 5-8 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Dowell Loggains is in his second season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024 [S1]. He came to Boone from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator [S7]. Before that, he was an NFL offensive coordinator for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets [S7]. He played quarterback at Arkansas [S7].

The 2026 numbers show a passing offense with a punch: 267.7 passing yards per game (33rd in FBS) and 421.8 total (48th) [S3]. Scoring is 29.5 points per game [S3]. The run game averages 154.2 yards [S3] at 4.24 per carry [S1]. The defense allows 352.3 yards and 21.8 points per game (54th) [S3], and holds opponents to 3.68 yards per carry [S1]. The Mountaineers are +4 in turnover margin (22nd) [S3], and their red-zone offense scores 92% of the time (24th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Malachi Singleton: 113 of 169, 1,429 yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 66.9% [S2][S3]. He started at Coastal and went 12 of 14 for 151 yards [S4].
• QB Henry Hasselbeck: the junior backup ran 21 times for 125 yards at Coastal and went 9 of 12 for 112 yards, including his first touchdown pass [S4]. Steady as a mule on a ridge.
• RB Jaquari Lewis: 346 yards on 70 carries, 8 TD [S3]. He scored four rushing touchdowns at Coastal [S4].
• WR Sam Pickett III: 26 catches, 411 yards, 4 TD [S3], including the 31-yard touchdown at Coastal [S4].
• DL Caleb Sandstrom: 5 sacks [S2]. LB Colton Phares: a team-high 38 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

App State is 4-2 overall and 1-1 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Mountaineers are 2-1 at home and 2-1 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The losses came at NC State (41-31) and at home to Old Dominion (10-3) [S1]. James Madison arrives at 7-0 and 4-0 in the league [S1]. A win Thursday would be the kind of view you climb all day to see.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

James Madison (7-0) at App State (4-2) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone · ESPNU [S3][S8] · It's also Family Weekend on campus [S10].

Last time out. We rallied to beat Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16. We trailed 24-14 at halftime, then pulled ahead behind Lewis's four touchdown runs and ran out the clock [S4]. JMU beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17, with Camden Coleman throwing for 185 yards and two touchdowns and George Pettaway running for 119 yards [S3].

App State's offense vs. JMU's defense. The Dukes allow just 16 points per game (19th) and 114.3 rushing yards (35th) [S3], with 18 sacks [S1]. Their pass defense allows 236.4 yards per game (103rd) [S3], so Singleton and Pickett may find room through the air. Both red-zone offenses are strong [S3], so finishing drives will matter.

JMU's offense vs. App State's defense. This is the steepest part of the trail. JMU averages 42.9 points per game (3rd in FBS) and 223.6 rushing yards (14th) [S3]. Pettaway has 755 yards and seven touchdowns, per AP [S3]. Coleman has 13 touchdown passes and one interception [S3]. Our run defense allows 137.8 yards per game (60th) [S3]. Sandstrom and the front will have to make plays in the backfield.

Series. JMU's athletics site lists the Dukes at 6-14 all-time against App State [S9], so the Mountaineers lead the series. But last year JMU won 58-10 in Harrisonburg on Nov. 15, 2025 [S9]. That one stung.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S11]. Singleton started at Coastal, and Hasselbeck played a big role [S4]. Thursday's quarterback plan isn't confirmed, and I found no other injury news.

James Madison's insider debuts this week too, a former cheer captain. I'll lend her a jacket. It gets cold on the mountain at night.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can App State slow a JMU run game averaging 223.6 yards per game [S3]?
2. Can Singleton and Pickett take advantage of JMU's 103rd-ranked pass defense [S3]?
3. Can the Mountaineers win the turnover battle against a +7 JMU team [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

Family Weekend is here [S10]. I'll share Boone spots once I've confirmed them. Bring layers. Not an ad.

report.title: "Quack-Quack, Wrong Pond": Ty Doucet-Harmon Welcomes the Panthers to Jonesboro
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Quack-quack, wrong pond. Well, howdy, I'm Ty Doucet-Harmon, and when I'm not up in the stands in Jonesboro, I'm guiding duck hunters through the flooded timber of the Arkansas Delta. I scout this football team the same way I scout a duck season: early mornings, patience, and a sharp eye for which way the birds are moving. I travel with the Red Wolves and I live with the Red Wolves, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, in a slow Delta drawl with a duck call never far from my lips. When we win, I blow the call and do a little wing flap. When we lose, I retreat to the duck blind, which is what I call the space behind the desk. Grab your waders. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Arkansas State football was founded in 1911 and has played in the Sun Belt since 2001 [S7]. The Red Wolves have claimed 12 conference championships, most recently in 2016, and one national championship at the NCAA College Division level in 1970 [S7]. The school changed its mascot to the Red Wolves in 2008 [S7]. Home is Centennial Bank Stadium in Jonesboro, opened in 1974 and listed at 30,382 seats [S7][S3]. The last five seasons climbed like a sunrise over the timber: 2-10, 3-9, 6-7, 8-5 and 7-6 [S3].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Butch Jones is the head coach [S7]; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 12, 2020 [S3]. This team throws it: Trey Owens has completed 68.7% of his passes [S5], and we average 231.7 passing yards a game (68th) [S5]. The run game is 130.4 a game (110th) [S5]. The defense is good against the pass, 184.3 yards allowed (31st) [S5], and it takes the ball away: 11 takeaways [S3] and a plus-3 turnover margin, 34th in FBS [S5]. Here's the hard truth from the blind: the run defense allows 195.4 a game (124th), and opponents convert 45.9% of third downs (129th) [S5]. We only have 3 sacks all year [S3]. That's an empty sky on opening morning.

4. Players to Know

• QB Trey Owens: 138 of 201, 1,631 yards per ESPN (1,622 per AP), 9 TD, 6 INT [S4][S5].
• RB Solomon Baggett: 287 yards on 61 carries per ESPN (289 on 62 per AP), 2 TD [S4][S5].

• K Clune Van Andel: made field goals of 29, 40 and 44 yards last week [S9]. That's a man who hits his birds.
• S Joe Drew: team-high 64 tackles [S4]. DT Ryan Reese: 1.5 sacks [S4]. CB Dontrae Henderson: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Arkansas State is 3-4 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt [S3]. We beat West Georgia 52-7, Kennesaw State 17-14 and Southern Miss 23-13 [S3]. We lost at Memphis 42-24, at TCU 31-7, a three-pointer at Louisiana 23-20 and a 56-49 shootout to South Alabama [S3]. After Georgia State, we have a week off, then host UL Monroe on Nov. 7 [S5]. Two of those losses were by a field goal and a touchdown [S3]. Close, friends. Real close.
Season so far, from the blind: some mornings the birds just don't come in. That TCU trip was one of them [S3]. But other mornings the sky fills up, like the 52-7 day against West Georgia [S3], and last week, when we grinded out the clock in Hattiesburg [S9]. A good guide knows the weather changes. You stay in the blind, you stay patient, and the ducks come back. Coach Jones has this team climbing, and seven wins last year proved it [S3].

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7 p.m. ET (6 p.m. Central) · Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8].

AP says we won time of possession by about 20 minutes [S9]. Kenyon Clark and Timothy Carter ran for touchdowns [S9]. Georgia State lost 49-22 at James Madison [S5].

report.title: "Next Stop, Third-and-Long": Malik Overstreet Rides Into Jonesboro
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Next stop, third-and-long. What's up, Atlanta, I'm Malik Overstreet. I went to policy school, I know every MARTA stop by heart, and I know every Georgia State third-down tendency the same way. I travel with the Panthers and I live with the Panthers, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, at Atlanta speed. My system for sizing up opponents is simple: traffic. A defense that can't move is the Connector at rush hour. A defense that flies around is I-285 at 3 a.m. on a Sunday. We're the big-city kids in a conference full of small towns, and I love every road trip into the country. When we win, I dance like I just found a parking spot downtown. When we lose, I blame the traffic on 75/85. Let's ride. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Georgia State football is young. The Panthers were founded in 2010 and play at the FBS level in the Sun Belt [S6]. Home is Center Parc Stadium, about ten minutes from our downtown campus [S6], listed at 25,000 seats [S2]. The last five seasons: a strong 8-5 in 2021, then 4-8, 7-6, 3-9 and a tough 1-11 in 2025 [S2]. So this 4-2 start? That's a green light on Peachtree at 5 p.m. You don't see it often, and you enjoy every second of it.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Dell McGee is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Feb. 23, 2024 [S2]. This year's offense moves like the HOV lane: 452.7 yards a game (23rd in FBS), 36.5 points (26th), 206 rushing yards (26th) and 246.7 passing (52nd) [S5]. We convert 47.5% of third downs (26th) [S5] and score on 92% of red zone trips (24th) [S5]. We hold the ball 32:34 a game, 25th [S5]. The defense is solid against the pass, 189.2 yards allowed a game (38th) [S5], and it gets after the quarterback with 19 sacks [S2]. Where we stall out: a minus-4 turnover margin, 113th in FBS [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Cameran Brown: 102 of 156 for 1,291 yards, 13 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. At James Madison he also ran nine times for 71 yards [S5].
• RB Lanear McCrary Jr.: 385 yards on 78 carries, 4 TD [S4][S5]. DJ Murray Jr. ran for 56 yards and caught three passes at JMU [S5].
• WR Rodshaun Dorsey: 21 catches, 333 yards and 7 touchdowns [S4][S5]. Seven! He's the express train.
• LB Xavier Esqillion: 7 sacks [S4]. Seven sacks in six games, folks. That's a man who never sits in traffic.
• LB Jaydon Hood: team-high 35 tackles [S4]. S Deuce Lee: 1 interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Georgia State is 4-2 and 1-1 in the Sun Belt, 3-0 at home and 1-2 on the road [S2]. The wins: North Carolina A&T 59-10, at Kennesaw State 31-17, Northern Illinois 35-14 and Old Dominion 42-10 [S2]. The losses: at UCF 44-30 and at James Madison 49-22 [S2]. After Jonesboro, Coastal Carolina comes to Atlanta on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math tonight. I'm just saying a road win would be the express lane into November.
About the road: both losses came away from home, against good teams [S2]. This is a chance to change that story.
Season so far, by traffic report: the A&T game was the Downtown Connector at 4 a.m., wide open, 59-10 [S2]. Kennesaw State was a short drive up I-75, and we got home happy, 31-17 [S2]. Old Dominion came to town and we scored 42 [S2]. JMU was a jam on a rainy Friday, and we never got out of it [S2]. A new week, a new route. Remember, after 1-11 last year, every one of these four wins means something [S2].

6. This Week: Georgia State (4-2) at Arkansas State (3-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7 p.m. ET · Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: James Madison beat us 49-22 on Oct. 17; Brown threw for 134 yards and a touchdown, and Dorsey caught a touchdown [S5]. Arkansas State beat Southern Miss 23-13, winning time of possession by about 20 minutes [S9].
Our offense vs. their defense: Arkansas State allows 195.4 rushing yards a game (124th), and opponents convert 45.9% of third downs (129th) [S5]. In the red zone, opponents score on 91.3% of trips (113th) [S5]. That's the Downtown Connector at rush hour, and we're on the scooter.
Their offense vs. our defense: Trey Owens has thrown for over 1,600 yards [S4][S5], and receiver Hunter Summers has 422 receiving yards [S5]. Our 38th-ranked pass defense meets their 68th-ranked passing game [S5].
Series: CFBD shows Arkansas State won four of the six meetings from 2016 through 2025 [S2][S3].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Our run game against the 124th-ranked run defense. (2) Turnovers; Arkansas State is plus-3 and we're minus-4 [S5]. (3) Red zone finishing.
My read: this one feels like a one-point game, decided in the last few minutes. Bring snacks, and stay to the final whistle.
To Ty Doucet-Harmon, Arkansas State's insider: we have duck in Atlanta too, my friend. It comes on a plate.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back in Atlanta? Ted's Montana Grill on Luckie Street, near Centennial Olympic Park, is an easy pregame or postgame family supper.
