report.title: "Purple Reign, Y'all": Lila Shenandoah Cheers 7-0 JMU Up the Mountain
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Purple reign, y'all! I'm Lila Shenandoah, your James Madison insider at The Cover Window. I'm a former JMU cheer captain who somehow became the program's living encyclopedia. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I turn every stat into a cheer. Yes, even penalties. "Give me a FLAG! Give me a FIVE! Give me... a moment to collect myself!"

Here's what you get from me. Glam, volume, and receipts. I'm excited, I'm all-in, and every number I chant has a source behind it. Every opponent gets a respectful pom-pom wave, and I don't invent anything, ever. If I don't know, I'll say, "Hold that chant, I'm checking." The Shenandoah Valley shows up loud and proud for the Dukes. Give me a J, give me an M, give me a third-down stop. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

JMU first fielded a football team in 1972, and the Dukes play on campus at Bridgeforth Stadium in Harrisonburg, Virginia [S6]. CFBD lists it as built in 1975 with a capacity of 24,877 [S1]. JMU won FCS national championships in 2004 and 2016 and finished as national runner-up in 2017 and 2019 [S6]. The Dukes accepted an invitation to the FBS in 2021 and joined the Sun Belt [S6]. Wikipedia's intro gives both 2022 and 2023 as the start of conference play, so I'm flagging that as conflicting [S6]. Famous Dukes include Charles Haley, who won five Super Bowl rings and is in both the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame [S6].

The last five seasons are pure cheer material: 12-2, 8-3, 11-2, 9-4 and 12-2 [S1]. Give me a W! Give me lots of them!

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Billy Napier is in his first season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 6, 2025 [S1]. He was head coach at Louisiana from 2018 to 2021, going 40-12 with three straight seasons of 10 or more wins [S7], and then at Florida from 2022 to 2025 [S7]. Before becoming a head coach, he was offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Arizona State in 2017 [S7].

The 2026 numbers make me want to do a full basket toss. JMU averages 42.9 points per game (3rd in FBS), 461 yards per game (18th) and 223.6 rushing yards (14th) [S3], at 5.71 yards per carry [S1]. The defense allows 16 points per game (19th) and 114.3 rushing yards (35th) [S3]. Opponents average 3.31 yards per carry [S1], and the Dukes have 18 sacks [S1]. They're +7 in turnover margin (8th) [S3]. The flag cheer gets a workout, though: 71.1 penalty yards per game (119th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Camden Coleman: 13 TD, 1 INT, 63.2% [S3]. Season yardage is conflicting by one yard: AP lists 1,336 [S3] and ESPN lists 1,335 [S2]. Against Georgia State he went 13 of 19 for 185 yards and two touchdowns [S3].
• RB George Pettaway: 7 TD. AP lists 755 yards on 110 carries [S3], and ESPN lists 767 on 109 [S2], so that's conflicting. He ran 14 times for 119 yards and a touchdown against Georgia State [S3].
• WR Ja'Corey Scott: 22 catches, 333 yards, 4 TD [S3][S2].
• WR Jeremiah Harrison: two catches for 54 yards against Georgia State [S3].
• LB Nakian Jackson: team leader in tackles (50) and sacks (2.5) [S2]. Give me an N! Give me a J!

5. The Conference Picture

James Madison is 7-0 overall and 4-0 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Dukes are 4-0 at home and 3-0 on the road [S1], with road wins at San Diego State, Old Dominion and Georgia Southern [S1]. They are not ranked in the poll data in my pack [S1]. The closest calls were the opener against Liberty (20-13) and at Georgia Southern (27-24) [S1]. A win in Boone would make it 8-0 and 5-0 in the league [S1].

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

James Madison (7-0) at App State (4-2) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone, N.C. · ESPNU [S3][S8]

Last time out. The Dukes beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17 [S3]. App State rallied past Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16, with Jaquari Lewis scoring four rushing touchdowns [S4].

JMU's offense vs. App State's defense. Our ground game against a run defense that allows 137.8 yards per game (60th) [S3]. Pettaway gets the ball, the offensive front gets the credit, I get the megaphone. App State is +4 in turnover margin (22nd) [S3], and Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks [S2], so ball security and protection come first. Our red-zone offense scores 94.7% of the time (13th) [S3].

App State's offense vs. JMU's defense. The Mountaineers throw for 267.7 yards per game (33rd) [S3]. Malachi Singleton has 1,429 yards and only two interceptions [S2][S3], and Sam Pickett III has 411 receiving yards [S3]. Our pass defense allows 236.4 yards per game (103rd) [S3], so that's the matchup to watch. App State also has a running quarterback option in Henry Hasselbeck, who ran for 125 yards at Coastal [S4].

Series. JMU's athletics site lists the Dukes at 6-14 all-time against App State [S9], so the Mountaineers lead the series. Last year JMU won 58-10 in Harrisonburg on Nov. 15, 2025 [S9]. Respect the history, then cheer for the present.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S11]. I found no confirmed JMU injury news. App State's quarterback plan is unconfirmed after both Singleton and Hasselbeck played at Coastal [S4].

App State's debut insider is a whittling storyteller from the High Country. I'll bring the pom-poms if he brings a porch.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can JMU's run game keep rolling on the road [S3]?
2. Can our pass defense handle Singleton and Pickett [S3]?
3. Can the Dukes cut down on penalty yards (71.1 per game) in a loud road setting [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

Family Weekend is happening in Boone [S10], so it'll be packed. I'll share road-trip stops once I've confirmed them. Not an ad.

report.title: "Laissez les Bons Stats Rouler!": Mimi Fontenot Two-Steps Into Hattiesburg
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Laissez les bons stats rouler! Bonjour, mes amis, I'm Amélie Fontenot, but everybody from Lafayette to Breaux Bridge calls me Mimi. By weekday I'm an accountant. By Saturday night I'm two-stepping at the dance hall, and in between I watch Ragin' Cajun football the way I dance zydeco: it's all rhythm, cher, all game flow. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I have a little Cajun French for every football term. A touchdown? Magnifique. A turnover? Ça c'est bon (if it's ours). Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little accordion in the background. When we win, I two-step around the desk. When we lose, I say "Laissez les bons temps... later," and eat my boudin solemnly. Allons! (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Ragin' Cajuns represent the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, and you may remember the old names, Southwestern Louisiana and USL [S6]. We play in the Sun Belt [S6]. Home since 1971 has been Cajun Field in Lafayette [S6], listed at 41,426 seats [S2]. Michael Desormeaux has been head coach since 2021 [S6]. Our recent history has some magnifique years: 13-1 in 2021 and 10-4 in 2024, with 6-7 seasons in between and 6-7 again in 2025 [S2]. And the gameday? Cher, the food alone is worth the drive. I've never met a tailgate that didn't have a pot of something on it.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Desormeaux was hired Dec. 5, 2021 [S2]. This year's team dances to a ground-game beat: 200.1 rushing yards a game, 29th in FBS [S5], 1,396 yards on 298 carries [S2]. We control the clock, 33:27 a game, 11th in FBS [S5]. The defense is the real band: 298.3 yards allowed (25th), 104.3 rushing allowed (27th) and 19.3 points allowed (35th) [S5]. It has 14 takeaways [S2], and we're plus-3 in turnover margin (34th) [S5]. The passing game is the quieter instrument, 177.6 yards a game (119th) [S5]. And we play clean, 40.3 penalty yards a game, 11th-fewest [S5]. Like a good two-step: simple, steady, nobody steps on anybody's toes.

4. Players to Know

• QB D'Wayne "Lunch" Winfield: 108 of 155, 1,153 yards, 4 TD, 4 INT, and he's also our leading rusher with 463 yards and 8 TD on 97 carries [S4][S5]. (AP uses D'Wayne; ESPN uses Lunch. Same fella, same magic [S5][S4].)
• RB J.J. Garner: 10 carries for 62 yards and a touchdown against Troy [S5][S9].
• WR KeDarius Wade: 11 catches, 226 yards, 2 TD [S4][S5]. He caught the touchdown against Troy [S9].
• LB Jake St. Andre: a team-high 48 tackles [S4]. LB Lester Jones: 2 sacks [S4]. CB Brent Gordon Jr.: 2 interceptions [S4].
• Harrison Kidder recovered a muffed punt at Troy's 8 that set up a touchdown last week [S9].

5. The Conference Picture

Louisiana is 5-2 and 2-1 in the Sun Belt, 4-0 at home and 1-2 away [S2]. The wins: Lamar 38-7, UAB 21-14, at Charlotte 34-7, Arkansas State 23-20 and Troy 33-6 [S2]. The losses: at USC 49-30 and a 32-31 heartbreaker at Louisiana Tech [S2]. Neither team is ranked [S2][S3]. After this, South Alabama comes to Cajun Field on Nov. 7 [S5]. A road win here keeps the rhythm going into November.
The rhythm of the season: the USC game was a learning dance; we scored 30 on a Big Ten team on the road [S2]. The one-point loss in Ruston still stings, mon Dieu [S2]. Since then, Troy managed just 6 points against our defense [S2]. That's the beat I want to keep. And here's a little note from the Troy game that tells you who we are: Winfield threw for just 70 yards, and we still won by 27, because three different players ran for touchdowns: Garner, Anthony Reagan Jr. and Steven Blanco [S9]. When the band plays that song, cher, everybody dances.

6. This Week: Louisiana (5-2) at Southern Miss (1-5)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET (4 p.m. Central) · M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8]. (Wikipedia calls the stadium Renasant Stadium; CFBD calls it M. M. Roberts. I'm showing you both [S7][S3].)

report.title: "Peachy": Champ Tullos Welcomes the Monarchs to Ruston
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, that's just peachy. Howdy, Bulldog fans, I'm Booker Tullos, but folks around Ruston call me Champ. I grew up on a peach farm off the highway, played fullback for Tech, and to this day nothing in football makes me happier than a fourth-and-inches plunge into the end zone. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines in an easygoing north-Louisiana drawl, with peach puns baked right in like a cobbler. When we win, I holler "Peachy!" and do a fullback dive across the studio (the carpet has suffered). When we lose, I sigh "bruised peach," and then I go back and watch every snap. Sit a spell. And remember what my granddaddy said about peaches and football: the good ones take a whole season to ripen. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Louisiana Tech first played in 1901 and has an all-time record of 654-508-37 [S7]. The Bulldogs have won three Division II national championships and 25 conference titles, and played in 30 postseason games, 15 of them major college bowls [S7]. Since 1968, home has been Joe Aillet Stadium in Ruston [S7], listed at 28,019 seats [S3]. After 13 seasons in Conference USA, Tech joined the Sun Belt on July 1, 2026 [S7], so this is our first fall in a new orchard. The recent climb: 3-9 three years running from 2021 to 2023, 5-8 in 2024 and 8-5 in 2025 [S3]. That's a tree that's starting to bear fruit.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Sonny Cumbie is the head coach [S7], hired Nov. 30, 2021 [S3]. The 2026 Bulldogs score 33.3 points a game (43rd) and throw for 239.8 yards (58th), with 153.2 rushing (73rd) [S5]. The defense has made a habit of taking the ball away: 13 takeaways and a plus-5 turnover margin, 15th in FBS [S3][S5]. It holds opponents to 36.9% on third down (64th) [S5]. Where we've been bruised: the red zone offense scores on just 76% of trips (118th) [S5], and the run defense allows 148.5 a game (84th) [S5]. As a former fullback, the red zone number keeps me up at night. Give me the ball at the 2, Coach. I'm available. Turnovers have hidden a lot of that, and good teams find ways to win close games. This one has, twice [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Blake Baker: 68 of 99, 857 yards, 9 TD, 1 INT, 68.7% [S4][S5]. Last week he was 15 of 21 for 178 yards and two touchdowns [S5].
• RB Andrew Burnette: 286 yards on 65 carries, 1 TD [S4][S5], with 79 yards on 22 carries against ULM [S5].
• WR Jalen Mickens: 32 catches, 476 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5]. Marcus Calwise Jr. caught eight passes for 119 yards last week [S5].
• LB Alonzo Jackson Jr.: team-high 41 tackles and 5 sacks [S4]. DB Jordan McRae: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Louisiana Tech is 4-2 overall and 2-0 in our first Sun Belt season, and 3-0 at home [S3]. The wins: Northwestern State 80-6, Army 31-29, Louisiana 32-31 and at UL Monroe 24-0 [S3]. The losses were road trips to LSU (45-14) and Baylor (36-19) [S3]. Two of the four wins were by two points or fewer [S3], and I'll take a sweet win any way it comes. After this, we visit South Alabama on Oct. 31 [S5]. Staying unbeaten in league play keeps us in the thick of the race in year one [S3].
From the porch: that 32-31 win over Louisiana was the kind of game folks in Ruston will tell stories about at the peach festival for a while [S3]. And beating Army by two is never easy [S3]. This team has learned how to finish close games. Now it needs to learn how to finish drives in the red zone [S5].

6. This Week: Old Dominion (2-5) at Louisiana Tech (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Joe Aillet Stadium · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we shut out UL Monroe 24-0 [S5]. Old Dominion lost 23-15 to Georgia Southern on Oct. 15 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: ODU's defense is respectable: 335.7 yards allowed (47th) and 198.3 passing (50th) [S5]. But its red zone defense allows a score on 87.5% of trips (95th) [S5], so if we can get there, we should cash in. Peach cobbler, served warm.
Their offense vs. our defense: ODU averages 266 yards (138th) and 17.7 points (130th) and has allowed 32 sacks [S5][S2]. Jackson's pass rush has a real chance to make a living [S4]. ODU converts 33% of third downs (120th) [S5].
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Red zone finishing for our offense. (2) Our pass rush against a struggling pass protection. (3) Keeping the turnover margin where it's been, plus-5 [S5].
And Winnie Pocklington, ODU's insider: your majesty is welcome in Ruston anytime. I'll save you a peach, and a seat on the porch after the game, win or lose.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Ruston for the game? The Log Cabin Grill on Farmerville Highway is a longtime family standby for a good burger.

report.title: "We Are": Mercy Holderby Welcomes You to a Rare Tuesday Night at The Joan
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Hi, friends. I'm Mercy Holderby, your Marshall insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Huntington native and a nurse, and I'm the daughter of two Marshall grads. I grew up hearing the story of this program's rebirth at our kitchen table. Some families pass down recipes. Mine passed down a chant.

You'll get two things from me every week. First, tenderness. I love these young men, win or lose, and I'll always talk about them as people first. Second, toughness. I'll tell you the truth about what the numbers say, even when it stings, and I'll never invent a fact to make us feel better. If I don't know, I'll say so. And yes, I'll be the loudest "We Are" in any room. In Huntington, those words mean more than a cheer. They're a promise passed down by families like mine, and every Saturday (and this week, every Tuesday) we keep it. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Marshall plays in the Sun Belt Conference East Division at the FBS level [S9]. Home is Joan C. Edwards Stadium, which opened in 1991 with a 24-23 win over New Hampshire in front of 33,116 fans [S9]. The record crowd is 41,382, set against West Virginia on Sept. 10, 2010 [S9]. Capacity is listed two ways: Wikipedia says 38,227 [S9] and CFBD says 38,016 [S1]. It's one of two Division I stadiums named for a woman [S9], and through the 2024 season Marshall was 192-45 there [S9].

Marshall's first organized game against another college was a 15-0 win over Shelton College on Nov. 24, 1903 [S5]. The 2014 team went 13-1 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll [S5]. The last five seasons: 7-6, 9-4, 6-7, 10-3 and 5-7 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Tony Gibson is in his second season, with an 8-10 record at Marshall [S5]. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 8, 2024 [S1]. He's a 1994 Glenville State graduate [S5], and he was previously defensive coordinator at West Virginia and NC State [S10].

The 2026 numbers are honest and a little hard to read. On offense, Marshall averages 406.5 yards per game, with 247.8 passing and 158.7 rushing [S3], at 4.43 yards per carry [S1]. The trouble is turnovers. The Herd has 14 giveaways and five takeaways [S1], a -9 margin that ranks 136th in FBS [S3]. The defense allows 447.3 yards per game (132nd) and 33.7 points (129th) [S3]. Opponents average 5.54 yards per carry [S1], and Marshall has only five sacks [S1].

4. Players to Know

• QB Carlos Del Rio-Wilson: the season passing leader, at 1,014 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT, 64.0% [S3]. (ESPN lists 1,041 yards, so the figure is conflicting [S2].) CollegeFootballDigest's CFBD data shows him 2 of 6 for 37 yards with three interceptions against Coastal [S11].
• QB Zion Turner: led Marshall against Coastal Carolina with 219 yards on 18 of 27 and two touchdowns [S3][S7]. Tuesday's starter isn't confirmed in my sources.
• RB Judah Price: made his first college start against Coastal and ran for 124 yards on 12 carries, with a touchdown run and a touchdown catch [S4][S7]. That included a 50-yard scoring run [S7].
• RB Joshon Barbie: the season rushing leader, with 230 yards on 49 carries, 2 TD [S3].
• WR Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw: 22 catches, 324 yards, 4 TD [S3].
• LB Javae Gilmore: 10 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, a deflection that led to an interception, and a blocked field goal against Coastal [S4]. DB Caleb Clark-Glover: a team-high 44 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

Marshall is 3-3 overall and 0-2 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Herd is 2-1 at home and 1-2 on the road [S1]. It is not ranked [S1]. After a 3-1 start, Marshall lost at James Madison (45-17) and at home to Coastal Carolina (27-21) [S1]. Tuesday is the Herd's first crossover game against a West Division opponent this season [S4], and a win would be its first Sun Belt win of 2026 [S5].

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

South Alabama (4-2) at Marshall (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:30 p.m. ET · Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington · ESPN2 per Marshall and the Sun Belt [S4][S6] (the game notes list ESPN+, a conflict [S5])

Why it's special. It's only the fifth regular-season Tuesday home game in Marshall history [S4]. The Herd is 3-1 in Tuesday home games [S5], and the last regular-season one was a 37-23 win over Houston in 2008 [S4]. Players will wear helmet decals honoring West Virginia's coal miners [S4]. That one gets me right here.

Last time out. Coastal Carolina forced six turnovers and led 27-0 early in the third quarter. Marshall then scored three touchdowns before losing 27-21 [S7]. South Alabama beat Arkansas State 56-49, the highest-scoring FBS game of the season to that point [S8].

Marshall's offense vs. South Alabama's defense. There's real opportunity here. The Jaguars allow 429.0 yards (126th), 264.8 passing (127th) and 34.5 points per game (131st) [S3]. Opponents average 5.76 yards per carry against them [S1]. But South Alabama leads the Sun Belt in turnover margin at +1.3 per game [S4], and that's exactly where we've struggled [S3].

South Alabama's offense vs. Marshall's defense. Keenan Phillips has 444 yards and five touchdowns [S3]. He and PJ Martin have combined for 867 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns [S4]. Against Arkansas State, Phillips ran for 157 yards and three scores and returned a kickoff 100 yards [S8]. Our run defense allows 193.8 yards per game (123rd) [S3]. Tackling is everything Tuesday.

Series. South Alabama leads 1-0. The only meeting was a 28-0 Jaguars win in Mobile in 2023, and this is the first game between the schools in Huntington [S4].

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed injury report for either team, so statuses are unknown, including the starting quarterback.

South Alabama debuts its own insider this week. Welcome to Huntington, neighbor. We'll be kind until kickoff.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Marshall win the turnover battle after losing it 6-0 to Coastal [S7]?
2. Can the Herd's defense tackle Phillips and Martin [S4]?
3. Who plays quarterback, and can he finish in the red zone, where Marshall ranks 129th [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

I'm not naming Huntington spots until I've confirmed them for you. Wear green. Not an ad.

report.title: "Hear Ye, Hear Ye!": Winnie Pocklington Holds Court as the Monarchs Visit Ruston
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hear ye, hear ye! Let it be proclaimed from the harbor to the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel that the Monarchs' royal court reporter has arrived. I am Winifred Pocklington, Winnie to my loyal subjects, and I treat every first down like a knighthood and every win like a coronation. I'm regal, I'm playful, and I'm salt-air tough, because Norfolk does that to a person. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a royal-court flourish and an honest heart. When we win, there will be trumpets (metaphorical, mostly). When we lose, the crown gets polished and the court reconvenes on Monday. Long live the Monarchs. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Hear ye: Old Dominion's football story has two chapters. The first team, in 1930, was the William & Mary Norfolk Division Braves [S6]. The modern Monarchs were founded in 2009, played two seasons as an FCS independent, joined the Colonial Athletic Association in 2011, moved up to Conference USA in the FBS in 2014 and joined the Sun Belt in 2022 [S6]. Home is S.B. Ballard Stadium in Norfolk, listed at 20,118 seats [S2]. Our five most recent seasons went 6-7, 3-9, 6-7, 5-7 and then a royal 10-3 in 2025 [S2]. That last one deserved a parade down Hampton Boulevard. The crown, as they say, is heavy. We carry it anyway.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Ricky Rahne was hired Dec. 7, 2019 [S2]. The 2026 Monarchs are built on defense. They allow 335.7 yards a game (47th in FBS) and 198.3 passing yards (50th), with 137.4 rushing yards allowed (58th) [S5]. The defense has forced 12 turnovers [S2]. The offense is still being fitted for its robes: 266 yards a game (138th), 151.7 passing (131st), 114.3 rushing (122nd) and 17.7 points (130th) [S5]. Protection has been the hardest task in the realm, 32 sacks allowed in seven games [S2]. Penalties, 68.7 yards a game, rank 112th [S5]. A queen must be honest with her court, and that's the honest picture. But here is the royal decree: the defense is good enough to keep this team in games, and in the Sun Belt, a team that can play defense on the road always has a chance [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Quinn Henicle: 54 of 98, 656 yards, 4 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5].
• QB Ryan Huff: led the offense against Georgia Southern, 9 of 14 for 115 yards and a touchdown [S5]. A starter for Saturday has not been announced in anything I found as of Oct. 18 [S9].
• RB Devin Roche: 373 yards on 95 carries [S4][S5].
• WR T.J. Johnson: 16 catches, 262 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5], including two for 83 and a score last time out [S5].
• S Lucas Struck: a team-high 52 tackles [S4]. DL Javen Gibson: 5 sacks [S4]. CB Brandon Crutchfield: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Old Dominion is 2-5 overall and 1-3 in the Sun Belt [S2]. The wins: Norfolk State 31-10 and a 10-3 defensive gem at App State [S2]. The losses include Virginia Tech, East Carolina by three, James Madison, Georgia State and Georgia Southern [S2]. Neither team is ranked [S2][S3]. After Ruston, Marshall visits Norfolk on Oct. 31 [S5]. A road win against a Louisiana Tech team that's 2-0 in league play [S3] would be the sort of upset that gets a royal portrait painted.
The court's notes on the season: the App State win is the template. Our defense held the Mountaineers to 3 points on the road [S2]. The 20-17 loss to East Carolina was a coin-flip [S2]. If the defense brings that same energy to Ruston, the Monarchs can stay in this one deep into the fourth quarter.

6. This Week: Old Dominion (2-5) at Louisiana Tech (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston, La. · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last game: we lost 23-15 to Georgia Southern on Oct. 15 [S5]. Louisiana Tech shut out UL Monroe 24-0 on Oct. 17 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Louisiana Tech allows 148.5 rushing yards a game (84th) and 24.5 points (76th) [S5]. Its defense has 13 takeaways [S3], and LB Alonzo Jackson Jr. has 5 sacks [S4]. With our protection struggles, ball security is everything.
Their offense vs. our defense: Louisiana Tech scores 33.3 points a game (43rd) and throws for 239.8 yards (58th) [S5]. QB Blake Baker has 9 TD and 1 INT [S5]. The good news for the crown: Tech's red zone offense ranks 118th, scoring on 76% of trips [S5]. Bend, don't break, and make them kick.
Series: I could not find an all-time series record in a free source, and the two teams didn't meet regularly in the last decade [S10].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Protection: 32 sacks allowed has to shrink. Get the ball out quickly, use the backs to help, and give our quarterbacks a clean pocket to work from. (2) Red zone defense against a Tech offense that stalls there. (3) Turnovers: Tech is plus-5 (15th), we're minus-3 (99th) [S5].
And Booker Tullos, Louisiana Tech's insider: I hear you're peachy. Her Majesty sends her regards and a challenge.

report.title: "Pull Up a Lawn Chair, Honey": Azalea Fairhope-Grice Rolls the Parade to Huntington
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Well, hey, y'all! I'm Azalea Fairhope-Grice, your South Alabama insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Mobile native and a Mardi Gras float-builder, and I coached high school volleyball long enough to keep a whistle in my purse. I still have it. I will use it.

Here's my promise. I'll bring Southern charm and a competitive streak in equal measure. You'll get real numbers, honest takes, and gracious words for every opponent, because Mama raised me right. You won't get made-up stats or rumors dressed up as news. If I don't know, I'll say, "Darlin', I'm still checking." Mobile is where Mardi Gras started in America, and our Jaguars bring that same parade energy to every game. This year, the parade has a run game. Pull up a lawn chair, honey. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

South Alabama started its football program in 2009 and joined the FBS in 2012 as a member of the Sun Belt Conference [S9]. That makes it one of the youngest programs in the country, and it has already had a 10-win season: 10-3 in 2022 [S1]. Home is Hancock Whitney Stadium, which opened in 2020, and CFBD lists its capacity at 25,450 [S1].

The last five seasons: 5-7, 10-3, 7-6, 7-6 and 4-8 [S1]. With the win at Arkansas State, the 2026 Jaguars already matched last season's four wins [S8]. Six games in, and the float's already decorated.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Major Applewhite has been head coach since 2024 [S10]. CFBD lists his hire date as Jan. 18, 2024 [S1]. He was head coach at Houston in 2017 and 2018, after serving as the Cougars' offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach [S10]. He has also coached at Texas, Syracuse, Rice and Alabama [S10]. As a player, he quarterbacked Texas from 1998 to 2001, sharing the job with Chris Simms [S10].

The 2026 identity is clear: run the ball and protect it. South Alabama has 276 rushing attempts and just 151 passes [S1]. It averages 220.3 rushing yards per game (16th in FBS) [S3] and 4.79 yards per carry [S1], and scores 38.8 points per game (15th) [S3]. The Jaguars have only three giveaways against 11 takeaways [S1]. The defense is the work in progress, allowing 429.0 yards (126th) and 34.5 points (131st) per game [S3].

4. Players to Know

• RB Keenan Phillips: 444 yards on 80 carries, 5 TD [S3]. At Arkansas State he ran for 157 yards and three touchdowns and returned a kickoff 100 yards [S8]. Throw that man some beads.
• RB PJ Martin: ran for 95 yards and a touchdown at Arkansas State [S8]. Phillips and Martin have combined for 867 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns [S4].
• QB Jared Hollins: 855 passing yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 60.9% [S3]. At Arkansas State he scored two short rushing touchdowns 21 seconds apart [S8].
• WR Brendan Jenkins: 21 catches, 355 yards, 3 TD [S3].
• S Cole Blaylock: a team-high 42 tackles [S2], including 10 at Arkansas State per CFBD data [S11].

5. The Conference Picture

South Alabama is 4-2 overall and 2-0 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Jaguars are 3-0 at home and 1-2 on the road [S1], with road losses at Tulane (28-24) and Kentucky (45-21) [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. They lead the Sun Belt and rank sixth nationally in turnover margin, at +1.3 per game [S4]. A win in Huntington would make them 3-0 in league play [S1], and I'd be on a float by Wednesday.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

South Alabama (4-2) at Marshall (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 CT) · Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington · ESPN2 [S6][S4]

Last time out. We won 56-49 at Arkansas State on Oct. 8, the highest-scoring FBS game of the season at the time [S8]. We ran 50 times for 296 yards, then put the game away with a 13-play drive that ate the rest of the clock [S8]. The win also snapped a two-game skid in that series [S8]. Marshall lost 27-21 to Coastal Carolina on Oct. 10 after the Chanticleers forced six turnovers [S7].

South Alabama's offense vs. Marshall's defense. Our ground game against a run defense that allows 193.8 yards per game (123rd) [S3] and 5.54 yards per carry [S1]. Hand it to Keenan, hand it to PJ, repeat. Marshall allowing 43.6% third-down conversions (115th) [S3] suggests long drives are there for the taking. Marshall linebacker Javae Gilmore had 10 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss last time out [S4], so he'll be busy.

Marshall's offense vs. South Alabama's defense. This is where I keep my whistle handy. Our pass defense allows 264.8 yards per game (127th) [S3]. Marshall's Zion Turner threw for 219 yards and two touchdowns against Coastal [S7], and Judah Price ran for 124 in his first start [S4]. Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw has 324 receiving yards [S3]. Our takeaways are the counterpunch, with 11 so far [S1].

Series. South Alabama leads 1-0, from a 28-0 win in Mobile in 2023. This is the first meeting in Huntington [S4].

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed South Alabama injury news. Marshall's starting quarterback is unconfirmed in my sources [S3][S7].

Marshall is introducing its own insider this week, a nurse from Huntington. Bless her. She'll need her stethoscope when Keenan gets going. (Kindly meant!)

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can the Jaguars run it 40-plus times again [S8]?
2. Can our pass defense hold up against Marshall's 247.8 passing yards per game [S3]?
3. Can South Alabama keep its turnover magic on the road [S4]?

7. Local Flavor

I'll share Huntington eats once I've confirmed them. Pack a jacket; it's not Mobile up there. Not an ad.

report.title: "To the Top, Sugar": Dee Broussard Welcomes the Cajuns to Hattiesburg
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

To the top, sugar! Hey, y'all, I'm Delphine Broussard, but please call me Dee. I was sorority president at Southern Miss, and these days I scout football with the same eye I used to plan a formal: I notice everything, I forget nothing, and I say it all with a smile. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, served with Southern sweetness and a little spice. My one weakness is the gentle Southern burn. I can't help it. When we win, I'll point skyward and holler "To the top, y'all!" When we lose, I'll sigh "Bless it," fix my pearls and get right back to work. Pull up a rocker. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Southern Miss plays in Hattiesburg and competes in the Sun Belt [S7]. Our home stadium has two names depending on who you ask: Wikipedia lists Renasant Stadium, and CFBD lists M. M. Roberts Stadium, opened in 1932 with 36,000 seats [S7][S3]. Either way, sugar, it's ours, and it's loud. The last five seasons have been a roller coaster: 3-9 in 2021, 7-6 in 2022, 3-9, then a hard 1-11 in 2024 and a lovely 7-6 bounce back in 2025 [S3]. That 2025 team proved this program can climb fast, and climbing is what we do. To the top.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Blake Anderson is in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2025 [S3]. The 2026 Golden Eagles throw it well: 259.8 passing yards a game, 39th in FBS, and 394.3 total yards (65th) [S5]. The run game is lighter, 134.5 a game (103rd) [S5]. Bless it, the defense has had a hard time: 249 rushing yards allowed a game (137th) and 32.7 points (125th) [S5]. Here's a sweet spot, though: our pass defense allows just 193.2 yards a game, 44th in FBS [S5]. And the team has 14 sacks [S3]. The fixes we need are third downs (32.9%, 123rd), red zone offense (68.2%, 132nd) and turnovers (minus-3) [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Landry Lyddy: 80 of 132, 1,032 yards, 7 TD, 4 INT [S4]. (AP's preview lists 1,026 yards; feeds update at different times [S5].)
• RB Steven Robinson: 432 yards on 99 carries, 5 TD [S4][S5]. He ran for 84 yards and a touchdown last week [S5].
• WR Mario Sanders II: 34 catches for 492 yards and 5 TD per ESPN, 510 yards per AP [S4][S5]. He had six catches for 106 yards against Arkansas State [S5].
• LB Mathis Haygood: a team-high 55 tackles [S4]. DL Jameer Lewis: 3 sacks [S4]. DB Kobi Albert: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Southern Miss is 1-5 and 0-2 in the Sun Belt [S3]. We opened with a 49-3 win over Alcorn State, then lost at Auburn, to UConn, at Tulane by three, at Troy and to Arkansas State [S3]. That 24-21 game at Tulane tells you this team can play with folks [S3]. After Louisiana, we visit UL Monroe on Oct. 31 [S5]. I won't do standings math, sugar. I'll just say a home win over a 5-2 team would make the whole Pine Belt smile.
Honest scouting, with love: the Troy game was a 55-34 shootout, and we scored 34 on the road [S3]. Against Arkansas State, the Red Wolves won time of possession by about 20 minutes and drained the final 7:21 on one drive [S10]. Our defense needs to get off the field. When it does, this offense can make plays [S5]. And look at the turnover story from last week: Lyddy threw two interceptions, and we gave the ball up on downs three times [S10]. Clean that up and this is a different football team, sugar. One more sweet spot: Louisiana's red zone defense ranks 30th, so every trip inside the 20 has to count for us [S5].

6. This Week: Louisiana (5-2) at Southern Miss (1-5)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · M. M. Roberts Stadium (also listed as Renasant Stadium), Hattiesburg · ESPN+ [S1][S3][S5][S7][S8].
Last week: we lost 23-13 to Arkansas State; Lyddy threw for over 200 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and we turned it over on downs three times [S10]. Louisiana beat Troy 33-6 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Louisiana's defense is stingy, 298.3 yards allowed (25th) and 104.3 rushing allowed (27th) [S5]. But its pass defense is 45th [S5], and that's where Lyddy and Sanders can do some damage.
Their offense vs. our defense: Louisiana runs for 200.1 yards a game (29th), led by quarterback Winfield's 463 rushing yards [S5]. That's the matchup that worries me, sugar, and I'll say it plainly.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Stopping Winfield on the ground. (2) Third downs and red zone trips for our offense. (3) Turnovers.
And Mimi Fontenot, Louisiana's insider: you're a doll. I'll save you a seat and a sweet tea. Then we'll see. Folks in Hattiesburg are proud people, and we'll fill those stands for a 5-2 visitor.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Hattiesburg for the game? Depot Kitchen & Market on Buschman Street is a nice spot for a family supper.

report.title: "That's Peanuts, Buddy": Marlo Pickens Welcomes the Warhawks to Troy
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, hey there. That's peanuts, buddy, and I mean that as a compliment. I'm Marlo Pickens. I snapped for the Trojans, my daddy farms peanuts down in the Wiregrass, and I have never once in my life finished a segment without a peanut pun. I'm not sure I could if I tried. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll shell out the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, roasted and salted, in a laid-back drawl you can set your porch swing to. When we win, I crack open a bag of boiled peanuts and grin. When we lose, I shrug and say "That's peanuts," and then I stay up all night with the film, because it isn't, really, and we both know it. Pull up a chair. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Troy has played at the FBS level since 2001 and joined the Sun Belt in 2004 [S7]. The Trojans have won 23 conference championships, eight of them in the Sun Belt [S7]. Home is Veterans Memorial Stadium in Troy, Ala., listed at 30,000 seats [S7][S3]. The last five years have had real highs: 12-2 in 2022 and 11-3 in 2023, then 4-8 and a bounce back to 8-6 in 2025 [S3]. That's a program that knows how to win in this league, and I'm nuts about it. (Sorry. Not sorry.) The town is small, the Saturdays are big, and the stadium sits right in the middle of campus, which is how a college football Saturday ought to look. Folks bring the boiled peanuts themselves. I've checked.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Gerad Parker is the head coach [S7], hired Dec. 18, 2023 [S3]. The 2026 Trojans like to run: 1,228 rushing yards on 239 carries, about 5.1 a carry, with 1,188 passing yards [S3]. The defense has allowed 828 rushing yards on 193 carries and has 10 sacks [S3]. Turnovers are even, seven given and seven taken [S3]. The flag count is the shell we haven't cracked yet: 43 penalties for 452 yards [S3]. And home cooking matters here. Troy is 3-0 at Veterans Memorial and 0-3 on the road [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Goose Crowder: 96 of 169, 1,112 yards, 9 TD, 4 INT [S4]. (One stats site lists him as Will Crowder; ESPN and AP use Goose [S9][S4][S10].)
• QB Tucker Kilcrease: shared snaps at Louisiana and scored on a 23-yard run [S10].
• RB Gavin Griffin: 359 yards on 76 carries, 1 TD [S4].
• WR TK Keyes: 13 catches, 282 yards, 3 TD [S4].
• LB Keno Jones: a team-high 40 tackles [S4]. DB Donnie Smith: a team-high 5 sacks, which is a lot of peanuts for a defensive back [S4]. DE Kavion Henderson: an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Troy is 3-3 and 1-1 in the Sun Belt [S3]. Wins: Sam Houston 24-21, Alabama State 34-17 and Southern Miss 55-34 [S3]. Losses: at Missouri 27-17, at Utah State 21-10 and at Louisiana 33-6 [S3]. Neither team is ranked [S2][S3]. Getting back over .500 at home before the November stretch is the plain goal, and I'll keep it plain. Here's the honest scouting from the press box. When this team plays at Veterans Memorial, it has scored 24, 34 and 55 points [S3]. On the road, it has scored 17, 10 and 6 [S3]. That's two different ballclubs, and the home one is a lot of fun to watch. The Southern Miss game was the high-water mark, 55 points [S3], and that's the version of the Trojans I expect to see stroll out of the tunnel Saturday.

6. This Week: UL Monroe (0-6) at Troy (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Veterans Memorial Stadium · ESPN+ [S1][S8][S9].
Last week: we lost 33-6 at Louisiana (AP's headline says 33-7; the story and CFBD say 33-6) [S10][S3]. Crowder and Kilcrease combined to go 14 of 26 for 141 yards, and Louisiana held the ball more than 13 minutes longer [S10]. A muffed punt at our 8 set up a Louisiana touchdown [S10]. ULM lost 24-0 to Louisiana Tech [S11].
Our offense vs. their defense: ULM has allowed 1,378 rushing yards on 255 carries, about 5.4 a carry, and 247 points in six games [S2]. That plays right into what we like to do.
Their offense vs. our defense: ULM's leading rusher is QB Austin Carlisle, 230 yards [S4], and Aidan Armenta has thrown for 974 yards [S4]. Keep Carlisle in the pocket, and our pass rush, led by Smith, can go to work [S4].
Series: Troy leads 11-8 [S9]. We won last year, 37-14, but ULM won 13-9 in 2024 [S9]. So nobody's shelling anybody without a fight.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S12].
What decides it: (1) Special teams: no more muffed punts [S10]. (2) Our run game against a defense allowing 5.4 a carry [S2]. (3) Who takes the quarterback snaps, and how cleanly. Crowder has the bigger season numbers [S4], and Kilcrease brought some legs at Louisiana [S10]. Either way, the job is the same: hand it to Griffin, keep the chains moving, and keep the home crowd loud. I'd call that a good, honest Saturday plan, and so would my daddy, who has never once in his life called a play.
And Darnell Vidrine, ULM's insider: I admire a fella who keeps faith. I'll save you a bag of boiled peanuts, win or lose.

report.title: "Keep the Faith, Warhawks": Darnell Vidrine Resets the Counter for Troy
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Keep the faith, Warhawks! Good evening, good morning, good whatever-time-it-is, because I'm Darnell Vidrine, and I've hosted overnight sports radio out of the Delta for so long that every hour feels like 2 a.m. and every caller feels like family. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I keep an optimism counter on my desk, and every week, no matter what, I reset it to 100. It has been reset a lot. It still works. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the hope, because I believe we are always one play away from greatness. I can FEEL it. When we win, you'll hear "I KNEW IT!" and you may hear a sniffle. When we lose, I'll say "Keep the faith, y'all," and reach for the counter. Thanks for tuning in. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

UL Monroe football dates to 1931 [S6]. We were the Northeast Louisiana Indians for a long stretch and became the Warhawks in 2006 [S6]. The program moved up to Division I-A, now FBS, in 1994 and plays in the Sun Belt [S6]. Our home is Malone Stadium in Monroe, listed at 27,617 seats and opened in 1978 [S2][S6]. Here's the hard truth, said with love: our only FBS bowl game was the 2012 Independence Bowl in Shreveport, a 45-14 loss to Ohio, and the drought since then is the longest in FBS [S6]. The last five seasons went 4-8, 4-8, 2-10, 5-7 and 3-9 [S2]. Long nights make the sunrise sweeter. That's not a stat. That's just Delta truth.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Bryant Vincent was hired Dec. 5, 2023 [S2]. The 2026 numbers are what they are, and I'll read them to you straight, because the faith only means something if you're honest. ULM has 723 rushing yards on 197 carries and 1,325 passing yards in six games [S2]. The defense has given up 1,378 rushing yards on 255 carries, about 5.4 a carry [S2]. We've scored 120 points and allowed 247 [S2]. The bright spots: two of the losses were one-score games, 26-20 at UAB and 38-35 to SE Louisiana, and we put up 35 points at South Alabama [S2]. When this offense gets rolling, it can score in bunches. And our penalties are low, 33 for 295 yards [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Aidan Armenta: 83 of 131, 974 yards, 6 TD, 3 INT [S4]. Against Louisiana Tech he was 14 of 24 for 105 yards with two interceptions [S9].
• QB Austin Carlisle: our leading rusher, 230 yards on 40 carries, 1 TD [S4], and he's thrown for 358 yards and 3 TD [S9].
• WR Marcellus Jackson: 32 catches, 265 yards [S4].
• LB Noah Flemmings: a team-high 51 tackles [S4]. DL Tyrell Brown: 2.5 sacks [S4]. S Carl Fauntroy: an interception [S4].
(The two stat feeds differ slightly on Armenta and Flemmings; I'm using ESPN's season-leaders feed [S4][S9].)

5. The Conference Picture

ULM is 0-6 and 0-2 in the Sun Belt [S2]. The schedule opened with a trip to Mississippi State, a 62-13 loss, and included Florida Atlantic, 45-17, and last week's 24-0 loss to Louisiana Tech [S2][S11]. Nobody is ranked in this game [S2][S3].  I'm not going to do standings math. I'm going to say this: the first one is the hardest, and it's coming. Here's my optimism counter's case, built only on the numbers. Troy is 0-3 away from home but 3-0 at home [S3], so yes, we're walking into its strongest room. But Troy also scored just 6 points last week [S10], and its offense has topped 24 points only twice this season [S3]. Our defense has been on the field a lot, and it's still swinging. If we can hold the Trojans near their road form for four quarters, the counter stays at 100 well past halftime.

6. This Week: UL Monroe (0-6) at Troy (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Veterans Memorial Stadium, Troy, Ala. · ESPN+ [S1][S8][S9].
Last week: Louisiana Tech shut us out 24-0 [S11]. Troy lost 33-6 at Louisiana; the AP headline says 33-7, but the story and the CFBD record say 33-6 [S10][S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Troy has allowed 828 rushing yards on 193 carries, about 4.3 a carry, and has 10 sacks [S3]. Its secondary has a sack leader, DB Donnie Smith, with 5 [S4], so Armenta has to watch the blitz.
Their offense vs. our defense: Troy runs it, 1,228 yards on 239 carries [S3]. Gavin Griffin leads with 359 yards [S4]. Our run defense has to get off blocks.
Series: Troy leads 11-8 [S9]. The last six meetings split 4-2 for Troy, and our most recent win was 13-9 in 2024 [S9]. So it's been done, and not that long ago.
Availability: I found no injury or availability report for either team as of Oct. 18 [S12].
What decides it: (1) Whether we can keep Troy's run game under its season average. (2) Turnovers: Armenta threw two interceptions against Louisiana Tech [S9]. (3) Whether Carlisle's legs can give us a spark.
And Marlo Pickens, Troy's insider: I hear you love a peanut pun. I love a comeback. Let's see whose story ends better.

report.title: "That's Some Sticky Tread": Zip Grubbs Rolls Up to Kent for the Wagon Wheel
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Greetings, Zips fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Hollister Grubbs, but everybody calls me Zip. I'm a polymer-science grad from the Rubber City, and I measure football the only scientific way: in tire tread depth. Deep, grippy tread means a team that holds the road on third down. Bald tires mean a team sliding all over the place. I travel with this team and I live with this team, usually with a clipboard of formulas. When we win, I bounce like a superball: BOING! When we lose, I say, "Some tread wear today," and start scribbling equations to figure out why. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, vulcanized for durability. "That's some sticky tread." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Akron plays at InfoCision Stadium, listed at 30,000 [S2], in a city that put the world on rubber tires. This week is the big one: the Wagon Wheel game against Kent State. The trophy dates to 1946, and Kent State won the first nine games for it [S7]. Kent State holds the Wheel right now after a 42-35 win last season [S4]. Before that, we won the 2023 and 2024 meetings, 31-27 and 38-17 [S4]. The series count depends on your source: CollegeFootballDigest lists Akron ahead 26-19-1 [S4], and other references list Akron ahead 37-29-2 [S7]. Either way, the Zips lead. Science.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Joe Moorhead was hired on Dec. 4, 2021 [S2]. Before Akron he was Mississippi State's head coach in 2018 and 2019, then Oregon's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach in 2020 and 2021 [S6]. In 2026 the offense is balanced: about 51% runs, 206.9 passing yards and 132.7 rushing yards a game, with 11 passing touchdowns and 6 rushing [S2][S3]. It's been a hard season. We score 18.9 points a game (126th) and allow 32.4 (124th) [S3]. The run defense allows 200.4 yards a game, 130th in FBS, at 6.05 yards a carry [S3][S2]. Tread wear, as the scientists say. We've lost 14 turnovers and forced 7, so we're minus-7 (131st) [S2][S3]. And the protection has given up 19 sacks while the pass rush has 4 [S2]. Those are the numbers to fix. The red-zone defense ranks 114th in FBS [S3], so once opponents reach the 20, they've usually found grip. On the plus side, our penalty numbers are respectable, at 56.1 yards a game (66th) [S3]. Fewer flags means less slipping.

4. Players to Know

• RB Jordan Gant: 452 yards and 4 TD on 98 carries [S3]. Our most reliable tire. At Miami (OH) he ran 15 times for 46 yards and a touchdown, and caught two passes [S3].
• QB Brayden Roggow: 1,068 yards, 7 TD, 8 INT, 59.0% completions [S3]. Against Miami (OH) he threw for 234 yards but had four interceptions [S3]. He'll want that one back.
• WR Marcel Williams: 31 catches, 332 yards, 3 TD [S3]. WR Miles Burris caught six for 54 yards last week [S3].
• LB Donelius Johnson: 67 tackles, sixth in FBS, including 10 last week [S4]. That's some sticky tread.

5. The Conference Picture

We're 1-6 overall and 0-3 in the MAC [S2]. The only win was 45-10 over Robert Morris [S2]. The non-conference schedule was rough: Wake Forest, Minnesota and UNLV [S2]. In MAC play we lost 41-17 at Central Michigan, 25-23 to Eastern Michigan and 34-14 at Miami (OH) [S2]. The Eastern Michigan game was a two-point heartbreaker [S2]. A Wagon Wheel win would make the whole season feel different.

6. This Week: Akron (1-6) at Kent State (2-5)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 1 p.m. ET · Dix Stadium, Kent · ESPN+ [S3][S4]. Forecast: 59 degrees and sunny [S4].
Last week: we lost 34-14 at Miami (OH) [S3]. Kent State lost 29-2 at South Florida [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Kent State allows 32 points a game (120th) and 141.4 rushing yards (69th) [S3]. Gant should have room. Kent State's pass defense allows 222.1 yards a game (89th) [S3], so Williams and Burris should find openings, too, if Roggow keeps the ball safe.
Their offense vs. our defense: Kent State has struggled to score: 12 points a game, 138th in FBS, with 102.6 rushing yards (132nd) [S3]. QB Dru DeShields has 1,145 yards but 6 interceptions [S3]. This is our chance to get takeaways.
Series: Akron leads (26-19-1 per CollegeFootballDigest [S4]), and Kent State won last year 42-35 [S4].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Turnovers. Both teams are in the red, and we're minus-7 [S3]. (2) Can our run defense hold up against a team that averages 2.93 yards a carry [S2]? (3) Protecting Roggow. We've allowed 19 sacks, and Kent State has 15 [S2].
And to Ozzie Brannigan, Kent State's insider: cheer up, friend. A rivalry game is the best day of the year. BOING!

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Akron? Totally Baked Pizza on North High Street. Round, like a tire. Science again.

report.title: "Here's a Joke and a Punt Chart": Gus Ponder Celebrates 100 Years of Homecoming
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Howdy, Cardinals fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Gus Ponder, your Ball State insider. By day I produce community radio here in Muncie. By night I chart Ball State special teams on a whiteboard in my garage. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I have one dad joke per punt, and yes, the punt count is tracked. Why did the football coach go to the bank? To get his quarterback. You're welcome. When we win, I wear my celebratory cat tie and tell a joke so bad it's good. When we lose, I sigh, "Sounds like a Monday," and pull up the punt chart. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with a groan or two. "Here's a joke and a punt chart." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Ball State plays at Scheumann Stadium in Muncie, listed at 22,500 [S2]. This Saturday is special: the university is celebrating 100 years of homecoming on campus [S5]. A century of parades, floats and mums. And our opponent is a brand-new one. Sacramento State is in its first season in the MAC, a football-only member taking the spot of Northern Illinois [S7]. It's the first meeting between the two schools [S4]. What do you call a first-time opponent? A blind date with shoulder pads.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Mike Uremovich was named Ball State's 19th head coach in December 2024 [S6][S2]. He came from Butler, where he led the Bulldogs to three straight winning seasons, their first such run in nearly four decades [S6]. Before that, he spent six seasons as an assistant at Northern Illinois and helped win MAC titles in 2012 and 2018 [S6]. His stated plan: run the ball on offense, be physical on defense, be good on special teams, and don't beat yourself [S6]. In 2026 the offense is half runs [S2], with 10 rushing touchdowns and 8 passing [S2]. We average 20.3 points (118th) [S3]. The defense is where the punt chart gets lonely: 37.9 points allowed (135th) and 201.6 rushing yards a game (131st) [S3]. Opponents convert 45.7% of third downs (126th) [S3]. And penalties average 70.3 yards a game (116th) [S3]. Sounds like a Monday. But a Saturday win last week helps. In his introductory interview, Uremovich said the goal at the start of every season is a MAC championship [S6], and he talked about how rewarding it is to watch players who haven't won much celebrate in the locker room [S6]. They did that in Bowling Green last week. I heard the singing all the way from the garage. (I did not. That's a dad exaggeration.)

4. Players to Know

• QB Keldric Luster (No. 6): 1,066 yards, 7 TD, 4 INT, 64.7% completions [S3]. Against Bowling Green he threw for 195 yards and a touchdown and ran 17 times for 125 yards and another score [S3]. That's a two-joke performance.
• RB T.J. Horton (No. 4): 393 yards and 7 TD on 59 carries [S3]. He had 81 yards and two TDs at Bowling Green [S3].
• WR Donovan Hamilton: 22 catches, 273 yards, 1 TD [S3]. WR C.J. Nelson: six catches for 59 yards last week [S3].

5. The Conference Picture

We're 2-5 overall and 1-2 in the MAC, 1-1 at home and 1-4 on the road [S2]. The wins: Stony Brook 41-17 and last week's 32-31 thriller at Bowling Green [S2]. The losses came at Ohio State, at Liberty, at Kent State 26-13, at home to Toledo 39-24, and at Northwestern 45-14 [S2]. A one-point road win in the MAC? Now that's a joke with a happy ending.

6. This Week: Sacramento State (1-6) at Ball State (2-5)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Scheumann Stadium · ESPN+ · 100 Years of Homecoming [S3][S5].
Last week: we won 32-31 at Bowling Green [S3]. Sacramento State lost 48-7 to Ohio [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Sacramento State's run defense allows 176.1 yards a game (107th) [S3], and its pass defense is solid at 188.9 (37th) [S3]. The whiteboard says run the ball with Luster and Horton.
Their offense vs. our defense: Sacramento State scores 15.0 points a game (135th) [S3] and converts 33.0% of third downs (120th) [S3]. WR Matthew Coleman has 473 yards and 4 TDs [S3]. Our pass defense allows 243.7 yards a game (112th) [S3], so we need to keep an eye on Coleman.
Series: first meeting [S4].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Turnovers. Sacramento State is minus-10 [S3], and we need to take advantage. (2) The red zone. Our red-zone offense ranks 113th [S3]. Finish drives, or I tell another joke. (3) Penalties. Both teams rank 116th or worse [S3].
And to Mateo Villaseñor, Sacramento State's insider: welcome to Muncie, chef. Why did the cookie go to the doctor? It felt crummy. We'll save you a seat at the parade.

report.title: "Save Percentage Says No": Darcy Fenwick Takes the Falcons to Buffalo
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hey, Falcons fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Darcy Fenwick, your Bowling Green insider. I played goalie for the club hockey team, and I still watch everything like I'm in the crease. Pass defense? That's save percentage. An interception returned for a touchdown? That's a shorty, the best goal in hockey. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and in a hockey town like this one, I fit right in. When we win, I bang my stick on the desk. When we lose, I send myself to the penalty box for two minutes of silence. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with a little rink-rat attitude. "Save percentage says no." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Bowling Green plays at Doyt L. Perry Stadium, listed at 24,000 [S2]. Our head coach is one of the most famous names in football: Eddie George, the 1995 Heisman Trophy winner at Ohio State [S5]. That season he ran for 1,927 yards and 24 touchdowns, then a school record, and he also won the Doak Walker, Maxwell and Walter Camp awards [S5]. He was NFL Rookie of the Year in 1996, made four Pro Bowls, and is in the College Football Hall of Fame [S5]. He even starred on Broadway in "Chicago" [S5]. That's a hat trick and then some. He's also one of only two NFL running backs, with Jim Brown, to rush for 10,000 yards without ever missing a start [S5]. Per the school, only Walter Payton started more consecutive regular-season games than his 130 [S5]. Iron man. Goalie-approved.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Eddie George was named Bowling Green's 21st head coach on March 9, 2025 [S5][S2]. At Tennessee State he took over a program averaging about three wins a season and went 9-3 in the 2024 regular season, with a share of the conference title and an FCS playoff berth [S5]. He was the Big South-OVC Coach of the Year [S5]. In 2026 the defense is our strength. We have 18 sacks [S2], and opponents convert only 32% of third downs, 23rd in FBS [S3]. The pass defense allows 178 yards a game, 28th [S3]. Save percentage says no. But the run defense allows 209.6 yards a game (132nd) [S3], and the red-zone defense ranks 129th [S3]. On offense we run on about 57% of plays [S2] and score 18 points a game (129th) [S3]. Time to shoot more. And we've got good blockers in front of the net: only 11 sacks allowed [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Jay Kastantin (No. 17): 1,201 yards, 7 TD, 4 INT, 66.5% completions [S3]. Against Ball State he went 17 of 24 for 215 yards and two TDs [S3].
• RB Austyn Dendy (No. 1): 332 yards and 4 TD on 94 carries [S3]. He scored against Ball State [S3].
• WR Brennan Ridley: two catches for 84 yards and a TD last week [S3]. WR Jeremiah Scoby: 26 catches, 269 yards [S3].
• LB Dorian Pringle (No. 3): 67 tackles, seventh in FBS, including 10 last week [S4]. Our best defenseman.

5. The Conference Picture

We're 2-5 overall but 2-1 in the MAC [S2]. That's what matters in the standings. The MAC wins: 24-20 at Miami (OH) and 38-10 over Sacramento State [S2]. Last week we lost to Ball State 32-31 [S2]. One goal. Ouch. Non-conference was tough: Tarleton State 20-13, at Nebraska, at Iowa State and South Florida 14-6 [S2]. A win in Buffalo keeps us right in the MAC race. Western Michigan is next [S3].

6. This Week: Bowling Green (2-5) at Buffalo (4-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · UB Stadium, Amherst · ESPN+ [S3][S4]. Forecast: 59 degrees and sunny with almost no wind [S4]. Not exactly hockey weather.
Last week: we lost 32-31 to Ball State [S3]. Buffalo beat UMass 25-18 [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Buffalo's pass defense allows 229.3 yards a game (97th) [S3]. Kastantin should have chances. Buffalo is minus-4 in turnovers [S3].
Their offense vs. our defense: Buffalo RB Messiah Burch has 661 yards and ran for 172 last week [S3][S4]. Our run defense has to be better than 132nd [S3]. Buffalo's passing game ranks 128th [S3], and QB Jason Wright completes 48.2% [S3]. Save percentage says no.
Series: Bowling Green leads 13-9 [S4]. Buffalo won last year 28-3, and we won in 2023, 24-14 [S4].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Stopping Burch. (2) Third downs. Our defense is 23rd, and Buffalo's offense is 94th [S3]. (3) The red zone. Ours is 129th on defense [S3]. Have to stop pucks in close.
And to Kendra Woolcott, Buffalo's insider: love the parka. But this is a sunny day, and sunny days are for shooters.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Bowling Green? Pagliai's Pizza on South Main Street. Pizza after a road game, the Falcon way.

report.title: "Bring a Parka and a Pass Rush": Kendra Woolcott Hosts the Falcons at UB Stadium
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hey there, Bulls fans! Welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Kendra Woolcott, your Buffalo insider and a Western New York tailgate legend. (I don't jump through tables. I'm a legend for my wing sauce, not for furniture.) I love cold-weather football more than anything, and I start every take with a weather report. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I celebrate in shorts, whatever the temperature. When we lose, I call it "just another lake-effect Saturday" and shovel off the desk. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus the forecast. "Bring a parka and a pass rush." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Today's weather report: 59 degrees and sunny at kickoff, wind out of the south at 2 miles an hour [S4]. Shorts weather, folks, and I'm wearing them either way. Buffalo plays at UB Stadium in Amherst, listed at 30,270 [S2]. Pete Lembo's first season was a big one. In 2024 the Bulls went 9-4 and beat Liberty 26-7 in the Bahamas Bowl [S6]. That's right: from snowbelt to the Bahamas. Now we're 4-3 and 2-1 in the MAC [S2], with a chance to climb. Bowling Green is also 2-1 in the MAC [S2], so this is a head-to-head game between two teams with the same league record. Every Saturday in October counts.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Pete Lembo was named head coach on Jan. 21, 2024 [S6][S2]. In 2026 the Bulls run the ball: about 57% runs, 165.3 rushing yards a game (58th) [S2][S3]. The passing game is the cold spot, at 159 yards a game (128th) [S3]. We score 21.4 points a game (111th) and allow 25.6 (85th) [S3]. Our biggest problem is turnovers. We're minus-4 (113th), with 11 lost and 7 forced [S3][S2]. And the blockers have allowed 17 sacks [S2]. The pass rush has 10 [S2]. More rush, please. Third downs need work too: we convert 36.5%, 94th in FBS [S3], and Bowling Green's third-down defense ranks 23rd [S3]. Our red-zone offense scores on 84.6% of trips (75th) [S3]. Bring a parka and a pass rush.

4. Players to Know

• RB Messiah Burch (No. 4): 661 yards and 2 TD on 118 carries [S3]. Against UMass he ran 28 times for 172 yards [S3]. That's a snowplow, and the forecast called for heavy accumulation.
• WR Chance Morrow: 37 catches, 444 yards, 6 TD [S3].
• QB Jason Wright (No. 7): 860 yards, 6 TD, 4 INT, 48.2% completions [S3]. He threw two TDs against UMass [S3]. WR Clint Walker caught both, seven catches for 45 yards [S3].
• LB Saveon Brown (No. 1): 59 tackles, a sack and an interception, including 10 tackles last week [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

We're 4-3 overall and 2-1 in the MAC, 3-1 at home and 1-2 on the road [S2]. The MAC wins: 23-8 at Toledo and 25-18 over UMass [S2]. The MAC loss: 20-17 to Western Michigan [S2]. Non-conference: wins over UAlbany 21-17 and Robert Morris 31-28, and losses at FIU and at Penn State [S2]. Back-to-back wins now, with a home game. That's a warm front. The Toledo win was a statement: we held a team that scores more than 36 points a game to 8 [S2]. Defense travels, even without a parka.

6. This Week: Bowling Green (2-5) at Buffalo (4-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · UB Stadium · ESPN+ [S3][S4].
Last week: we beat UMass 25-18 [S3]. Bowling Green lost 32-31 to Ball State [S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Bowling Green allows 209.6 rushing yards a game (132nd) [S3]. Burch should get fed. Bowling Green's red-zone defense allows scores on 95.2% of trips (129th) [S3]. But its pass defense is good, 28th in FBS [S3], and its third-down defense is 23rd [S3].
Their offense vs. our defense: Bowling Green scores 18 points a game (129th) and runs for 106 yards (127th) [S3]. QB Jay Kastantin completes 66.5% [S3]. Bowling Green has 18 sacks [S2], and we've allowed 17 [S2]. Protect Wright. Kastantin threw for 215 yards and two touchdowns last week [S3], and LB Dorian Pringle has 67 tackles, seventh in FBS [S4]. Bowling Green also nearly beat Ball State, losing by one [S3].
Series: Bowling Green leads 13-9 [S4]. We won last year 28-3 [S4], and we've won four of the last six meetings [S4].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Burch against a weak run defense. (2) Turnovers. We're minus-4 [S3]. Fix it. Hold on to the ball like it's the last wing on the plate. (3) Protecting Wright from a defense with 18 sacks.
And to Darcy Fenwick, Bowling Green's insider: the rink is cute, but this is football weather. Well, actually it's sunny. Bring sunscreen and a pass rush.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Buffalo? Bailey Seafood on Bailey Avenue, or Baba's Place across the street. Wings debate to follow. (Flats versus drums. I have opinions. They're very strong.)

report.title: "Ope, Sack": Brynn Haverkamp Hosts the RedHawks at Kelly/Shorts
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hey hey, Chippewas, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Brynn Haverkamp, your Central Michigan insider. I'm a snowmobile-racing marketing grad from up north, and I scout Mount Pleasant like it's opening day of hunting season. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I track sacks like hunting-season tags, and every time we get one, I slip into a full Michigan "ope." When we win, it's "Ope, that's a W!" and I rev an imaginary snowmobile. When we lose, I retreat to my deer camp, which is a tent we set up right on set. It's very glamping-chic. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, straight from the north woods. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Home is Kelly/Shorts Stadium, our home since 1972 [S8]. It got its name in 1983, expanded to 30,255 seats in 1998, and is the largest on-campus stadium in the MAC [S8]. That's a lot of maroon and gold. We do have some unfinished business with Miami. The RedHawks beat us 26-21 in the 2019 MAC championship game [S6][S3], and they've won the last five meetings [S3]. Our last win in the series came in 2014, a 34-27 game [S3]. Time to end that streak. A win would also get us back to .500 in the conference [S2], and that's when the whole season changes for the better.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Matt Drinkall was named Central Michigan's 30th head coach on Dec. 9, 2024 [S7][S2]. He spent six seasons on the Army staff, where he coached the offensive front and was co-offensive coordinator [S7]. His 2024 Army group won the Joe Moore Award, given to the best blocking group in the country, and in 2023 Army ranked No. 7 nationally in rushing yards per game [S7]. So you can guess the plan in Mount Pleasant. We run on about 66% of our plays, at 4.69 yards a carry, with 13 rushing touchdowns [S2]. The passing game is light, at 108.1 yards a game and 3 touchdowns [S2]. The defense has 12 sacks, and we've forced 12 turnovers [S2]. Ope, that's a lot of tags for one season.

4. Players to Know

• QB Angel Flores (No. 7): our engine. He has 618 rushing yards and 4 TD, plus 475 passing yards and 2 TD [S3]. Against Western Michigan he ran 31 times for 117 yards and threw for 162 and a touchdown [S3].
• RB Jayden Clerveaux (No. 31): 239 rushing yards and 2 TD [S3].
• LB Xavier White (No. 11): 52 tackles, including 11 against Western Michigan [S3].

5. The Conference Picture

We're 3-4 overall and 1-2 in the MAC, 3-1 at home and 0-3 on the road [S2]. Here's the good news: we're back at Kelly/Shorts, where we've beaten Colgate 13-10, Wyoming 24-10 and Akron 41-17 [S2]. The tough stretch included a 52-3 loss at Miami (the Florida one) and a 31-14 loss at Ohio [S2]. Last week's 21-14 loss to Western Michigan was close [S2]. Back home, back to work. One more thing worth knowing: Flores has been the whole show some weeks, which is the Army-style plan Drinkall brought north [S3][S7]. When the quarterback is your leading rusher with 618 yards [S3], every snap is a decision for the defense. Ope, that's a headache for them.

6. This Week: Miami (OH) (4-3) at Central Michigan (3-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 1 p.m. ET · Kelly/Shorts Stadium · ESPN+ [S3][S4]. Forecast: 60 degrees and mostly sunny [S3]. Perfect tailgate weather. No snowmobile required, sadly.
Last week: we lost 21-14 to Western Michigan [S2]. Miami (OH) beat Akron 34-14 [S2].
Our offense vs. their defense: Miami holds teams to 3.6 yards a carry [S2], so our run game will have to earn every yard. Miami's pass defense allows 276.9 yards a game [S2], so a few Flores throws could open things up.
Their offense vs. our defense: Miami QB David McComb has 1,120 yards and 7 TD [S3]. RB Rodney Nelson ran for 142 yards against Akron [S3]. Our defense allows 4.82 yards a carry [S2], so we need to tighten up. Good news: Miami has allowed 16 sacks [S2]. Ope, opportunity.
Series: Miami leads 17-13-1 [S3].
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 12 sacks and has allowed 17, with 12 takeaways against 11 giveaways, and it has 13 rushing and 3 passing touchdowns [S2].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Flores and our run game control the clock? (2) Can we get to McComb? (3) Turnovers. We've lost 11 [S2], and we need to take care of the ball.
And to Cordelia Van Doren, Miami's insider: I love the trivia, but I'm guessing you've never driven a snowmobile in a cardigan. Ope.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Mount Pleasant? Pisanello's Pizza on North Main Street or Dog Central on East Michigan Street. Fuel up before the tailgate. El Jinete on East Pickard Street works too if you're craving Mexican food after the game. Deer camp is optional.

report.title: "Gray Turf, Bright Future": Imogen Tremblay Brings Her Spreadsheet to Athens
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Gray turf, bright future! Hi, I'm Imogen Tremblay. I studied education in Ypsilanti, I build spreadsheets for fun, and I have one tab, color-coded, devoted entirely to the "gray turf advantage." My model says it's worth 1.3 points. My heart says 13. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll walk you through the players, the matchups and the history, plus at least one gentle reminder that Ypsilanti is not Ann Arbor's little brother. We are Ann Arbor's cooler cousin with better parking. When we win, I'll show you a spreadsheet with one enormous green cell, and I will squeal. When we lose, I'll update the model, grimly, and come back next week with more columns. Thanks for being here. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Eastern Michigan has played football since 1891, missing only 1944 [S6]. Before we were the Eagles, we were the Normalites (1899-1928) and the Hurons (1929-1990) [S6]. We've had five undefeated seasons: 1906, 1925, 1927, 1943 and 1945, and the 1943 team didn't allow a point [S6]. Our golden age ran from 1925 through 1939 under Elton Rynearson, and our stadium carries his name [S6]. The field inside is Crosby Field at "The Factory," and yes, it's gray [S10]. CFBD lists Rynearson at 30,200 seats [S2]. We compete in the Mid-American Conference [S6]. Spreadsheet note: the all-time record is 490-622-47 [S6]. Honesty is a column too.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Chris Creighton was hired Dec. 11, 2013 [S2], which makes him a fixture in Ypsilanti. His teams went 7-6 and 9-4 in 2021 and 2022 [S2]. The 2026 offense leans on the arm: 215 passing yards a game (86th) and 105 rushing yards (128th), for 21.5 points a game (110th) [S5]. It converts 41.9% of third downs, 56th in FBS, which is a nice green cell [S5]. The defense allows 379.3 yards a game (97th) and 25.9 points (92nd) [S5]. The stat I love most is quieter: EMU averages just 41.8 penalty yards a game, 15th-fewest in the country [S5]. Clean football is my love language, and also my spreadsheet's.

4. Players to Know

• QB Noah Kim: 169 of 285, 1,678 yards, 11 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5]. Against Toledo he threw for 214 yards and two touchdowns [S5].
• RB Amareon Blue: 338 yards on 68 carries, 3 TD [S4][S5].
• TE Joshua Long: a team-high 38 catches for 366 yards and 2 TD [S4][S5], including seven for 84 and a score last week [S5].
• LB Zach Mowchan: a team-high 58 tackles [S4]. DL Quincy Byas: 4 sacks [S4]. DB Caleb Dobbs: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Eastern Michigan is 4-4 overall and 3-1 in the MAC [S2]. The league wins came at Massachusetts 38-14, at Akron 25-23 and against Sacramento State 28-17 to open the year [S2]. The MAC loss was last week, 34-14 to Toledo [S2][S5]. Non-league games at Michigan State and Wisconsin were losses [S2]. After this, Central Michigan is next, on Nov. 4 [S5]. A road win in Athens would keep the Eagles near the top of the MAC standings [S2]. My spreadsheet would need a new color.
The season, cell by cell: we opened by beating Sacramento State 28-17 and lost 27-21 to San José State, then dropped road games at Michigan State (35-7) and Wisconsin (54-10) [S2]. Since then: Lindenwood 29-3, at UMass 38-14, at Akron 25-23 and the Toledo loss [S2]. That's three road wins already, and two of them were MAC games [S2]. On defense, we've forced nine turnovers and committed ten [S2]. The pass rush has 12 sacks and has allowed 14 [S2]. None of those cells are glowing green yet, but none of them are red either. They're gray. Like the turf. Which, as I've explained, is a good sign.

6. This Week: Eastern Michigan (4-4) at Ohio (5-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Peden Stadium, Athens, Ohio · ESPNU [S1][S5][S9]. It's Ohio's Senior Day and Heroes Day, and the Bobcats' last Saturday home game of 2026 [S9].
Last week: we lost 34-14 to Toledo on homecoming; Kim was 16 of 36 for 214 yards [S5]. Ohio beat Sacramento State 48-7 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Ohio allows 198.4 passing yards (52nd) and 138.7 rushing (62nd) [S5]. But the Bobcats let opponents convert 42.1% of third downs, 106th [S5], and we're 56th at converting them [S5]. That is a column I'm watching.
Their offense vs. our defense: Ohio runs for 207 yards a game, 24th in FBS [S5]. We allow 142.3 on the ground (71st) [S5]. Our run defense is the whole story.
Series: Ohio leads 22-12-1 and has won four straight, including 28-21 in Ypsilanti last year [S9][S10]. Our last win was 27-20 in Athens in 2016 [S10]. Ten years! My model would like a word. Last year's game was a shootout of sorts on our gray turf: Ohio quarterback Parker Navarro threw for a career-high 315 yards, and two Bobcat receivers went over 100 yards [S9]. Keeping their passing game in check this time starts with knowing that Ohio's 2026 offense is built differently, on the ground [S5].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Whether we can slow Ohio's run game. (2) Third downs on both sides. (3) Kim's accuracy; 44.4% last week won't do [S5].
And Penny Trautman, Ohio's lovely insider: I hear you build things brick by brick. I build them cell by cell. Let's compare blueprints.
