report.title: "Thin Air, Thick Defense": Ansel Rimrock Welcomes the Aztecs to Fort Collins
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Thin air, thick defense. Hello, friends, I'm Ansel Rimrock. Most mornings you'll find me on a trail in the foothills west of town, and on fall Saturdays you'll find me with the Rams. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. I'm a calm guy, but don't mistake calm for quiet: I'm competitive right down to my trail shoes. I think football is just a long trail run with blocking. You pace yourself, you climb, you don't panic on the switchbacks, and you finish strong. Fort Collins on a fall Saturday is green and gold from the foothills to the stadium. Visiting teams breathe a little harder up here, and our kids love it. Ram tough, trail ready. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Colorado State Rams compete in the Pac-12 [S7]. Our big rivalries are with Colorado, Wyoming and Air Force [S7]. We've played at Canvas Stadium since 2017; before that, the Rams spent 49 seasons, 1968 to 2016, at Sonny Lubick Field at Hughes Stadium [S7]. CFBD lists Canvas at 36,500 seats [S3]. The last five seasons were a steep climb: 3-9, 3-9, 5-7, a nice 8-5 in 2024 and then 2-10 in 2025 [S3]. Every trail has a hard stretch. We're climbing out of one.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jim Mora was hired on Nov. 26, 2025, and this is his first season [S7]. The offense can move: 445.3 yards a game (34th), 35.7 points (29th) and 274.7 passing yards (26th) [S5]. And we take care of the ball. We've turned it over only 4 times [S3] and taken it away 12 times [S3], good for a plus-8 margin, 6th in FBS [S5]. We play disciplined, 42.3 penalty yards a game (17th) [S5]. Now the hard switchback, friends. The defense is allowing 530.3 yards a game, 274.3 rushing yards and 43.2 points, all 138th in FBS [S5]. I said thick defense. I'm still waiting for the thick part. It'll come.

4. Players to Know

• QB K'saan Farrar: 89 of 144 for 931 yards, 5 TD, 2 INT [S4][S5]. At Texas State he went 26 of 41 for 282 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions [S5].
• RB Brown: 431 yards on just 47 carries, 3 TD. That's more than nine yards a carry [S4][S5]. Heads-up: ESPN lists him as Mel Brown and AP as Jayden Brown; I'm showing both [S4][S5].
• WR Reginald "RJ" Vick Jr.: 24 catches, 367 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. WR Jackson Harper: five catches for 91 yards at Texas State [S5].
• LB Oumar Diomande: team-high 54 tackles [S4]. DL Jack Moran: 1.5 sacks [S4]. CB CJ Blocker: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Colorado State is 2-4 and 0-2 in the Pac-12 [S3]. The season started fast: Wyoming 35-13 in the rivalry, then Southern Utah 58-24 [S3]. Then a tough climb: BYU 41-23, a 59-45 shootout at UTSA, Oregon State 56-26 and at Texas State 66-27 [S3]. After San Diego State, we visit Utah State on Oct. 31 [S5]. I don't do standings math on a trail. I just look at the next switchback.
Season so far, in trail terms: the first two miles were downhill and fast. Then came four straight climbs against BYU, UTSA, Oregon State and Texas State, and the legs got heavy [S3]. Every trail runner knows that feeling. You don't quit at mile four. You drink some water, shorten your stride and keep going.
The good news: beating Wyoming is never a small thing up here [S3]. And scoring 45 at UTSA shows how fast this offense can move [S3].

6. This Week: San Diego State (3-4) at Colorado State (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Mountain) · Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins · The CW [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we lost 66-27 at Texas State on Oct. 15 [S5]. San Diego State beat Fresno State 26-23 on Oct. 17 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: San Diego State allows 449 yards a game (133rd) and 276.6 passing yards (131st) [S5]. Farrar, Vick and Harper should find room up top.
Their offense vs. our defense: San Diego State averages 292.9 yards (133rd) and converts only 29.3% of third downs (135th) [S5]. But it runs it, 144.4 yards a game, and Lucky Sutton ran for 110 last week [S5]. Our run defense has to win this climb.
Ball control: San Diego State's average time of possession is 24:47, 138th in FBS [S5]. We'll have the ball plenty.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Our run defense against Kinnard and Sutton. (2) Farrar against a 131st-ranked pass defense. (3) Our plus-8 turnover habit [S5].
To Kai Delgado-Sorensen, San Diego State's insider: holding your breath under a wave is one thing. Try running a mile at 5,000 feet. I'll lend you a water bottle.

Why I Love This Team

I love that this team keeps hold of the football [S3]. I love that Brown averages more than nine yards a carry [S4]. I love that this is a first-year staff building something [S7]. And I love Fort Collins in late October, when the foothills turn and the stadium fills up. Ram tough, trail ready.

report.title: "Gnarly": Kai Delgado-Sorensen Paddles Out to Fort Collins
report.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen · San Diego State Insider
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Gnarly. Hey, dudes and dudettes, I'm Kai Delgado-Sorensen. I'm out in the water at Ocean Beach most mornings before the sun's all the way up, and I'm at every Aztecs game when it goes down. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. Fair warning: I rate defenses by swell size. A soft defense is ankle-high mush. A great one is a ten-foot wall, totally gnarly. Don't let the surfer drawl fool you, though. I've watched every snap this season, some of them twice, with a notebook full of salt stains. When we win, I yell "Gnarly!" and mime catching a wave. report.title: "Go With the Flow": Yesenia Calderwood Floats the Bobcats Into Week 8
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Eat 'em up, Cats! Hey, y'all, I'm Yesenia Calderwood, and if you can't find me at a Bobcats game, I'm probably floating down the San Marcos River on an inner tube with a sun hat and a radio. I travel with the Bobcats and I live with the Bobcats, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, sunny and laid-back but fiercely proud. San Marcos has a clear, cold river and a hot, rising football team. Grab a tube, grab a seat, and enjoy the ride with us. My motto for life and football: go with the flow, then run it up the middle. When we win, I'm floating on air. When we lose, I let the river carry it away and get ready for next week. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Texas State football began in 1904 and has an overall winning record [S7]. The program has 14 conference titles, nine of them outright [S7]. As of 2026, the Bobcats play in the Pac-12 [S7]. Home games are in San Marcos at the stadium Wikipedia calls UFCU Stadium and CFBD lists as Bobcat Stadium, opened in 1981 with 30,000 seats [S7][S3]. Texas State is now the fourth-largest university in Texas [S7]. And the recent current is strong: 4-8, 4-8, then 8-5, 8-5 and 7-6 [S3]. That's a river rising.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

G.J. Kinne is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 2, 2022 [S3]. His offense is a flash flood, y'all. Texas State leads all of FBS in total offense at 562.3 yards a game [S5]. We run for 303.5 a game, 3rd in the country, and score 40 points a game, 9th [S5]. We convert 56.1% of third downs, 4th [S5]. That's going with the flow, then running it up the middle, over and over. The defense is where the water gets choppy: 297.3 passing yards allowed a game, 137th, and 32.2 points (122nd) [S5]. And our turnover margin is minus-5 [S5]. Here's the thing, though: when an offense moves like this, every possession is a chance to put points on the board. We hold the ball 31:30 a game, 37th in FBS [S5]. Keep the defense rested, keep the river flowing, and good things happen.

4. Players to Know

• QB Brad Jackson: 106 of 157 for 1,439 yards, 14 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. Against Colorado State he went 14 of 19 for 213 yards and a touchdown, and ran 13 times for 181 yards and three more scores [S5]. Whoa, that's a waterfall.
• RB Torrance Burgess Jr.: 838 yards on 108 carries, 5 TD [S4][S5]. Against Colorado State: 224 yards and four touchdowns on 24 carries [S5].
• WR Chris Dawn Jr.: 29 catches, 348 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. Beau Sparks: two catches for 57 yards against the Rams [S5].
• DB Jayden Bradley: team-high 44 tackles [S4]. DL Tymere Jackson: 2.5 sacks [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Texas State is 3-3 and 1-1 in the Pac-12, and 3-1 at home [S3]. We lost at Texas 59-7, then lost to UTSA 31-26 [S3]. Then the current picked up: North Texas 49-35, Incarnate Word 63-10 [S3]. We lost a 31-29 heartbreaker at San Diego State [S3], then beat Colorado State 66-27 [S3]. After Utah State, we go to No. 21 Boise State on Oct. 31 [S5]. No standings math on the river, y'all. Just know a home win keeps us floating.
The close ones: five points against UTSA and two points at San Diego State [S3]. A couple of bounces, and this record looks a lot different.
Season so far, from the tube: the Texas game was cold water, a shock to the system [S3]. Since then, this offense has scored 26, 49, 63, 29 and 66 [S3]. That's a river that keeps rising, and it's the most treasured part of my fall.

6. This Week: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 p.m. Central) · San Marcos · CBS Sports Network [S1][S5][S8].
Our offense vs. their defense: Utah State allows 140.8 rushing yards a game (68th) [S5] and lets opponents convert 40.4% of third downs (93rd) [S5]. Burgess and Jackson should find running room.
Their offense vs. our defense: Utah State scores 14.5 points a game (136th) and gains 310 yards (129th) [S5]. But our pass defense is 137th [S5], and receiver Eli Wood has 472 receiving yards [S5]. We have to keep an eye on him.
Red zone: we've scored on just 71% of our trips, 128th in FBS [S5]. Y'all, that's where we have to finish.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Our run game against a 68th-ranked run defense. (2) Pass defense against Wood. (3) Finishing in the red zone [S5].
To Hyrum Tolleson, Utah State's insider: ice cream and a river float? Now you're speaking my language. Come on down.

Why I Love This Team

I love an offense that leads the country [S5]. I love Burgess running like the river after a storm [S5]. I love that the Bobcats keep rising [S3]. And I love San Marcos on a fall night. Eat 'em up, Cats!

report.title: "Udderly Dominant": Hyrum Tolleson Brings Cache Valley Heart to San Marcos
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Go Aggies! Well, hello there, neighbors. I'm Hyrum Tolleson, and I've spent most of my life on a dairy up in Cache Valley, which is a fancy way of saying I've been up before the sun since I was eight years old. I travel with the Aggies and I live with the Aggies, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, slow and steady, the way you'd tell a story over the fence. I'm a patient man. It takes a lot to get me riled, and a lot less to get me laughing. Logan sits in a valley so pretty it almost feels unfair. Our Aggies play with that small-town heart, and afterward, everybody goes for ice cream. I always order a double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream, win or lose. When we play well, that's udderly dominant. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Utah State football was established in 1892, which makes it one of the oldest programs in the western United States [S6]. We play in the Pac-12 now [S6]. Home since 1968 has been Merlin Olsen Field at Maverik Stadium in Logan [S6], listed at 25,513 seats [S2]. The field is named for Merlin Olsen, a Pro Football Hall of Famer who played here [S6]. The Aggies have won 13 conference championships across four different leagues, most recently in 2021 [S6], the year we went 11-3 [S2]. Since then: 6-7, 6-7, 4-8 and 6-7 [S2]. Steady folks. We'll get the herd back to the top.

The defense is the steady cow in the barn: 23.5 points allowed (66th) and 140.8 rushing yards allowed (68th) [S5]. It's kept us close. Four of our six games were decided by 12 points or fewer, including a 16-14 loss at Washington and a 17-16 win over Washington State [S2].

4. Players to Know

• RB Javen Jacobs: 393 yards on 70 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5]. He ran for 62 yards and a touchdown against Washington State [S5].

• S Brevin Hamblin: team-high 50 tackles and an interception [S4]. LB Jordan Pendleton: 2.5 sacks [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Utah State is 2-4 and 1-1 in the Pac-12 [S2]. The season: a 29-17 loss to Idaho State, a 16-14 loss at Washington, 33-0 at Utah, a 21-10 win over Troy, a 37-18 loss at Boise State and a 17-16 win over Washington State [S2]. We had last week off [S2]. After San Marcos, Colorado State comes to Logan on Oct. 31 [S5]. I won't do standings math, neighbors. I'll just say a .500 league record keeps the barn lights on.
On the road: we're 0-3 away from home this year [S2], and three of those trips were to Washington, Utah and Boise State. Tough barns.
Season so far: the Washington game still sticks with me. Two points, on the road, against a Big Ten team [S2]. That told me plenty about this team's heart. And the 17-16 win over Washington State? I had ice cream for dinner that night.

6. This Week: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (5:30 p.m. Mountain) · San Marcos, Texas · CBS Sports Network [S1][S5][S8]. CFBD calls the venue Bobcat Stadium; Wikipedia calls it UFCU Stadium [S3][S7].
Last time out: we beat Washington State 17-16 on Oct. 9 [S5]. Texas State beat Colorado State 66-27 on Oct. 15 [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: here's the challenge, neighbors. Texas State leads the entire country in total offense, 562.3 yards a game, and runs for 303.5 a game (3rd) [S5]. They convert 56.1% of third downs (4th) [S5]. Running back Torrance Burgess Jr. has 838 yards [S5], and quarterback Brad Jackson ran for 181 yards and three touchdowns last game [S5]. That's a stampede. Our defense has to tackle.
Our offense vs. their defense: Texas State allows 297.3 passing yards a game, 137th in FBS [S5]. Brosterhous and Eli Wood should have a chance to make plays.
One more: Texas State scores on only 71% of its red zone trips (128th) [S5]. If we bend, we must not break.

What decides it: (1) Tackling the run game. (2) Our passing game against the 137th-ranked pass defense. (3) Holding onto the ball; both teams are below even in turnovers [S5].
To Yesenia Calderwood, Texas State's insider: a river float sounds lovely. Come see Logan sometime, and the ice cream's on me.

Why I Love This Team

I love that this team keeps showing up, even when the scoreboard is rough. I love Eli Wood's hands [S4]. I love that Utah State has been playing football since 1892 [S6]. And I love that after every game, win or lose, Logan goes out for ice cream. Go Aggies!

report.title: "Wave the Flag": Hank Palouse Welcomes the Broncos to the Palouse
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Wave the flag. Howdy, neighbors, I'm Hank Palouse. I drive a combine for a living out in the wheat country, and I haven't missed a game in Pullman since cassette tapes. And yes, I still have the tapes. A whole shoebox of them, labeled by year, in the cab of my pickup. I travel with the Cougars and I live with the Cougars, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little dry Palouse humor and a lot of love for Ol' Crimson, the flag that shows up at every big game in the country. When we win, I wave Ol' Crimson right here in the studio. When we lose, I say "Cougs never quit," and then I tell you a 20-minute story about harvest. You've been warned. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Washington State University is in Pullman, and the first Cougar football team took the field in 1894 [S7]. We play in the Pac-12 [S7]. Home is Martin Stadium, which opened in 1972; the ground there dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field [S7]. CFBD lists the venue as Gesa Field, 32,952 seats [S3]. The last five seasons were 7-6, 7-6, 5-7, 8-5 and 7-6 [S3]. Steady folks out here, like the wheat: some years are a bumper crop, some years you pray for rain, but you always plant again.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Kirby Moore is in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 12, 2025 [S3]. I'll be honest, neighbors, because that's how we do it out here: it's been a hard first year. The defense allows 383.1 yards a game (102nd) and 27.1 points (101st) [S5]. One bright spot: we hold opponents to 37% on third down, 66th in FBS [S5]. And here's the big bright spot. Last week we found a quarterback.

4. Players to Know

• QB Owen Eshelman: the redshirt freshman made his first career start at Oregon State and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns, ran for 136 yards on 15 carries and a touchdown, and led three straight touchdown drives late [S9]. AP says our 30 points were the most we've scored against an FBS team this season [S9]. That's a foot of fresh topsoil on a dry field, neighbors.

Four of those were on the road [S3]. Next up after Boise, we head to San Diego State on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing math on the standings, neighbors. I'm doing math on how loud Pullman gets for a ranked visitor.
That one-point game in Logan still sits with me like hail on a ripe field [S3]. But Cougs never quit.
Why I still love this team: because in the fourth quarter at Corvallis, down big, a redshirt freshman in his first start led three straight touchdown drives [S9]. Nobody quit. Nobody ever does out here. That's a tape I'll be labeling and keeping, right next to the good ones from the old days.

6. This Week: No. 21 Boise State (5-1) at Washington State (1-6)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6 p.m. ET (3 p.m. Pacific) · Martin Stadium / Gesa Field, Pullman · USA Network [S1][S3][S5][S7][S8].

Our offense vs. their defense: Boise State's pass defense allows 261.3 yards a game, 126th [S5]. Eshelman just threw for 289 [S9]. Now that's a crop I'd like to harvest.
